A material document contains information on the type of goods movement, the date and time of posting, the identifier of the user that created the goods movement, the materials transacted, quantities and units of measure, and associated details. The details are recorded in table MATDOC in SAP S/4HANA. Many goods movements reference other SAP S/4HANA documents. For instance, a goods receipt from a supplier can reference a purchasing document and line item. This information is recorded in the material document as well. Each material document line item contains a movement type code. The movement type in the SAP S/4HANA system is represented by a three-character code that identi- fies the type of goods movement to be recorded (goods receipt, goods issue, transfer posting). Movement types play an important control function in determining what data is required to successfully post the goods movement and to pass information into other system components, such as financial accounting. Special stock indicators are used for some movement types depending on the situation. Movement types are paired with a reversal movement type. These reversal movement types are used to undo a movement already posted in the system. It is typical practice to have the reversal movement type be one more than the movement type number. For example, the reversal movement type for a goods receipt for a purchase order (101) is 102. Examples of movement types important for SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement include the following:  101: Goods Receipt for a Purchasing Document  543 O: Goods Issue from Component Stock Provided to Supplier

sections.title: Goods Receipts
sections.en: 7.3.1 Goods Receipts Goods receipts are goods movements that result in an increase in stock. They are important goods movements for SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement as they form an important process link between purchasing and financial accounting. Goods receipts usually reference other SAP S/4HANA documents, such as purchase orders or inbound deliveries. This streamlines the entry of the goods receipt data, much of which can be copied directly from the reference document. However, there are types of goods receipts that can be entered without any reference, such as when initial stocks are entered into the system at startup. Goods receipts can be entered into the SAP S/4HANA system in two ways: a material document can be posted directly in the system using the Post Goods Movement app or, if the supplier of the goods transmits an advance shipping notification (ASN) to you, you can then convert this communication into an inbound delivery document in SAP S/4HANA. Inbound delivery documents can be used when available to plan inbound 7 Inventory Management 246 receipts with much more precision in materials planning. This is due to the shipped quantities and delivery dates being much firmer than at the time of purchase order entry or order acknowledgement. The inbound delivery can be created in the SAP S/4HANA system with reference to one or more purchasing documents. As an alternative, these documents can also be created via the receipt of an advance shipping notification from the supplier of the goods prior to the actual receipt. EDI or SAP Business Network are often utilized by companies to transmit ASNs to an SAP S/4HANA system. Inbound deliveries allow for more precise planning of the inbound movements and provide up-to-date firm supply data to mate- rials planning. The confirmation control key entered on the purchasing document line item controls the method by which a goods receipt is posted. If the confirmation control key allows inbound deliveries, then that document must be referenced to receive the goods. Oth- erwise, the purchase order or scheduling agreement line item can be referenced directly at goods receipt. Here are some examples of goods receipts movement types used in the system:  Movement types for goods receipts with reference to documents – 101: Goods Receipt with reference to Purchase Order or Production Order  Movement types for goods receipts without reference – 561: Initial Stock Entry for Unrestricted Use Stock – 563: Initial Stock Entry for Quality Inspection Stock – 565: Initial Stock Entry for Blocked Stock Goods receipts can be posted using SAP Fiori apps that post goods movements directly into inventory management. Some goods receipts also can be posted using apps that integrate with shipping documents, such as inbound deliveries. Both types of goods receipts are described in the following sections. Posting Goods Receipts There are a variety of SAP Fiori apps for inventory management that can be used to record the arrival of goods at your facility. These apps are described in more detail in the sections ahead. The following SAP Fiori apps are available in SAP S/4HANA for processing goods receipts:  Post Goods Receipt for Purchasing Document  Post Goods Receipt without Reference  Manage Stock  Post Subsequent Adjustment  Material Documents Overview © 247 7.3 Goods Movements In addition, the following SAP GUI for HTML apps are also available for processing goods receipts:  Post Goods Movement  Output Material Documents Post Goods Receipt for Purchasing Document The Post Goods Receipt for Purchasing Document app is used to record the physical receipt of goods into a facility. This app requires the receipt of these goods to be made with reference to an existing purchasing document, such as a purchase order or sched- uling agreement. It is vital that goods receipts reference the correct purchasing docu- ments used to order them for the procure-to-pay business process to work efficiently. The Post Goods Receipt for Purchasing Document app (see Figure 7.3) lets you do the following:  Post the receipt of goods with reference to a purchasing document that contains order items for stock material (procurement for stock).  Post the receipt of goods with reference to a purchasing document that contains order items with single or multiple account assignments (procurement for direct consumption).  Post the receipt of goods into supplier consignment stock.  Receipt of goods received from subcontractors.  Post the receipt of goods into goods receipt blocked stock, which will be released after evaluation.  Post the receipt of shelf life–managed materials into stock.  Post the receipt into stock of items that have been issued from stock transport pur- chase orders.  Assign batches during goods receipt processing for those materials that require them.  Assign serial numbers during goods receipt processing for those materials that require them.  Use predefined output forms in output management for material documents, which can be copied and changed according to your requirements. This app cannot process purchasing document items which fulfill at least one of the fol- lowing conditions:  The Delivery Completed line-item indicator is set.  The line item contains an account assignment category that is not supported by the app.  Receipts for scheduling agreements for stock transport. If all items of a purchasing document fulfill at least one of these conditions, the pur- chasing document is not able to be processed in this app. Use the Post Goods Move- ment app as an alternative. 7 Inventory Management 248 Figure 7.3 Post Goods Receipt for Purchasing Document App The app supports goods receipts for the following account assignment categories:  A: Asset  C: Sales order  F: Order (production)  K: Cost center  M: Individual customer requirements  P: Project  Q: Project make-to-order  R: Service order  S: Third party  X: All auxiliary account assignments The following special stocks are also supported:  E: Sales order stock  K: Consignment stock from vendor  Q: Project stock The Post Goods Receipt for Purchasing Document app is assigned to the inventory manager and warehouse clerk standard authorization roles. Post Goods Receipt without Reference The Post Goods Receipt without Reference app is used to record the physical receipt of goods into a facility for which an existing purchasing document does not exist. © 249 7.3 Goods Movements The Post Goods Receipt without Reference app (see Figure 7.4) lets you do the following:  Post the receipt of goods without reference to an existing purchasing document that contains order items for stock material (procurement for stock). Note that goods receipts for stocks for consumption purposes are not supported in this app.  Post the receipt of shelf life–managed materials into stock.  Assign batches during goods receipt processing for those materials that require them.  Assign serial numbers during goods receipt processing for those materials that require them.  Use predefined output forms in output management for material documents, which can be copied and changed according to your requirements. Figure 7.4 Post Goods Receipt without Reference App The following special stocks are also supported:  E: Sales order stock  K: Consignment stock from supplier  Q: Project stock The Post Goods Receipt without Reference app is assigned to the warehouse clerk stan- dard authorization role. Manage Stock The Manage Stock app (see Figure 7.5) can perform the following types of goods move- ments in the SAP S/4HANA system:  Initial entry of stock balances for unrestricted use, quality inspection or blocked stocks.  Scrapping of material for unrestricted use, quality inspection or blocked stocks. 7 Inventory Management 250 Figure 7.5 Manage Stock App: Selection Screen You will be asked to enter a material and plant. The screen in Figure 7.5 will be shown. Click the up arrow next to the storage location and stock type that you would like to perform transactions on. The Manage Stock processing dialog box (see Figure 7.6) is shown. Enter the transaction (Initial Entry or Scrapping), the quantity of goods to be processed, and cost center if required. Press the Post button. Figure 7.6 Manage Stock App: Processing Dialog Box Note that batch-managed, shelf life–managed, and serial number–managed stocks can also be processed using this app. © 251 7.3 Goods Movements The Manage Stock app supports movement-type-dependent reason codes. Reason codes let you add a short explanation for the underlying purpose of a specific goods movement, such as poor quality. You can also enter free texts for the document header or for an individual line item. The Manage Stock app lets you check the range of cover- age based on the consumption of unrestricted stock in the last 30 days. If you notice that you’ve made an error in posting goods movements, you can correct the error by reversing the material document and posting the goods movements again. To reverse the material document, use the Material Documents Overview app. The Manage Stock app is assigned to the inventory manager standard authorization role. Post Subsequent Adjustment The Post Subsequent Adjustment app (see Figure 7.7) is used to make correction entries in stocks consumed during a subcontracting process. When a goods receipt for a sub- contracted item is posted, goods issues are done for the components sent to the sup- plier, based on the bill of material maintained in the purchasing document line item. Sometimes, suppliers consume more or less of a component than planned. This app allows component corrections, both over- and underconsumptions, to be made after the original goods receipt is posted. This app requires the following:  The referenced purchasing document line item must have a subcontracting item category.  A goods receipt must have already been posted for the selected line item. Figure 7.7 Post Subsequent Adjustment App 7 Inventory Management 252 The Post Subsequent Adjustment app is assigned to the inventory manager and ware- house clerk standard authorization roles. Material Documents Overview The Material Documents Overview app (see Figure 7.8) lets you display generate a list of material document items based on filter criteria and display the details for a selected material document item. You can also reverse a material document through this app. Figure 7.8 Material Documents Overview App This app can be used to do the following:  Display a material document item list based on filter criteria.  Display the details for a specific material document item.  Display a graphical process flow for a material document with the relevant preced- ing and follow-on documents.  Get an overview of material documents, such as goods issue, goods receipt, and material movements with document date, movement type, and document items.  View serial numbers assigned to a material document line item.  Add attachments to a material document.  Export the result list to a spreadsheet.  Reverse a selected material document. The Material Documents Overview app is assigned to the inventory manager and ware- house clerk standard authorization roles. © 253 7.3 Goods Movements Post Goods Movement The Post Goods Movement app (see Figure 7.9) is used to perform goods movements, including goods receipts, in the SAP S/4HANA system. It can also be used to review a specific material document and its associated documents. This app is used when the simplified goods receipt SAP Fiori apps do not support all aspects of the type of goods receipts needed for your enterprise—for example, if custom goods receipt movement types are used. The Post Goods Movement app runs directly on the backend SAP S/4HANA system and is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Transaction MIGO. The Post Goods Movement app is assigned to the inventory manager and warehouse clerk standard authorization roles. Figure 7.9 Post Goods Movement App Output Material Documents The Output Material Documents app (see Figure 7.10) is used to create printouts, goods receipt labels, and other types of messages from the inventory management compo- nent. The Output Material Documents app runs directly on the backend SAP S/4HANA sys- tem and is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Transaction MB90. The Out- put Material Documents app is assigned to the inventory manager and warehouse clerk standard authorization roles. 7 Inventory Management 254 Figure 7.10 Output Material Documents App Processing Goods Receipts via Inbound Deliveries There are a variety of apps that can be used to record the arrival of goods at your facility if your supplier transmits details to you via an advance shipment notification. These apps are described in more detail in the following sections. The Post Goods Receipt for Inbound Delivery app is available in SAP S/4HANA for pro- cessing goods receipts that reference inbound deliveries. In addition, the following SAP GUI for HTML apps are also available:  Inbound Deliveries for Purchase Orders  Create Inbound Delivery  Change Inbound Delivery  Display Inbound Delivery  My Inbound Delivery Monitor Post Goods Receipt for Inbound Delivery The Post Goods Receipt for Inbound Delivery app (see Figure 7.11) enables a user to record goods receipts with reference to an inbound delivery document. The app dis- plays a selection of inbound deliveries from the supplier that can be posted. Note that if an inbound delivery is required for the purchasing document, this app must be used to post the receipt of the goods. This requirement is controlled via the confirmation control key on the purchasing document line item. This app can be used to do the following: © 255 7.3 Goods Movements  Post the receipt of goods with reference to an inbound delivery containing order items for stock material (procurement for stock).  Post the receipt of goods with reference to an inbound delivery containing order items with single or multiple account assignments (procurement for direct con- sumption).  Post the receipt of batch-managed materials into stock.  Post the receipt of serial number–managed materials into stock.  Post the receipt of shelf life–managed materials into stock.  Post the receipt of goods into supplier consignment stock.  Post the receipt of subcontracted goods into stock. The app supports the same account assignment categories and special stocks as the Post Goods Receipt for Purchasing Document app. The Post Goods Receipt for Inbound Delivery app is assigned to the receiving specialist and warehouse clerk standard authorization roles. Figure 7.11 Post Goods Receipt for Inbound Delivery App Inbound Deliveries for Purchase Orders The Inbound Deliveries for Purchase Orders app (see Figure 7.12) is used to list purchase orders that have been approved but do not yet have inbound deliveries created. Users can select the purchase orders for which they wish to create inbound deliveries. A log of the inbound deliveries created is then displayed. 7 Inventory Management 256 Figure 7.12 Inbound Deliveries for Purchase Orders App The Inbound Deliveries for Purchase Orders app runs directly on the backend SAP S/4HANA system and is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Transaction VL34. The Inbound Deliveries for Purchase Orders app is assigned to the receiving specialist standard authorization role. Create Inbound Delivery The Create Inbound Delivery app is used to create an inbound delivery that references an individual purchasing document. The referencing purchase document data is entered (see Figure 7.13), then the system creates the inbound delivery for verification (see Figure 7.14) prior to saving. Figure 7.13 Create Inbound Delivery App: Selection Screen The Create Inbound Delivery app runs directly on the backend SAP S/4HANA system and is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Transaction VL31N. The Create Inbound Delivery app is assigned to the receiving specialist standard authorization role. © 257 7.3 Goods Movements Figure 7.14 Create Inbound Delivery App Change Inbound Delivery The Change Inbound Delivery app (see Figure 7.15) is used to make changes to an exist- ing inbound delivery. The fields that can be changed and the permissible values depend on the status of the document and how far it has progressed in the procure to pay cycle. Figure 7.15 Change Inbound Delivery App 7 Inventory Management 258 The Change Inbound Delivery app runs directly on the backend SAP S/4HANA system and is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Transaction VL32N. The Change Inbound Delivery app is assigned to the receiving specialist standard authorization role. Display Inbound Delivery The Display Inbound Delivery app (see Figure 7.16) is used to show all details for an existing inbound delivery. The Display Inbound Delivery app runs directly on the back- end SAP S/4HANA system and is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Trans- action VL33N. The Display Inbound Delivery app is assigned to the inventory management, receiving specialist, and warehouse clerk standard authorization roles. Figure 7.16 Display Inbound Delivery App My Inbound Delivery Monitor The My Inbound Delivery Monitor app (see Figure 7.17) is used to generate worklists of current inbound deliveries and to take appropriate action for the deliveries selected. Worklists can be created that allow update of putaway quantities for line items and to post goods receipts against inbound delivery documents. General lists of inbound deliveries that meet entered criteria can also be generated. The My Inbound Delivery Monitor app runs directly on the backend SAP S/4HANA sys- tem and is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Transaction VL06I. The My Inbound Delivery Monitor app is assigned to the receiving specialist standard authori- zation role. © 259 7.3 Goods Movements Figure 7.17 My Inbound Delivery Monitor App

sections.title: Goods Issues
sections.en: 7.3.2 Goods Issues Goods issues are classified as goods movements that result in a decrease in stock quan- tities. Goods issues can be planned in the SAP S/4HANA system or can be executed without preplanning. Planned goods issues are issued with reference to an existing document, such as an outbound delivery for a customer order or a reservation for production materials. Those customers requiring shipping integration with their goods issue processes will generally reference outbound delivery documents created by the warehouse. Unplanned goods issues are issued without any reference. Examples include scrapping of defective material or issuing samples from stock. Here are the movement types for goods issues with and without reference documents:  Movement types for goods issues with reference to documents – 261: Goods Issue to Production Order – 601: Goods Issue to Outbound Delivery to Customer – 641: Goods Issue to In-Transit Stock between Plants in Same Company Code – 643: Goods Issue to In-Transit Stock between Plants in Differing Company Codes  Movement types for goods issues without reference – 201: Goods Issue to Cost Center – 333: Goods Issue to Sampling from Unrestricted Use Stock – 551: Goods Issue to Scrap from Unrestricted Use Stock 7 Inventory Management 260 Note Apps used for goods issues without reference include the following:  Manage Stock  Post Goods Movement These apps were described in Section 7.3.1. If you use outbound delivery documents to manage shipping operations, then you can post goods issues in inventory management via these documents. The following apps can be used to manage outbound deliveries in the SAP S/4HANA system:  My Purchase Orders—Due for Delivery  Manage Outbound Deliveries We’ll describe these apps in the following sections. My Purchase Orders—Due for Delivery The My Purchase Orders—Due for Delivery app (see Figure 7.18) is used to create out- bound deliveries for those purchase orders that involve outbound movements of material. These types of purchase orders include returns of material to suppliers or the provisioning of component materials to a subcontractor out of storage location stock. Specific selection criteria are entered, and a list of eligible purchase orders is shown. Outbound deliveries then can be created for the selected orders. Figure 7.18 My Purchase Orders—Due for Delivery App © 261 7.3 Goods Movements The My Purchase Orders—Due for Delivery app runs directly on the backend SAP S/4HANA system and is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Transaction VL10B. The My Purchase Orders—Due for Delivery app is assigned to the shipping spe- cialist standard authorization role. Manage Outbound Deliveries The Manage Outbound Deliveries app (see Figure 7.19) produces a list of outbound deliveries to your specifications. You can click a specific outbound delivery to see details about the document, such as the ship-to customer, weights, or volumes. You can then process the documents, depending on the status of the delivery. For instance, you can post a goods issue for a delivery from this app if it has been completely picked. If you subsequently need to change a delivery document, you can use the app to reverse the goods issue posting and then edit the document. Figure 7.19 Manage Outbound Deliveries App The Manage Outbound Deliveries app is used to do the following:  Search for outbound deliveries using provided filter criteria  Sort your table entries in ascending or descending order  Pick the outbound delivery by transferring to the Pick Outbound Delivery app  Post goods issues for one or more outbound deliveries  Reverse goods issue postings for one or more outbound deliveries The Manage Outbound Deliveries app is assigned to the shipping specialist standard authorization role. 7 Inventory Management 262

sections.title: Stock Transfers
sections.en: 7.3.3 Stock Transfers Stock transfers are goods movements in inventory management that result in a change in physical or logical location for the goods being transacted. Stock transfers can be done within a plant or between two distinct plants. There are three types of stock transfers:  From one storage location to another storage location within a plant  From one plant to another plant within a company code  From one plant to another plant, where the plants are in different company codes Stock transfers can take place using one-step or two-step processes. In one-step stock transfers, the material moves from the issuing plant and storage location to the receiv- ing plant and storage location immediately upon posting. One-step stock transfers are typically used when goods movements are performed in the system after the physical transfer takes place or when the transit time between the two storage locations is min- imal. The following movement types are used for one-step stock transfers:  301: Plant to Plant  311: Storage Location to Storage Location Two-step stock transfers are used to separately record the goods issue from the issuing plant and storage location from the goods receipt into the receiving plant and storage location. This two-step process has the benefit of providing visibility into in-transit stock quantities between the two locations. The following movement types are used for two-step stock transfers:  303: Plant to Plant—Goods Issue from Shipping Plant/Storage Location  305: Plant to Plant—Goods Receipt in Receiving Plant/Storage Location  313: Storage Location to Storage Location—Goods Issue from Shipping Storage Loca- tion  315: Storage Location to Storage location – Goods Receipt in Receiving Storage Loca- tion Note that these movement types can only be used with unrestricted use stock. Simple movements of stock can be recorded in the SAP S/4HANA system with just a material document. The following apps can be used to perform stock transfers using inventory management goods movements:  Transfer Stock—In-Plant  Transfer Stock—Cross-Plant We’ll describe these apps in the following sections. Following their discussion, we’ll dive into the methods by which these are done, via stock transport orders and in-transit stock reporting. © 263 7.3 Goods Movements Transfer Stock—In-Plant The Transfer Stock—In Plant app is used to make transfer postings within a plant. Uti- lize this app to make storage location to storage location stock transfers. You can trans- fer unrestricted, quality inspection or blocked stocks. You can move supplier consignments, sales orders, or project special stocks between storage locations as well. Enter the material to be transferred and the plant. The screen where you can select the issuing storage location/stock type (see Figure 7.20) appears. Click the up arrow icon cor- responding to the storage location and stock type from which the goods are being issued. Figure 7.20 Transfer Stock In-Plant App: Select Issuing Storage Location/Stock Type The screen where you can select the receiving storage location/stock type (see Figure 7.21) appears. Click the down arrow icon corresponding to the storage location and stock type into which the goods are being received. Figure 7.21 Transfer Stock In-Plant App: Select Receiving Storage Location/Stock Type The Transfer Stock In-Plant processing dialog box (see Figure 7.22) appears. Enter the quantity of goods being moved, then click the Post button. A material document is cre- ated, documenting the stock transfer in the system. 7 Inventory Management 264 Figure 7.22 Transfer Stock In-Plant App: Processing Dialog Box This app also lets you transfer from one stock type to another. In addition, it allows transfers of ownership from supplier consignment stock to unrestricted use stock. You can also transfer quantities between two sales order stocks or two project stocks, and you can enter free texts for the document header or for an individual line item. You can also check the range of coverage for the existing stocks based on the consumption of unrestricted use stock materials in the last 30 days. You can branch from this app to other apps, such as Stock—Single Material and Mate- rial Documents Overview. The Transfer Stock—In-Plant app is assigned to the inventory manager and warehouse clerk standard authorization roles. Transfer Stock—Cross-Plant Use the Transfer Stock—Cross-Plant app to create transfer postings from one plant to another. You can also transfer stock from one stock type to another using this app. It is similar in look and feel to the Transfer Stock—In-Plant app discussed in the previous section. © 265 7.3 Goods Movements Enter the material to be transferred. The screen where you can select issuing plant/ stock type (see Figure 7.23) appears. Then click the up arrow icon corresponding to the plant and stock type from which the goods are being issued. Figure 7.23 Transfer Stock—Cross-Plant App: Select Issuing Plant/Stock Type The screen where you can select receiving plant/stock type (see Figure 7.24) appears. Click the down arrow icon corresponding to the plant and stock type into which the goods are being received. Figure 7.24 Transfer Stock—Cross-Plant App: Select Receiving Plant/Stock Type The Transfer Stock Cross-Plant processing dialog box (see Figure 7.25) appears. Enter the issuing storage location, receiving storage location, and quantity of goods being 7 Inventory Management 266 moved, then click the Post button. A material document is created, documenting the stock transfer in the system. Figure 7.25 Transfer Stock Cross-Plant App: Processing Dialog Box You can create a stock transport order directly from this app via the Create Stock Trans- port Order button. Note that stock transport order configuration needs to be set in the backend system to support this feature. This simple approach frees you from having to remember obscure movement types to transact these changes. You can record free texts for the document header or for an individual line item, and you can use a predictive analytics model to forecast the delivery date for a stock trans- port order from this app as well. You can branch from this app to other apps, such as Manage Stock, Transfer Stock—In- Plant, and Material Documents Overview. The Transfer Stock—Cross-Plant app is assigned to the inventory manager and ware- house clerk standard authorization roles. © 267 7.3 Goods Movements Stock Transport While using inventory management goods movement to process material transfers is a simple method, most companies require more precise tracking of goods movements in materials planning, purchasing, and the warehouse. SAP offers the use of stock trans- port orders (STOs) to facilitate these detailed requirements. A stock transport order is a kind of purchase order. A stock transport order uses a sup- plying plant code in lieu of a supplier in the header of the purchase order. You can think of a stock transport order as a purchase from an internal supplier to your company group instead of an external supplier. There are two kinds of stock transport orders:  Intracompany stock transport orders The supplying and receiving plants belong to the same company code.  Intercompany stock transport order The supplying and receiving plants belong to different company codes. Stock transport orders have the following advantages over inventory management stock transfer movements:  The goods receipt can be planned in the receiving plant.  A separate freight supplier can be entered in the order and freight bills matched to these freight suppliers.  Delivery costs can be captured and billed.  Materials planning can see the planned supply in the receiving plant, and the demand in the issuing plant once the stock transport order is created.  Outbound deliveries are used to manage the outbound process in the warehouse, similar to the process used to deliver goods to the customer. There are three process variations, which we’ll discuss in the following sections, for the stock transfer process using stock transport orders:  Stock transport order without delivery  Stock transport order with delivery using shipping  Stock transport order with delivery and billing document The process variation used depends on your business requirements for tracing the logistics flow from planning, shipping, in-transit stock, and receiving the goods. Stock Transport Order without Delivery The stock transport order without delivery process variant uses only stock transport purchase orders to manage the process. No logistics documents are utilized. The pur- chase order type in the standard system is UB, and the item category on each line item is U. The goods movements are valuated at the price of the material in the issuing plant. 7 Inventory Management 268 The Post Goods Movement app can be used to post goods movements with reference to the stock transport order. The movement types are 351 for the goods issue in the issuing plant and 101 for the goods receipt in the receiving plant. Note that the stock transport order without delivery process can only be done with a two-step process. All goods movements are recorded in the purchase order history of the stock transport order. Both the intracompany and intercompany variants are supported. The prerequisites for the stock transport order without delivery process variant are as follows:  Material masters for the goods being transferred are set up in both plants  A ship-to customer master is set up that represents the receiving plant The steps in the stock transport order without delivery process flow are as follows: 1. Stock transport requisition is created manually or via materials planning (optional) 2. Stock transport order is created manually, or by converting stock transport requisi- tions 3. A goods issue with reference to the stock transport order is done in the issuing plant, which decrements the material and moves it into in-transit stock into the issuing plant 4. In-transit stock is monitored 5. A goods receipt with reference to the stock transport order is done in the receiving plant Stock Transport Order with Delivery via Shipping The stock transport order with delivery via shipping process variant uses outbound deliveries in addition to stock transport purchase orders to manage the process. The pur- chase order type in the standard system is UB, and the item category on each line item is U. The goods movements are valuated at the price of the material in the issuing plant. This process variant supports both one-step and two-step movements of material. Stock transport orders with deliveries is the most common process used to execute intracompany stock transport orders as it has integration with the logistics depart- ment and does not require billing documents to be exchanged between the plants. Outbound deliveries are used to manage the outbound process in the warehouse, sim- ilar to the process used in sales to deliver goods to customers. All goods movements are posted with reference to the outbound delivery created with reference to the stock transport order. The movement type for the goods issue in the issuing plant is 647 for the one-step process and movement type 641 for the two-step process. The movement type for the goods receipt in the receiving plant is 101 for the two-step process. Note that no goods receipt is necessary in the one-step process as the goods move into the unrestricted stock of the receiving plant immediately upon goods issue from the issuing plant. © 269 7.3 Goods Movements All goods movements are recorded in the purchase order history of the stock transport order. Both the intracompany and intercompany variants are supported. The prerequisites for the stock transport order with delivery process variant are as fol- lows:  Material masters for the goods being transferred are set up in both plants  A supplier master is set up that represents the issuing plant  A ship-to customer master is set up that represents the receiving plant The steps in the stock transport order with delivery (one step) process flow are as follows: 1. Stock transport requisition is created manually or via materials planning (optional). 2. Stock transport order is created manually, or by converting stock transport requisi- tions. 3. A replenishment outbound delivery (document type NL) is created with reference to the stock transport order to manage the shipping activities. 4. The goods are picked from the warehouse and staged for delivery. 5. A goods issue with reference to the replenishment outbound delivery is done in the issuing plant, which decrements the material. 6. A goods receipt in the receiving plant is automatically done upon successful posting of the goods issue. The steps in the stock transport order with delivery (two-step) process flow are as fol- lows: 1. Stock transport requisition is created manually or via materials planning (optional). 2. Stock transport purchase order is created manually or by converting stock transport requisitions into STOs. 3. A replenishment outbound delivery (document type NL) is created with reference to the stock transport order to manage the shipping activities. 4. The goods are picked from the warehouse and staged for delivery. 5. A goods issue with reference to the replenishment outbound delivery is done in the issuing plant, which decrements the material stocks and moves them into in-transit stock into the issuing plant. 6. In-transit stock is monitored. 7. A goods receipt with reference to the replenishment outbound delivery is done in the receiving plant upon receipt of the goods. Stock Transport Order with Delivery and Billing Document The stock transport order with delivery and billing document process variant uses out- bound deliveries in addition to stock transport orders to manage the process. The pur- chase order type in the standard system is NB, and the item category on each line item 7 Inventory Management 270 is blank. While this is similar to a purchase order to an external supplier, the supplier on an intercompany STO must be linked to the issuing plant code in the business partner master data. The goods movements are valuated at the price of the material in the issuing plant which is maintained in purchasing pricing condition records. This process variant sup- ports both one-step and two-step movements of material. This is the most common scenario to process intercompany stock transport orders as they require integration with the logistics department and require billing documents to be exchanged between the two companies. Outbound deliveries are used to manage the outbound process in the warehouse, sim- ilar to the process used by sales to deliver goods to customers. All goods movements are posted with reference to the outbound delivery created from the stock transport order. The movement type for the goods issue in the issuing plant is 641. The movement type for the goods receipt in the receiving plant is 101. All goods movements are recorded in the purchase order history of the stock transport order. The prerequisites for the stock transport order with delivery and billing document pro- cess variant are as follows:  Material masters are set up in both plants  Supplier master is set up that represents the issuing plant  Ship-to customer master is set up that represents the receiving plant  Purchasing pricing condition records exist for pricing the material in the stock transport order  Billing condition records exist for pricing the material in the intercompany billing document The steps in the stock transport order with delivery two-step process flow are as fol- lows: 1. A stock transport requisition is created manually or via materials planning (optional). 2. A stock transport order is created manually, or by converting stock transport requi- sitions. 3. A replenishment outbound delivery (document type NLCC) is created with reference to the stock transport order to manage the outbound shipping activities. 4. The goods are picked from the warehouse and staged for delivery. 5. A goods issue with reference to the replenishment outbound delivery is done in the issuing plant, which decrements the material stocks and transfers them into cross- company in-transit stock into the receiving plant. 6. A billing document for the shipped goods is produced and presented to the receiv- ing company code. © 271 7.3 Goods Movements 7. Cross company in-transit stock is monitored. 8. A goods receipt with reference to the replenishment outbound delivery is done in the receiving plant upon receipt of the goods. 9. A vendor invoice is created with reference to the billing document in the receiving company code. In-Transit Stock Reporting It’s important to monitor the status of in-transit stocks in the system, especially those that involve a two-step process. This will ensure that all physical stock transfers are posted in a timely manner and that up-to-date stock information is available for mate- rials planning. SAP S/4HANA provides the following apps to obtain reports for in-process stock trans- fers:  Display Stock in Transit  Stock in Transit on Key Date  Overdue Materials—Stock in Transit We’ll describe these apps in the following sections. Display Stock in Transit The Display Stock in Transit app (see Figure 7.26) is used to show all stocks that have been issued from one plant and are currently in transit to another plant. It also shows stock transport purchase order references and the value of the goods transferred. Figure 7.26 Display Stock in Transit App 7 Inventory Management 272 The Display Stock in Transit app runs directly on the backend SAP S/4HANA system and is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Transaction MB5T. The Display Stock in Transit app is assigned to the inventory manager standard authorization role. Stock in Transit on Key Date The Stock in Transit on Key Date app (see Figure 7.27) is used to show all stocks that have been issued from one plant and are currently in transit to another plant on a spec- ified key date. It also shows stock transport order references and the value of the goods in transit. Figure 7.27 Stock in Transit on Key Date App The Stock in Transit on Key Date app runs directly on the backend SAP S/4HANA sys- tem and is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Transaction MB5TD. The Stock in Transit on Key Date app is assigned to the inventory manager standard authoriza- tion role. Overdue Materials—Stock in Transit The Overdue Materials—Stock in Transit app (see Figure 7.28) provides information on materials for which a stock transport order has been created and issued, but which have not been received to date. You can identify these materials to complete the stock trans- fer process or to investigate potential issues with the transfers. Use the Overdue Materials—Stock in Transit app to do the following:  Review the stock transport orders for which materials are scheduled to arrive in a plant.  Display a list of stock transport order line items for which the stock transfer process hasn’t yet been completed, has been completed, or both.  Follow up on the results by choosing a purchase order or a material from the list, and then choosing one of the following apps: Post Goods Receipt for Purchasing Docu- ment, Stock—Single Material, or Stock—Multiple Materials.  See the stock value of overdue stocks in transit; stock value calculation is based on stock quantity of the selected reporting date multiplied by the current material price.  Use a predictive analytics model to forecast the delivery date for a stock transport order. © 273 7.3 Goods Movements The Overdue Materials—Stock in Transit app is assigned to the shipping specialist, receiving specialist, and warehouse clerk standard authorization roles. Figure 7.28 Overdue Materials—Stock in Transit App

sections.title: Transfer Postings
sections.en: 7.3.4 Transfer Postings Transfer postings are goods movements that result in a change in identity, usability, or ownership for a quantity of stock. Typically, the stock doesn’t physically move in the system during a transfer posting. However, it is possible to combine some types of transfer postings with changes in location as well. The Transfer Stock—In-Plant app is used to post transfer postings in the SAP S/4HANA system. The Post Goods Movements app also can be utilized to create transfer posting goods movements. Descriptions of these apps can be found in Section 7.3.3. Let’s take a closer look at the types of transfer postings, as follows:  Stock identity Transfer postings that result in a change in stock identity involve a change in mate- rial. Note that a material can only to transferred to the stock of another material if both materials share the same base unit of measure. If a material is batch-managed in the SAP S/4HANA system, a change in batch identity can also be posted. Both the material and batch can be changed at the same time. The 309 movement type is 7 Inventory Management 274 used to change material or batch quantities in stock. Use the Post Goods Movements app to post changes in material or changes in batches.  Stock usability Transfer postings that result in a change in stock usability involve a change in the stock type. In general, most stock types can be transferred interchangeably. How- ever, if quality management is active for a material in a plant, then transfers into or out of quality inspection stock must be done in conjunction with a quality manage- ment process, such as inbound inspection. Movement types used to transfer stock from one stock type to another are shown in Table 7.1. Use the Transfer Stock—In- Plant app for transfer postings from one stock type to another within a plant.  Stock ownership If you have stocks delivered to your facility by a supplier on a consignment basis and you wish to take financial ownership of these stocks prior to consumption, you enter a transfer posting to recognize that fact. Similarly, if you accept returns of stock delivered on a consignment basis to your customer, you post a transfer post- ing as well. Movement type 411 K is provided for this purpose. Use the Transfer Stock—In-Plant app to post stock ownership changes within a plant.

sections.title: Physical Inventory
sections.en: 7.4 Physical Inventory Good accounting practices require periodic reconciliation of the stock balances found in the SAP S/4HANA system to the physical stocks in the warehouse. These assets need to be reflected accurately in the company’s financial statements. Accurate stock bal- From Stock Type To Stock Type Movement Type Quality inspection Unrestricted use 321 Unrestricted use Quality inspection 322 Blocked Unrestricted use 343 Unrestricted use Blocked 344 Blocked Quality inspection 349 Quality inspection Blocked 350 Customer returns Unrestricted use 453 Customer returns Quality inspection 457 Customer returns Blocked 459 Table 7.1 Stock Transfer Movement Types for Usability Changes © 275 7.4 Physical Inventory ances also optimize the benefits of MRP for assuring availability of material for produc- tion and sales processes. The system provides a variety of physical inventory methods to accomplish this requirement. Regardless of the method used, all physical inventory processes encom- pass the following three phases (see Figure 7.29): 1. Creation of the physical inventory documents 2. Entry of the physical counts into SAP S/4HANA 3. Posting of physical inventory differences Figure 7.29 Physical Inventory Process Phases A physical inventory document is required to start the process. This document forms the basis for planning and performing a physical inventory, for recording counts, and for posting any differences found between the system and the physical stocks. Physical inventory documents contain a header, which holds information about the count event itself, such as the document number, the person responsible for the count, and the planned count date. Line items on the physical inventory document contain the materials being counted and hold the system and actual count information. Stocks are counted in inventory management based on the following:  Material  Plant  Storage location  Stock type  Valuation type/batch  Special stock Each combination of these elements will be counted separately during a physical inventory. Print physical inventory lists Enter count Post differences Create physical inventory documents 1 Stock count 2 Analyze differences 3 7 Inventory Management 276 The method of creating physical inventory documents is dependent on the technique used for the count. SAP S/4HANA supports the following techniques:  Manual physical inventory (spot inventory)  Annual physical inventory  Continuous physical inventory  Cycle counting  Sample-based physical inventory For additional information on these physical inventory methods, consult the SAP Help website. Once the documents are created, it is common to print the physical inventory count sheets. These are then distributed to the counters, who record the physical quantities on the sheet. Count sheets can be transferred to a mobile application for counting as well. After the physical count is recorded, this information is entered into the SAP S/4HANA system. The system can provide feedback to the entry clerk if the quantity recorded during the count exceeds the system count based on a defined threshold percentage. This helps prevent data entry errors. Once the counts are entered, they can be analyzed by authorized personnel. This anal- ysis may result in a recount of the material in that storage location. Once the physical inventory counts are confirmed, any differences detected need to be posted to inven- tory management so that the physical and system counts are reconciled. This action results in a goods movement posting either incrementing or decrementing the quan- tity of goods in stock. Financial postings are also made at the same time. SAP S/4HANA supplies apps to use in managing the physical inventory processes sup- ported by the system. There are apps to support the execution of a physical inventory and others for monitoring the physical inventory processes and reporting. SAP sup- plies the following SAP Fiori apps to support physical inventory processes:  Create Physical Inventory Documents  Schedule Physical Inventory Document Creation  Manage Physical Inventory Count  Manage Physical Inventory Documents  Cycle Counting—Classification These apps are described in more detail in the following sections. The system also con- tains legacy apps for managing the physical inventory process, which will be described as well. © 277 7.4 Physical Inventory

sections.title: Create Physical Inventory Documents
sections.en: 7.4.1 Create Physical Inventory Documents You use the Create Physical Inventory Documents app (see Figure 7.30) to create phys- ical inventory documents for selected materials. You use this app when you want to perform a physical inventory for a specified set of materials of your choosing. Select the materials that you want using the filter criteria supplied. You can click a material line to obtain current stock balances, key figures, and material master infor- mation. You can then create one or more physical inventory documents based on grouping information you supply to the app. Figure 7.30 Create Physical Inventory Documents App The Create Physical Inventory Documents app is assigned to the inventory manager and warehouse clerk standard authorization roles.

sections.title: Schedule Physical Inventory Document Creation
sections.en: 7.4.2 Schedule Physical Inventory Document Creation You use the Schedule Physical Inventory Document Creation app (see Figure 7.31) to create and schedule a batch job that will create physical inventory documents for you periodically, which saves time and effort. SAP supplies two predefined job templates for annual inventory and cycle counting. These templates can be copied and changed according to your requirements. The app 7 Inventory Management 278 allows you to define the start date and time for the job, and recurrence pattern, along with other control elements. Figure 7.31 Schedule Physical Inventory Document Creation App The Schedule Physical Inventory Document Creation app is assigned to the inventory manager standard authorization role.

sections.title: Manage Physical Inventory Count
sections.en: 7.4.3 Manage Physical Inventory Count You use the Manage Physical Inventory Count app (see Figure 7.32) to search for and enter physical inventory counts into the system. Filters allow you to quickly locate the physical inventory documents requiring entry. Materials on the document are grouped into uncounted and counted categories. You can update a previously entered count for a material if the PI document status permits this. Ad hoc (unplanned) physical inventory counts are also supported in this app. The app allows a user to create a physical inventory document and enter count results all in one step. Physical inventory counts of serialized items are supported. The Manage Physical Inventory Count app is assigned to the inventory manager and warehouse clerk standard authorization roles. © 279 7.4 Physical Inventory Figure 7.32 Manage Physical Inventory Count App

sections.title: Manage Physical Inventory Documents
sections.en: 7.4.4 Manage Physical Inventory Documents You use the Manage Physical Inventory Documents app (see Figure 7.33) to list and dis- play information about physical inventory documents in the system. Figure 7.33 Manage Physical Inventory Documents App 7 Inventory Management 280 Select the physical inventory documents that you want using the filter criteria sup- plied, such as planned count date and storage location. From the resulting list, you can display more detailed information on the header of an individual document, and drill into the individual materials to be counted and their status. You can also initiate a recount for one or more items, or post count results directly. The Manage Physical Inventory Documents app is assigned to the inventory manager and warehouse clerk standard authorization roles.

sections.title: Cycle Counting—Classification
sections.en: 7.4.5 Cycle Counting—Classification You use the Cycle Counting—Classification app (see Figure 7.34) to manage cycle count indicator maintenance for the materials subject to this type of physical inventory. You can assign cycle count indicators for those materials that need them, change them, and delete them from materials that will not be cycle counted in the future. You can also have the app automatically propose new cycle count indicators based on historical consumption or forecasted usage. The app then updates the material masters with the updated information. Figure 7.34 Cycle Count—Classification App The Cycle Count—Classification app is assigned to the inventory manager standard authorization role. © 281 7.4 Physical Inventory

sections.title: SAP GUI for HTML Apps
sections.en: 7.4.6 SAP GUI for HTML Apps In addition to the SAP Fiori apps described so far, a number of SAP GUI for HTML apps that correspond to legacy SAP ERP transactions are available for execution of physical inven- tory processes. This allows you to migrate to SAP Fiori and continue to use the same inventory processes you have used in the past. These apps are described in Table 7.2. App Name App ID Description Standard Roles Create Single PI Document MI01 Use this app to manually create a physical inventory document. You use this app when you want to per- form a physical inventory for a spe- cific set of materials of your choosing. Inventory manager, warehouse clerk Change Physical Inventory Document MI02 Use this app when you want to add or change materials that need to be counted. Inventory manager, warehouse clerk Enter Inventory Count MI04 Use this app to enter count results that have been recorded by the inventory counter on the physical inventory count sheet in the system. Inventory manager, warehouse clerk Change Physical Inventory Count MI05 Use this app to modify an entered count for a physical inventory docu- ment prior to clearing. Inventory manager, warehouse clerk Enter PI Count w/o Document MI09 Use this app to enter physical inven- tory counts for materials without first creating a physical inventory document. This app combines the creation and entry of count steps into one transaction. Differences must be cleared in a subsequent step to com- plete the physical inventory process. Inventory manager, warehouse clerk Enter and Post PI Count w/o Document MI10 Use this app to enter physical inven- tory counts and post differences for materials without first creating a physical inventory document. This app combines creation, entering, and clearing of differences steps into one transaction. Inventory manager Table 7.2 SAP GUI for HTML Apps for Legacy Physical Inventory Transactions 7 Inventory Management 282 Request Physical Inventory Recount MI11 Use this app to recount items from a counted physical inventory docu- ment. This creates a new physical inventory document that references the items selected for recount from the original document. Inventory manager Process Physical Inventory Count Results MI20 Use this app to create a list of physical inventory differences in the system based on entered selection criteria. A list of physical inventory items that meet the criteria is displayed. You can clear the differences directly from this list, or you can enter or change count results. Inventory manager Print Physical Inventory Documents MI21 Use this app to print activated, uncounted physical inventory docu- ments that can be distributed to the persons performing the count. Inventory manager, warehouse clerk Create Physical Inventory Documents—Regular Stock MI31 Use this app to create several physi- cal inventory documents at one time based on entered selection criteria. The physical inventory documents are then created in a batch run and are available for counting. Note that this app creates docu- ments for normal storage location stocks only; there are other apps for creating physical inventory counts for special stocks. Inventory manager, warehouse clerk ABC Analysis for Cycle Counting MIBC Use this app to set cycle count indica- tors on the material master for those materials subject to the cycle count- ing method of physical inventory. The cycle count indicator determines the frequency per year with which a material needs to be counted per the settings in configuration. The system analyzes consumption or forecast data for that material and plant in the system and sets the cycle count indicator accordingly. Inventory manager App Name App ID Description Standard Roles Table 7.2 SAP GUI for HTML Apps for Legacy Physical Inventory Transactions (Cont.) © 283

sections.title: Reporting in Inventory Management
sections.en: 7.5 Reporting in Inventory Management 7.5 Reporting in Inventory Management Proper control of physical stocks requires a robust set of reporting capabilities. S/4HANA builds on SAP ERP’s inventory management reporting strengths by adding new capabili- ties to visualize the current stock situation, thus enabling fast action in the case of logis- tics bottlenecks. These capabilities include inventory analytics, which show key perfor- mance indicators in real time, and the inventory overview pages, new in SAP S/4HANA, which show multiple key analytics on a single screen. There are a number of inventory management reporting apps that come delivered with the SAP S/4HANA system. These apps can be broadly grouped into six types:  Inventory overview pages  Goods movements reporting apps  Stock balances reporting apps  Monitoring financial inventory values apps  Inventory management object pages  Inventory analytics We’ll discuss each type in the sections that follow.

sections.title: Inventory Overview Pages
sections.en: 7.5.1 Inventory Overview Pages Inventory overview pages allow inventory managers, analysts, and warehouse person- nel to see all relevant metrics for their operations on one page. These metrics are arranged as actionable cards that can be rearranged or hidden. Filters can be applied to the overview pages, which instantly reflect on the displayed metrics. This allows the user to focus on important items, enabling decision-making and follow-on actions in a timely manner. For list cards, selecting the header of a card brings you to the app itself; selecting an item shows more detailed item information. For graphical or analytical cards, selecting the card displays detailed analytical information. Display Physical Inventory Progress MIDO Use this app to get an overview of the progress of physical inventories in your facility. Inventory manager Display PI Document Line Items for Materials MI22 Use this app to determine the physi- cal inventory documents used to count specific materials over time. Inventory manager App Name App ID Description Standard Roles Table 7.2 SAP GUI for HTML Apps for Legacy Physical Inventory Transactions (Cont.) 7 Inventory Management 284 There are three overview page apps delivered with the SAP S/4HANA system for use by inventory control personnel:  Overview Inventory Processing  Overview Inventory Management  Inventory Analysis Overview We’ll discuss these apps in the following sections. Overview Inventory Processing The Overview Inventory Processing app (see Figure 7.35) shows the most important information and tasks relevant for a warehousing clerk. The information is displayed on a set of actionable cards. You can therefore focus on the most important tasks, enabling faster decisions and immediate action. Figure 7.35 Overview Inventory Processing App The following cards are available in the Overview Inventory Processing app:  Recent Inventory Counts  Warehouse Throughput History  Recent Material Documents  Monitor Purchase Order Items  Overdue Materials—GR Blocked Stock  Outbound Delivery List  Inbound Delivery List © 285 7.5 Reporting in Inventory Management Additional details on the capabilities of these cards can be found in the app documen- tation on the SAP Help website. The Overview Inventory Processing app is assigned to the warehouse clerk standard authorization role. Overview Inventory Management The Overview Inventory Management app (see Figure 7.36) is used by inventory man- agers to show the most important information and tasks relevant at the current time. The information is displayed on a set of actionable cards. You can therefore focus on the most important tasks, enabling faster decisions and immediate action. Figure 7.36 Overview Inventory Management App The following cards are available in the Overview Inventory Management app:  Recent Material Documents  Overdue Material—GR Blocked Stock  Stock Value by Stock Type  Stock Value by Special Stock Type  Warehouse Throughput History  Monitor Purchase Order Items  Overdue Materials—Stock in Transit 7 Inventory Management 286 Additional details on the capabilities of these cards can be found in the app documen- tation on the SAP Help website. The Overview Inventory Management app is assigned to the inventory manager standard authorization role. Inventory Analysis Overview The Inventory Analysis Overview app is used by inventory analysts to show the most important information and tasks relevant at the current time. The information is dis- played on a set of actionable cards. You can therefore focus on the most important tasks, enabling faster decisions and immediate action. The following cards are available in the Inventory Analysis Overview app:  Stock Value Increase despite Consumption  More than 100 Days without Consumption  Monitor Batches by Longest Time in Storage  Monitor Batches by Earliest Expiration Date Additional details on the capabilities of these cards can be found in the app documen- tation on the SAP Help website. The Inventory Analysis Overview app is assigned to the inventory analyst standard authorization role.

sections.title: Goods Movement Reporting Apps
sections.en: 7.5.2 Goods Movement Reporting Apps It’s often useful to determine how the stock balances in the system were derived. This is especially true when trying to reconcile physical inventory counts with book inven- tories. Goods movement reports in SAP S/4HANA allow you to list goods movements that meet user-entered selection criteria for analysis and action. SAP S/4HANA features two apps to report on goods movements recorded in the sys- tem:  Material Documents Overview The Material Documents Overview app was described in detail in Section 7.3.1.  Display Material Document List The Display Material Document List app (see Figure 7.37) is used to display material documents that meet entered selection criteria. The Display Material Document List app runs directly on the backend SAP S/4HANA system and is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Transaction MB51. The Dis- play Material Document List app is assigned to the inventory manager and warehouse clerk standard authorization roles. © 287 7.5 Reporting in Inventory Management Figure 7.37 Display Material Document List App

sections.title: Stock Balances Reporting Apps
sections.en: 7.5.3 Stock Balances Reporting Apps There are several SAP Fiori apps supplied for stock balances reporting and to monitor the current quantities of stocks in the SAP S/4HANA system. These include the fol- lowing:  Stock—Single Material  Stock—Multiple Materials  Manage Batches In addition, several SAP GUI for HTML transactions are also supplied by SAP for stock monitoring:  Batch Information Cockpit  Display Stock Overview  Display Warehouse Stock We’ll discuss these apps in the following sections. Stock—Single Material The Stock—Single Material app (see Figure 7.38) provides an overview of all stocks for one material. You can review your stock by specific plants and storage locations for 7 Inventory Management 288 which you are responsible. The app can display the stock information as a table or a dia- gram. The Stock—Single Material app has the following capabilities:  Display a stock overview for a single material by plant and storage location as a table or a bar graph.  Display the stock history of the material for the last 12 periods as a curve diagram (see Figure 7.39).  Drill down into the stock history (day-end closing) or to the material documents for each day.  Compare the stock information with the safety stock and minimum safety stock val- ues defined for that material.  Transfer to other apps, such as the following: – Manage Stock – Transfer Stock—In-Plant – Transfer Stock—Cross-Plant – Material Documents Overview – Stock—Multiple Materials The Stock—Single Material app is assigned to the shipping specialist, receiving special- ist, and inventory manager standard authorization roles. Figure 7.38 Stock—Single Material App © 289 7.5 Reporting in Inventory Management Figure 7.39 Stock History in Plant Stock—Multiple Materials The Stock—Multiple Materials app (see Figure 7.40) provides an overview of stocks for one or more materials. You can review your stock by specific plants and storage loca- tions for which you are responsible. The app can display the stock information as a table or a diagram. Figure 7.40 Stock—Multiple Materials App The Stock—Multiple Materials app has the following capabilities:  Display a stock overview of one or more materials.  Display the value of your stock; stock value calculation is based on stock quantity of the selected reporting date multiplied by the current material price.  Export the results to a spreadsheet. 7 Inventory Management 290 The Stock—Multiple Materials app is assigned to the shipping specialist, receiving spe- cialist, and inventory manager standard authorization roles. Manage Batches The Manage Batches app (see Figure 7.41) lets you create, edit, and display batches in your SAP S/4HANA system. This app gives you quick and easy access to batch-relevant information. New or changed batch records can be stored as draft versions. This allows others to locate and review these draft versions using the search or filter options to complete their work. The Manage Batches app allows you to do the following:  Search for existing batches or ranges of batches.  Edit existing batch masters.  Create new batch masters.  Obtain information about other business documents related to the batch, such as inspection lots or deliveries.  Save new or changed batches as drafts for others to work on.  Transfer to the Stock—Single Material or Transfer Stock—In-Plant apps. The Manage Batches app is assigned to the inventory manager and warehouse clerk standard authorization roles. Figure 7.41 Manage Batches App © 291 7.5 Reporting in Inventory Management Batch Information Cockpit You can use the Batch Information Cockpit app (see Figure 7.42) for further analysis and control options, such as calling up the batch master for changing and displaying mas- ter data, classification data, and the batch where-used list, containing information about the lifecycle of a batch. The Batch Information Cockpit app runs directly on the backend SAP S/4HANA system and is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Transaction BMBC. The Batch Information Cockpit app is assigned to the quality technician standard authorization role. Figure 7.42 Batch Information Cockpit App Display Stock Overview The Display Stock Overview app (see Figure 7.43) is used to display current stock bal- ances for a single material in all plants, storage locations, and special stock types across the enterprise. The Display Stock Overview app runs directly on the backend SAP S/4HANA system and is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Transaction MMBE. The Display Stock Overview app is assigned to the inventory manager and warehouse clerk stan- dard authorization roles. 7 Inventory Management 292 Figure 7.43 Display Stock Overview App Display Warehouse Stock The Display Warehouse Stock app (see Figure 7.44) is used to display current stock bal- ances for one or more materials in selected plants and storage locations. The Display Warehouse Stock app runs directly on the backend SAP S/4HANA system and is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Transaction MB52. The Display Warehouse Stock app is assigned to the inventory manager standard authorization role. Figure 7.44 Display Warehouse Stock App © 293 7.5 Reporting in Inventory Management

sections.title: Monitoring Financial Inventory Values Apps
sections.en: 7.5.4 Monitoring Financial Inventory Values Apps The monetary value tied up in physical stocks in your facility is a key metric by which inventory managers are measured. Therefore, SAP S/4HANA provides several standard reports to help monitor financial inventory values and to manage and control inven- tory values. In addition, the following apps can be used to monitor the financial inventory values in the system:  Material Inventory Values—Balance Summary  Material Inventory Values—Line Items We’ll discuss these apps in the following sections. Material Inventory Values—Balance Summary Use the Material Inventory Values—Balance Summary app (see Figure 7.45) to under- stand the quantities and values of your material inventories on a specific date, which can be current or in the past. Figure 7.45 Material Inventory Values—Balance Summary App The Material Inventory Values—Balance Summary app allows you to do the following:  View inventory values and quantities sorted by company code, general ledger account, material group, material, business transaction type, posting date, and doc- ument number.  Analyze line items in detail with a wide number of attributes (plant, material) and key figures (inventory quantity, inventory amount in up to three currencies. 7 Inventory Management 294  Filter and analyze inventories using dimensions such as general ledger account, material, profit center, and fiscal year.  Show the analysis of the line items using graphics, tables, or a combination of both. The Material Inventory Values—Balance Summary app is assigned to the inventory manager standard authorization role. Material Inventory Values—Line Items The Material Inventory Values—Line Items app (see Figure 7.46) is used to understand quantities and values of your material inventories at the line item level. Figure 7.46 Material Inventory Values—Line Items App This app displays the following information about material inventory values:  The inventory value and quantity of the journal entries that affect the value of mate- rial inventories during a particular period  The date of the source document, the proposed posting date, and the actual posting date The Material Inventory Values—Line Items app allows you to do the following:  View inventory values and quantities sorted by company code, general ledger account, material group, material, business transaction type, posting date, and doc- ument number.  Analyze line items in detail with a wide number of attributes (plant, material) and key figures (inventory quantity, inventory amount in up to three currencies). © 295 7.5 Reporting in Inventory Management  Filter and analyze inventories using dimensions such as general ledger account, material, profit center, and fiscal year.  Show the analysis of line items using graphics, tables, or a combination of both. The Material Inventory Values—Line Items app is assigned to the inventory manager standard authorization role.

sections.title: Inventory Management Object Pages
sections.en: 7.5.5 Inventory Management Object Pages There are several inventory management object pages available in SAP S/4HANA:  Material Document  Material  Supplier  Customer  Inbound Delivery  Outbound Delivery We’ll discuss these object pages in the following sections. Material Document Object Page The Material Document object page (see Figure 7.47) displays useful information about the material document posted in the SAP S/4HANA system. Via this object page, you can navigate to related business objects and to transactional apps. Figure 7.47 Material Document: Object Page 7 Inventory Management 296 Here you can do the following:  Display an overview of material document header and line item data, such as move- ment type, document date, and materials transacted.  Obtain a graphical process flow of other business documents related to this material document (see Figure 7.48).  Navigate to additional information relevant to this material document, such as details for related business partners, related master data, or related documents. The Material Document object page is assigned to the inventory manager and ware- house clerk standard authorization roles. Figure 7.48 Material Document: Process Flow Material Object Page The Material object page (see Figure 7.49) is used to display an overview of a specific material. You navigate to this object page from other SAP Fiori apps, or you can navi- gate to additional information related to this material, such as detailed information about related master data or related documents. The Material object page can also show the following:  Suppliers of the material, using the purchasing view  Procurement master data and documents for the material (see Figure 7.50) The Material object page is assigned to the purchaser, warehouse manager, warehouse clerk, and accounts payable accountant standard authorization roles. © 297 7.5 Reporting in Inventory Management Figure 7.49 Material Object Page Figure 7.50 Procurement Master Data and Documents for Material Supplier Object Page The Supplier object page (see Figure 7.51) is used to display an overview of a specific sup- plier. You navigate to this object page from other SAP Fiori apps, or you can navigate to 7 Inventory Management 298 additional information related to the individual supplier, such as detailed information about related business partners, related master data, or related documents. The Supplier object page can also show the following:  Company code data for the supplier  Communication and blocking data for the supplier  Materials provided to your company by the supplier  Annual spend for the supplier The Supplier object page is assigned to the buyer, accounts payable accountant, and many other standard authorization roles. Figure 7.51 Supplier Object Page Customer Object Page The Customer object page (see Figure 7.52) is used to display an overview of a specific customer. You navigate to this object page from other SAP Fiori apps, or you can navi- gate to additional information related to the individual customer, such as detailed infor- mation about related business partners, related master data, or related documents. The Customer object page can also show the following:  Company code and sales area data for the customer  Related sales orders and billing documents for the customer  Communication data and blocking data for the customer The Customer object page is assigned to the customer master specialist and accounts receivable accountant standard authorization roles. © 299 7.5 Reporting in Inventory Management Figure 7.52 Customer Object Page Inbound Delivery Object Page Use the Inbound Delivery object page (see Figure 7.53) to display details about a specific inbound delivery document. You can also easily access related documents and master data related to this inbound delivery document, such as business partners. Figure 7.53 Inbound Delivery Object Page: General Information 7 Inventory Management 300 You can navigate to this app by searching for inbound deliveries from the Enterprise Search area of the SAP Fiori launchpad. You can search for inbound deliveries using key fields such as receiving point, material number, or supplier. The results are shown in a worklist from which you can easily retrieve details for each inbound delivery doc- ument listed. The Inbound Delivery object page can be used to do the following:  Display attributes of the inbound delivery document, such as receiving point, over- all status, and delivery date.  Display the materials to be received, along with quantity and receiving plant and storage location.  Display the contact details of the business partners involved in the inbound delivery.  Display the process flow, a graphical overview of the chain of connected process steps and corresponding business documents (see Figure 7.54). For example, you can view the purchase order that preceded the inbound delivery or the material docu- ment that recorded the goods receipt posting for the inbound delivery. The Inbound Delivery object page is assigned to the receiving specialist, inventory man- ager, and warehouse clerk standard authorization roles. Figure 7.54 Inbound Delivery Object Page: Process Flow © 301 7.5 Reporting in Inventory Management Outbound Delivery Object Page Use the Outbound Delivery object page (see Figure 7.55) to display details about a spe- cific outbound delivery document. You can also easily access related documents and master data related to this outbound delivery document, such as business partners. Figure 7.55 Outbound Delivery Object Page: General Information You can navigate to this app by searching for outbound deliveries from the Enterprise Search area of the SAP Fiori launchpad. You can search for outbound deliveries using key fields such as shipping point, material number, or customer. The results are shown in a worklist from which you can easily retrieve details for each outbound delivery doc- ument listed. The Outbound Delivery object page can be used to do the following:  Display attributes of the outbound delivery document, such as shipping point, over- all status, and delivery date.  Display the materials to be shipped, along with quantity and shipping plant and storage location. 7 Inventory Management 302  Display the contact details of the business partners involved in the outbound deliv- ery.  Display the process flow, a graphical overview of the chain of connected process steps and corresponding business documents (see Figure 7.56).
