sections.title: Home Page and Enterprise Contract Management Overview
sections.en: 9.2.1 Home Page and Enterprise Contract Management Overview The SAP S/4HANA Cloud for enterprise contract management home page provides an overview of the most critical tasks in a single screen based on the data from the under- lying apps, as in Figure 9.2. It allows you to analyze and identify upcoming important dates, reminders, and transactions and take necessary action via the to-dos section and the inbox. It also includes apps focused on the user type. In Figure 9.2, the user is a con- tracts user. The apps most relevant to a user role are displayed: those that allow for requesting and creating contracts. From this page shown in Figure 9.2, you can navigate to Enterprise Contract Management— Processes and Flows and from there move onward to the apps. Figure 9.2 SAP Enterprise Contract Assembly Login Page In the Processes and Flows tab shown in Figure 9.3, you can navigate further into the SAP S/4HANA Cloud for enterprise contract management apps to request a legal con- tract or manage legal transactions. Figure 9.3 Enterprise Contract Management Processes and Flows © 365 9.2 SAP Fiori Apps for Enterprise Contract Management Overview As a contracts manager, you also have further apps assigned for legal content manage- ment, including the Enterprise Contract Management Overview app, as shown in Fig- ure 9.4. The information and access displayed in this app is organized by cards. Figure 9.4 Enterprise Contract Management Overview The information displayed in the Enterprise Contract Management Overview app can be filtered by applying the available filters, such as Contexts, Legal Transaction, and Main Entity. These filters will apply to all relevant cards. For example, you can filter the content of all cards according to a specific legal context or main entity by choosing the respective filters. The following cards are available in this app:  Context Expires Soon Displays expiring contexts sorted by earliest Valid To date.  Legal Transactions with Open Issues Displays legal transactions that are at risk sorted by the creation date of the legal transaction.  Legal Transaction Status Displays the total number of legal transactions and a pie chart showing the status of legal transactions for the current quarter. By clicking each of the status segments in the pie chart, you can display the list of those specific transactions within the Man- age Legal Transactions app.  Context Status Displays the total number of contexts and a pie chart showing the status of the con- texts for the current quarter. By clicking each of the status segments in the pie chart, you can display the list of those specific contexts within the Manage Contexts app. 9 Enterprise Contract Management and Assembly 366  Document Stamps Displays the total number of legal documents that have been stamped and a pie chart showing the total stamp names of such documents for the current quarter. By clicking each of the statuses in the pie chart, you can display the list of those specific documents within the Manage Legal Documents app.  Document Status Displays the total number of legal documents and a pie chart showing the status of the documents for the current quarter. By clicking each of the statuses in the pie chart, you can display the list of those specific documents within the Manage Legal Documents app.  Open Documents Displays the total number of open documents out of the overall documents sorted by the Created or In Process status. By clicking the View All link, you can display the list report of Manage Legal Documents, with all documents filtered based on the sta- tus In Process or Created. If you click the object stream of this stack of cards, you can display the open documents. From here, you can edit or download these documents.  Signed and Accepted Documents Displays the total number of documents with status Accepted and total number of documents that have the stamp Signed, sorted by date and time.  Upcoming Dates Displays the upcoming dates of the legal transactions, sorted by earliest transaction first.  Upcoming Reminders Displays legal transactions for which reminders have been set and their reminder types and dates, sorted by earliest reminder date first.  Average Document Creation Time Displays the average time taken to create legal documents per quarter.  Average Document Finalization Time Displays average time taken to finalize a legal document per quarter.  Pending Tasks of My Legal Transaction Displays legal workflow tasks that are pending. The display list is grouped by legal transaction. This card also displays the total number of pending tasks and the tasks completed in the current year, last six months, or last 30 days.  Average Task Processing Time Displays average time taken to process each workflow task per quarter, based on task types. This card also displays the total number of tasks processed in a year and the number of tasks processed in a day.  Task Completion Displays the number of tasks completed per quarter, based on task types and the total number of tasks completed in a year. © 367 9.2 SAP Fiori Apps for Enterprise Contract Management Overview

sections.title: Manage Contexts
sections.en: 9.2.2 Manage Contexts This app helps create and manage a context used as a template when creating a legal transaction. A context covers a particular business scenario, such as procurement or sales and distribution processes, and provides a foundation for how a legal transaction is processed and what kind of information needs to be provided. Log into the SAP Fiori launchpad, navigate to the Manage Contexts app, and click its tile to execute the app. This app displays existing contexts and allows for filtering/search by Context ID, Owner, Status, Editing Status, and validity dates, as shown in Figure 9.5. Figure 9.5 Manage Contexts The following functions are provided in the app:  Live update function The list of contexts in the content area is updated immediately when a user changes the filter criteria.  Deleting contexts Select a context and delete it directly from the list. Deleting a context is possible only if it isn’t yet assigned to a legal transaction. 9 Enterprise Contract Management and Assembly 368  Personalization of the table settings Display additional columns and rearrange the order of the displayed columns.  Creating contexts From this app, create a new context by clicking the + sign (Create Object). As shown in Figure 9.6, first you fill out header and general information, and then the required information in all of the tabs: – Under the Categories tab, enter the categories that describe the business scenario covered by the context. – In the Parties section, define the parties involved in the business scenario repre- sented by this context. Parties can be entities such as suppliers or purchase orga- nizations, internal contacts, and external contacts. Entities marked as Main Entity in the context are mandatory and can’t be deleted in the legal transaction process. – In the Relationships section, define the legal transactions used in the business scenario covered by this context. For example, in a context for a supplier contract, a legal transaction for the purchase order may be considered a relationship. – In the Dates tab, enter timelines and milestones for the business scenario covered by this context. – It’s possible to define a simple release or even a complex workflow process under the Workflow tab. Figure 9.6 Create Context  Editing contexts From the list of contexts displayed in the Manage Contexts app, you can navigate to the item details and review or edit the context. Here, you can add, display, edit, or © 369 9.2 SAP Fiori Apps for Enterprise Contract Management Overview remove categories, parties, relationships, workflow steps, and dates. Depending on the type of change, a new version of the context can be created.

sections.title: Categories for Legal Content
sections.en: 9.2.3 Categories for Legal Content This app displays existing categories and allows for filtering/search by Category ID, Type, Status, and so on, as shown in Figure 9.7. This SAP Fiori app can be accessed from the SAP Fiori launchpad by clicking its tile. Figure 9.7 Categories for Legal Content By clicking the Create button, you can create new categories. By clicking any of the cat- egories listed, you can go to the details of the category and make changes as needed and also add or edit children categories. The delete function is also available on the ini- tial page of the app. From the initial page on which all the categories are listed, you can export the categories to an Excel file. The app allows import of categories as well. The categories created in this app can be used in the Manage Context, Request Legal Content, and Manage Legal Transactions apps.

sections.title: Manage Legal Documents
sections.en: 9.2.4 Manage Legal Documents Log into SAP Fiori launchpad, navigate to the Manage Legal Documents app, and click its tile to execute the app. When this app is started, a list of available legal documents is displayed, together with the filter bar, which includes filters such as Editing Status, Doc- ument, Legal Transaction, Content Type, Access Level, Main Organization, and more. The list of legal documents displayed includes both created documents and the ones that were uploaded in a static file through the Manage Legal Transaction app. 9 Enterprise Contract Management and Assembly 370 This app provides the following capabilities and features:  Select any document from the list displayed that you want to download and click the Download button to download the document.  Select a document and click the Send for e-Sign button to send the document for e-signature. Enterprise contract management is integrated with the DocuSign e-signature provider, which allows legal documents to be sent to the DocuSign account.  This app shows the e-signature status of a legal document in the header section of the document.  From inside a legal document, the user can edit the document and cancel the e-sign process if the signature isn’t needed.  The app allows users to delete legal documents.

sections.title: Manage Legal Tasks
sections.en: 9.2.5 Manage Legal Tasks This app helps manage the legal workflow tasks that are in the user’s inbox. The work- flow tasks are grouped per legal transaction from where these tasks were triggered. You can launch this app from the SAP Fiori launchpad. The steps to manage legal tasks are as follows: 1. When you open the app, it displays the workflow tasks and allows you to filter by Task Type, Processor, Agent Role, Status, Processed On, and Last Notified On. 2. From the initial page of the app, you can open any of the legal tasks that are listed by clicking it. Once the legal task details are displayed, you can forward the task to another agent if the current agent is unavailable. Notes can be added for the receiv- ing agent while forwarding the task. 3. From the initial list page, key users can notify the responsible agent about tasks that are pending or those tasks that are about to expire. This action can be performed from within the task as well. 4. By clicking a task, the user can view its details in the object page. The object page pro- vides the details under different tabs, such as General Information, Related Task, Agents (details of the agents who have processed this task), Notified On, and Com- ments.

sections.title: Request Legal Contract
sections.en: 9.2.6 Request Legal Contract For requesting a contract, upon navigating into the Request Legal Contract app and cre- ating a new request, you are asked to select the contract context as shown in Figure 9.8. The app comes with an intuitive wizard to take you through a multistep process of pro- viding necessary information and submitting a request for a legal contract. Based on © 371 9.2 SAP Fiori Apps for Enterprise Contract Management Overview the information provided through this app, a legal transaction is created and sent to the responsible person or team for further processing. This app allows you to add or remove documents and mark a document as mandatory or nonmandatory. It’s also possible to upload an attachment through this app. This SAP Fiori app can be started from the SAP Fiori launchpad by clicking the Request Legal Contract tile. Figure 9.8 Contract Request: Context Definition The steps involved in submitting a request for legal content are as follows: 1. Basic Data Enter a Name and choose a Context ID (as shown in Figure 9.8). This should have already been created in the Manage Contexts app. The context selected here pro- vides information for the following steps based on the template of the context. 2. Categories The Group, Path, and Category are filled in based on the context. If the category is marked as Required, it can’t be removed or changed. However, the user can add addi- tional categories if needed. 3. Parties Parties are entities such as customers or suppliers, internal contacts such as pur- chase managers or legal counsels, or external contacts such as contact persons or signing authorities. If the context selected in step 1 has predefined parties, the sys- tem adds those parties automatically. It isn’t possible to remove main or required entities, but it’s possible to add additional parties. 4. Relationship Add relationships in this step. Based on the type of the legal request—for example, a nondisclosure agreement—enter the legal transaction that deals with the master agreement. 9 Enterprise Contract Management and Assembly 372 5. Dates Enter dates, such as the start date, end date, or renewal date, in this step. 6. Review Once all the information needed for the legal content request has been entered, the user can review all the entries in this step and correct or update as needed. Depending on the context selected in step 1, the overall number of steps can vary. If, for example, no relationships are predefined in the context, step 4 won’t be shown in the wizard. It’s possible to add relationships if needed at a later stage after the legal transac- tion is created from this legal request. Now that the legal content request is submitted, the system creates a legal transaction based on the request. This legal transaction will be available in the worklist of the Man- age Legal Transactions app.

sections.title: Manage Legal Transactions
sections.en: 9.2.7 Manage Legal Transactions This app is used to manage a legal transaction through its lifecycle. It’s possible to define the renewal and termination dates for legal transactions using this feature. In addition, the app offers a situation-handling feature to define situations to notify the legal coun- sel when the status synchronization of a legal transaction has failed and should be pro- cessed to ensure successful synchronization. The app displays existing legal transactions and allows filtering/search by Legal Transaction Number, Context, Editing Status, Created By, Changed By, Health (status), and so on, as shown in Figure 9.9. Figure 9.9 Manage Legal Transactions The display columns of the results can be personalized by rearranging columns or show- ing additional columns. From the list displayed, it’s possible to navigate to individual © 373 9.2 SAP Fiori Apps for Enterprise Contract Management Overview legal transactions and edit them as well. From within the legal transaction, it’s possible to create a task and start the workflow. A History function to display the change log for the legal transaction is also provided in this app. Figure 9.10 shows the Edit view of an existing legal transaction; it allows the user to navigate to tabs for Categories, Parties, Relationships, Dates, Reminders, and Tasks and to edit data. From the Documents tab, it’s possible to add documents to the legal transaction. Figure 9.10 Edit Legal Transaction From the initial page of the app, you can select an existing transaction and create a ref- erence transaction by clicking the Create with Reference button. This defines a rela- tionship and ensures traceability between the source and reference transactions. From the initial page of the app, you can select an existing legal transaction and use the Copy button to create a new legal transaction. This app allows you to link objects that are connected to the legal transaction by using the Link Objects feature from within the legal transaction.

sections.title: Manage Workflow Templates
sections.en: 9.2.8 Manage Workflow Templates This SAP Fiori app is available within the SAP S/4HANA Cloud for enterprise contract management solution. To access this app, log into the SAP Fiori launchpad, navigate to the Manage Workflow Templates app, and click its tile. The Manage Workflow Tem- plates app enables the user to create and manage workflow templates associated with contract types. After opening the app, you see the list view, which displays the templates that exist in the system. From this page, you can search or filter templates by Template Name, Sce- nario, Template Type, Workflow Stage, and Created On. 9 Enterprise Contract Management and Assembly 374 From the initial list page of the app, choose + (create) to create a new template. On the create page, enter a name for the template and enter the values as in Figure 9.11. Figure 9.11 Create Workflow Template

sections.title: Customizing Enterprise Contract Management
sections.en: 9.3 Customizing Enterprise Contract Management Enterprise contract management requires some basic customizing to be done in the SAP S/4HANA system. The functionalities explained in the previous section work based on the values maintained in this section. We’ve provided the details of the standard set- tings and values, but it’s possible to customize the system according to varying busi- ness requirements. For example, the business object types defined here are for the purpose of classifying object types to meet business requirements and context.

sections.title: Number Ranges
sections.en: 9.3.1 Number Ranges At the time of creation of legal transactions, contexts, categories, and documents, the system assigns IDs. These IDs are assigned based on the range maintained in this cus- tomizing step. SAP-standard number ranges are shown in Table 9.1. These values are maintained via the following menu path: IMG (SPRO)  Enterprise Contract Manage- ment  General Settings  Number Ranges  Maintain Number Ranges for Legal Transac- tions/Maintain Number Ranges for Contexts/Maintain Number Ranges for Categories/ Maintain Number Ranges for Documents. © 375 9.3 Customizing Enterprise Contract Management

sections.title: Background Job Definitions
sections.en: 9.3.13 Background Job Definitions SAP S/4HANA comes with a job repository for scheduling technical background jobs. Scope-dependent jobs need to be defined in this repository before they can be acti- vated. The application components to which these jobs belong need to be active in the system before maintaining the related table, table STJR_JOBD_SCOPE. For this activity, go to IMG (SPRO)  SAP NetWeaver  Application Server  System Administration  Activa- tion of Scope-Dependent Background Job Definitions (S/4HANA). The following is the list of scope-dependent background job definition names:  SAP_LCM_LT_STATUS_UPDATE  SAP_LCM_CTX_STATUS_UPDATE  SAP_LCM_LT_SEND_EMAIL_REMINDERS  SAP_LCM_SYNCHRONIZE_CATEGORIES  SAP_LCM_CTX_REMOVE_OBS_CATEG 9.4 Summary SAP S/4HANA Cloud for enterprise contract management makes it easy to request con- tracts online, automate contract creation, use workflows, manage document versions, and standardize reviews, approvals, and processing, which makes enterprise-wide access to all legal content easy and fast. This solution ensures legal compliance and increases contracting performance. It also helps corporations to conduct business more effectively, keep customers and suppliers happy, and outperform competitors. The next chapter will focus on the external sourcing functionality in both SAP S/4HANA and SAP Ariba, which is used to drive the correct source of supply for each contract. ©

sections.title: Sourcing Strategies
sections.en: 10.1 Sourcing Strategies A sourcing solution is offered in SAP S/4HANA that integrates with SAP Ariba and SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network helps establish easy and quick connections to millions of suppliers worldwide who are already in the network. In this approach, the sourcing process is initiated in SAP S/4HANA, from which you reach out to suppliers in SAP Business Network, identify the sources through SAP Ariba Sourcing, award the 10 External Sourcing 392 suppliers in SAP Ariba Sourcing, and bring the data back to SAP S/4HANA to create a purchase contract or purchase order to complete the process. The process flow is shown in Figure 10.1. Within SAP Best Practices, this scope item is known as sourcing with SAP Ariba Sourcing. Figure 10.1 Sourcing with SAP Ariba Sourcing: Process Flow Sourcing optimization is achieved in SAP S/4HANA with the help of the SAP Fiori apps described in the next section, as well as the features and functionalities available within SAP Ariba solutions. The sourcing solution helps achieve the following:  Provides visibility and identifies savings opportunities  Standardizes source-to-contract processes across business units © 393

sections.title: Request for Quotation
sections.en: 10.2 Request for Quotation  Drives materials cost savings and optimization across all spend categories  Increases speed and efficiency across different teams  Reduces risk by finding better suppliers and innovation partners 10.2 Request for Quotation A request for quotation (RFQ) is a request from a purchasing organization of a company that’s sent to suppliers, soliciting them to submit a quotation for the supply of materi- als or services. The request for quotation document is a purchasing document created in the SAP S/4HANA system either from a purchase requisition or by copying an exist- ing RFQ. RFQs also can be created manually without referencing any other document. RFQs for lean services can be created by selecting Services as the Product Type Group at the item level. It’s possible to create a single RFQ that contains both material and service items. It’s important to note that the RFQs created in the new SAP Fiori app can’t be viewed or pro- cessed in the SAP GUI environment and vice versa. The RFQ and quotation solution offered using SAP GUI processes and transactions in SAP ERP isn’t a strategic choice in SAP S/4HANA. Support for this legacy RFQ solution is likely to end at some point in the future.

sections.title: Sourcing with SAP Ariba Sourcing and SAP Business Network
sections.en: 10.2.1 Sourcing with SAP Ariba Sourcing and SAP Business Network Sourcing is the ability of the purchasing organization to work in collaboration with the millions of suppliers available in SAP Business Network. The buyers together with the suppliers can improve efficiency and meet compliance requirements across the entire sourcing process. This approach incorporates seamless processes, transparent commu- nications between the buyers and suppliers, and trust between the parties involved in the sourcing process. Sourcing capability is achieved through SAP Ariba Sourcing. This section explains the process steps on the SAP S/4HANA side. In this process, once the RFQ is created and published in SAP S/4HANA, it’s sent to SAP Ariba Sourcing, where a sourcing request is created based on the RFQ received from SAP S/4HANA. The RFQ type used for this process in SAP S/4HANA is an external sourcing request. The buyer then creates a sourcing project in SAP Ariba Sourcing with reference to the sourcing request and publishes the project. This sourcing project results in RFQs in the SAP Ariba Sourcing application for the suppliers to respond to. The suppliers can access these RFQs and submit their responses or quotations through their SAP Ariba accounts in SAP Ariba Sourcing. After the RFQ closing time, the buyer can review all the responses from different suppliers, compare them, and award one or more suppliers in SAP Ariba Sourcing. The awarded quotations are automatically sent to SAP S/4HANA, in which purchase orders or contracts are created, depending on the document type selected in SAP Ariba Sourcing. 10 External Sourcing 394

sections.title: Sourcing with Standalone SAP S/4HANA
sections.en: 10.2.2 Sourcing with Standalone SAP S/4HANA It is possible to execute sourcing without utilizing SAP Ariba integration. In this sce- nario, a request for quotation is created in the SAP S/4HANA system. Bidders are selected, and the request for quote is sent out of the SAP S/4HANA system directly. Responses from the bidders to the RFQ are received back via email or other communi- cation channels and then manually entered into the system. The received quotes can then be compared. Once the winning bid is selected by the sourcing group, it is marked as awarded in SAP S/4HANA, and another communication is sent to the winning sup- plier. The losing bids can also receive a communication as well. The winning bid can then be manually converted by the sourcing group into a purchase order or a contract, depending on the situation.

sections.title: Quote Automation for Procurement
sections.en: 10.2.3 Quote Automation for Procurement If a purchasing organization is interested in requesting only price and quantity infor- mation or shipping costs, it’s possible to use the external price request RFQ type. This RFQ type, once saved and published in SAP S/4HANA, is sent to SAP Business Network, where the suppliers can create their responses. These bids submitted by suppliers through their SAP Ariba accounts are sent back to SAP S/4HANA, where they can be processed. The buyer can compare the bids (quotations) received, award one of those in the SAP S/4HANA system, and then create a purchase order or contract from that win- ning bid. This process, called quote automation integration for procurement, is now integrated into the automation of source-to-pay with the SAP Business Network best practice.

sections.title: Request for Price
sections.en: 10.2.4 Request for Price This RFQ process helps the buyer to create price requests in SAP S/4HANA and send them directly to suppliers by email or send a printed version by mail. The internal sourcing request RFQ type is used for this process. Suppliers respond to the RFQ by pro- viding their quotations via email or mail. The buyer manually creates quotations in the SAP S/4HANA system using the Manage Supplier Quotations app based on the quota- tions received from the suppliers. The quotations created in the SAP S/4HANA system are compared, and the best one is awarded. It’s possible to award the best quotation in one of the following ways: directly within the quotation by clicking Award, from the list in the Manage Supplier Quotations app, or from the list in the Compare Supplier Quo- tations app. After awarding the quotation, the follow-on document, either a purchase order or a contract, is created in SAP S/4HANA. Quotations that do not meet the requirements should be set to Rejected or Completed manually. After completion of this process, the RFQ may be set to Completed as well. The process flow is shown in Fig- ure 10.2. Within SAP Best Practices, this scope item is known as request for price. © 395

sections.title: SAP Fiori Apps for External Sourcing
sections.en: 10.3 SAP Fiori Apps for External Sourcing Figure 10.2 Request for Price: Process Flow 10.3 SAP Fiori Apps for External Sourcing There are several SAP Fiori apps that are used to enable the external sourcing processes described in the previous section. In the following sections, we will describe each of these apps in detail. 10 External Sourcing 396

sections.title: Manage Requests for Quotation
sections.en: 10.3.1 Manage Requests for Quotation The Manage Requests for Quotation SAP Fiori app is used to create RFQs in the SAP S/4HANA system. The RFQ created is sent to SAP Ariba Sourcing based on the configu- ration explained later in this chapter. Then the sourcing process is carried out in SAP Ariba and the awarded quotation is sent back to SAP S/4HANA to create a purchase order or purchase contract. This SAP Fiori app provides the capability to display the list of all existing RFQs and to search for RFQs by RFQ Number, RFQ Type, Status, Company Code, Purchasing Organi- zation, Purchasing Group, Quotation Deadline, and so on. This app also helps copy an existing RFQ, create a new RFQ from scratch, and delete an RFQ. It’s possible to custom- ize the filters and display columns, as shown in Figure 10.3. Here you can do the follow- ing:  Customize and save your own filter settings  Customize the filter bar individually  Copy, Delete, or Create a request for quotation  Customize and save your own table layout From this app, you also can display an existing RFQ by clicking any of the listed RFQs. This allows the user to review all the information within the RFQ, including output details/status, legal transactions associated with the RFQ, and process flow. The Manage Requests for Quotation app is assigned to the purchaser standard authorization role. Figure 10.3 Manage Requests for Quotation App

sections.title: Create Request for Quotation via the Process Purchase Requisitions App
sections.en: 10.3.2 Create Request for Quotation via the Process Purchase Requisitions App To create an RFQ from an existing purchase requisition, access the Process Purchase Requisitions app, select the purchase requisition, then click the Create RFQ button, as shown in Figure 10.4. © 397 10.3 SAP Fiori Apps for External Sourcing Figure 10.4 Process Purchase Requisitions App: Create RFQ This action will take you to the Request for Quotation creation screen shown in Figure 10.5, where the RFQ type, quotation deadline, and organizational information such as company code and purchasing organization are entered. Here you can see how to do the following: 1 Publish an RFQ to SAP Ariba Sourcing once all data is complete 2 Edit details of the existing request for quotation To create a request for quotation, fill in the header and item details, select bidders to whom the RFQ is to be sent, and publish RFQs to SAP Ariba Sourcing for follow-on pro- cesses. Figure 10.5 Create/Edit Request for Quotation 10 External Sourcing 398 The system adds all the information, including item details, from the purchase requisi- tion. It’s also possible to specify the follow-on document, either a purchase order or con- tract, for the RFQ on this screen. This app allows you to maintain delivery and payment terms, add bidders if desired, and add attachments. Once all values are entered, the RFQ is published. At this point, the RFQ is sent from SAP S/4HANA to SAP Ariba Sourcing. Then the sourcing process is carried out in SAP Ariba and the awarded quotation is sent back to SAP S/4HANA to create a purchase order or purchase contract. The Process Pur- chase Requisitions app is assigned to the purchaser standard authorization role.

sections.title: Monitor Request for Quotation Items
sections.en: 10.3.3 Monitor Request for Quotation Items The Monitor Request for Quotation Items app, shown in Figure 10.6, enables the strate- gic purchaser to monitor RFQ items. It allows the user to display the list of all the RFQ items in a table view, along with a chart for awarded quotation value and submitted quotation value. By default, the chart is displayed per supplier; you can change the set- tings to display the chart per company code, plant, purchasing organization, and many more options. The app provides options to choose the chart type, such as bar chart, line chart, pie chart, and more. The output results can be filtered by RFQ number, RFQ type, quotation deadline, purchasing category, material group, company code, plant, pur- chasing organization, and so on. The user can select any RFQ item to view the corre- sponding quotes and general information and navigate to view contextual information related to a supplier or material. The Monitor Request for Quotation Items app is assigned to the purchaser standard authorization role. Figure 10.6 Monitor RFQ Items App © 399 10.3 SAP Fiori Apps for External Sourcing

sections.title: Compare Supplier Quotations
sections.en: 10.3.4 Compare Supplier Quotations The Compare Supplier Quotations app (see Figure 10.7) enables the purchaser to com- pare supplier quotations received against an RFQ and to find the best offer. It allows you to search for a specific RFQ and display all quotations received for it; it also allows you to check whether all the invited suppliers have submitted their quotations. To select the quotation to be awarded, press the radio button next to the quotation num- ber. Selecting Award creates a purchase order or contract. The Document icon exports the list of quotations to a spreadsheet. In this app, you can see how to do the following:  Select the best quotation  Create a purchase order or contract  Export the list of quotations to a spreadsheet The app displays an overview of all quotations for a selected RFQ, providing informa- tion such as basic supplier data, total net value (which reflects the complete net costs for the goods or services, including transportation costs), and fully quoted items (fully quoted items are items that the supplier can deliver in the requested quantity). Figure 10.7 Compare Supplier Quotations App This app identifies the lowest-priced item as the best-priced item. Other factors, such as supplier evaluation score, are not included in the calculation. The purchaser can award the best quotation directly from this app and create a purchase order or con- tract. The Compare Supplier Quotations app is assigned to the purchaser standard authorization role. 10 External Sourcing 400

sections.title: Manage Supplier Quotations
sections.en: 10.3.5 Manage Supplier Quotations The Manage Supplier Quotations app (see Figure 10.8) enables the user to display all supplier quotations that have been received for different RFQs. It also allows the user to select any quotation and view its detailed information. The Manage Supplier Quota- tions app is assigned to the purchaser standard authorization role. Figure 10.8 Manage Supplier Quotations App The app’s features include the following:  Search for a quotation by quotation number, type, status, submission date, supplier, RFQ number, RFQ type, and more  Display detailed information for a quotation by selecting the quotation from the search result list  Display item details, such as the actual item, quantity, and pricing details  Submit quotations that are in the In Preparation status  Edit quotations that are in the In Preparation or Submitted status  Delete quotations that are in the In Preparation status © 401 10.3 SAP Fiori Apps for External Sourcing  Award quotations  Set quotations to Completed  Navigate to detailed information about suppliers and RFQs

sections.title: Manage Workflows for RFQs
sections.en: 10.3.6 Manage Workflows for RFQs The Manage Workflows for RFQs app enables the business process specialist to config- ure workflows for RFQs in the SAP S/4HANA system. Both one-level approval by the manager of the workflow initiator and multilevel approval by the manager of the work- flow initiator and by higher-level managers are possible. This app allows the user to perform the following activities:  Display the list of existing workflow definitions.  Display detailed information for a workflow definition.  Create new workflows and define the step sequence. You can define the start condi- tions and the order in which the start conditions are checked. You can also define the order of the steps. If you have more than one workflow defined, the workflow is selected depending on the fulfilment of the start condition.  Copy an existing workflow and modify it according to your business needs.  Set validity periods for workflows and activate or deactivate workflows.

sections.title: Manage Workflows for Supplier Quotation
sections.en: 10.3.7 Manage Workflows for Supplier Quotation The Manage Workflows for Supplier Quotation app lets you define an approval process for supplier quotations, which allows the approver to check the awarded quotations before a follow-on document is created. The awarded quotation can be approved or rejected. For external sourcing request (RE) types, the workflow process isn’t relevant because these quotations are approved and awarded in SAP Ariba Sourcing. The default setting for quotations of the price quotation (RSI) and internal quotation (RQ) types is auto- matic approval. This app helps the user define a workflow process based on the busi- ness requirements for these quotation types. Both one-level approval by the manager of the workflow initiator and multilevel approval by the manager of the workflow initi- ator and by higher-level managers are possible. This app comes with the following standard features:  Display the list of existing workflow definitions  Display the details of an existing workflow definition  Create new workflows by defining start conditions and step sequence  Copy an existing workflow to create a new start conditions  Activate or deactivate workflows 10 External Sourcing 402 Setting up a workflow for quotations using this app doesn’t require any development skills. This app helps the business user to set up a workflow by following the steps described ahead. Figure 10.9 shows the steps involved. Start the Manage Workflows for Supplier Quotation app and click the Add button to create a workflow. Enter a name for the workflow and provide a description if necessary. You can set up a validity period for this workflow. Choose one or more start conditions for the workflow to start. In this example, start conditions are set to 10,000.00. The workflow will start only if the selected start conditions are met. Standard start conditions available are as follows:  Quotation Follow-On Document Category  Quotation Follow-On Document Type  Initiator of Workflow  Quotation Document Currency  Quotation Document Type  Supplier Quotation Creator  Quotation Total Net Amount Is Greater Than  Quotation Total Net Amount Is Less than or Equal To Figure 10.9 Create Workflow for Supplier Quotation © 403 10.3 SAP Fiori Apps for External Sourcing The next step in setting up the workflow is to add a step sequence, as listed in Table 10.1.

sections.title: My Inbox
sections.en: 10.3.8 My Inbox The My Inbox app displays the list of all quotations that have been sent for approval. Note that this same app is used to centralized approval processing for other docu- ments, such as purchase orders. The user can perform the following actions on quota- tions through this app:  Approve quotations  Reject quotations  Claim a quotation so that only he/she can approve or reject it  Forward a quotation to another user for approval  Suspend a quotation for a certain period of time  Display the workflow or task log

sections.title: Request for Quotation Types
sections.en: 10.3.9 Request for Quotation Types The Request for Quotation Types app (see Figure 10.10) is used to display requests for quotation by RFQ type. You can see the following types of RFQs in this app:  External price requests RFQs that obtain pricing from external systems, such as SAP Ariba  External sourcing requests RFQs for which the bid and award process happens in an external system, with the results sent back to SAP S/4HANA  Internal sourcing requests RFQs that are created and managed entirely within the SAP S/4HANA system The Request for Quotation Types app, as shown in Figure 10.10, allows you to do the fol- lowing:  Display information about the RFQ types in your system  Analyze RFQ type data using customized filters, charts, and tables Step Sequence Type Start Condition Recipient Exception Handling Automatic Release of Supplier Quote Allowed/Selectable N/A Allowed/Selectable Release Supplier Quote Allowed/Selectable Allowed/Selectable Allowed/Selectable Table 10.1 Workflow for Supplier Quotation: Step Sequence 10 External Sourcing 404 Figure 10.10 Request for Quotation Types App

sections.title: Configuring Request for Quotation
sections.en: 10.4 Configuring Request for Quotation With SAP S/4HANA, you can take advantage of the SAP Best Practices activation approach for customizing, as explained in Chapter 2. However, if you choose the tradi- tional customizing approach, this section can help. Please review the customizing information in the SAP Help site as well. For the sourcing process (RFQ) to work in SAP S/4HANA along with SAP Ariba, the configuration described in the following sections needs to be done in the SAP S/4HANA system.

sections.title: Number Ranges
sections.en: 10.4.1 Number Ranges Request for quotation and supplier quotation are the two types of documents that need to be configured for the sourcing solution in SAP S/4HANA. These documents are assigned a unique number at the time of creation for identification. The system will use a number from within the number range defined in this step. Number ranges, which include starting and ending numbers and assignment type (external or internal), are defined using the values shown in Figure 10.11 via menu path IMG (SPRO)  Materials © 405 10.4 Configuring Request for Quotation Management  Purchasing  Sourcing  RFQ and Supplier Quotation  Define Number Ranges for Purchasing Documents. Figure 10.11 Define Number Ranges for Purchasing Documents

sections.title: Activate cXML Message Types
sections.en: 10.4.5 Activate cXML Message Types In this customizing activity, you determine the cXML message types that you want to exchange with SAP Business Network. Start by navigating to IMG (SPRO)  Integration with Other SAP Components  Business Network Integration  Integration with the Ariba Network  Framework Settings  Define Basic Message Settings. Then, maintain the recommended settings as shown in Table 10.7.

sections.title: Credentials and Endpoints
sections.en: 10.4.6 Credentials and Endpoints In this customizing activity, the credentials that identify your company on SAP Busi- ness Network are identified and the endpoints are enabled. The values to be used for this configuration are explained ahead. The values shown in Figure 10.15 are only examples; the values in real projects are unique to each organization. Figure 10.15 Credentials for SAP Business Network Start by navigating to IMG (SPRO)  Integration with Other SAP Components  Business Network Integration  Integration with the Ariba Network  Framework Settings  Define Credentials and End Points for Ariba Network. Choose New Entries and enter the follow- ing values:  SAP Business Network ID The ID of your buyer account  Shared Secret Your SAP Business Network buyer account shared secret  Test Account Check this box if it’s a test account  Enable System ID Used if multiple buyer systems use the same SAP Business Network buyer account  System ID Enter system ID here if system ID is enabled Application Component ID Object Type Object Type Description cXML Mes- sage Type Direction Active BNS-ARI-SE-ERP RFQS4H Request for Quotation QTEQ Outbound Active BNS-ARI-SE-ERP QUOTES4H Quote QTEM Inbound Active Table 10.7 cXML Message Types © 409 10.4 Configuring Request for Quotation  Enable End Points Select for authentication and polling After completing these settings, select the newly created entry, double-click End Points for SAP Business Network, and enter values as shown in Figure 10.16. Enter the following:  SAP-Internal Key System ID, entered in the previous step  Ariba End Point ID Endpoint ID “<S/4 HANA>”, created in the SAP Business Network buyer account (usually the same as the system ID)  Shared Secret SAP Business Network buyer account shared secret Figure 10.16 Endpoints for SAP Business Network

sections.title: Assign Network ID to Company Code
sections.en: 10.4.7 Assign Network ID to Company Code In this activity, the SAP Business Network ID is assigned to company codes in the SAP S/4HANA on-premise system. The SAP Business Network ID assigned here will be sent with each document sent to SAP Business Network and is used to identify the sender. You need to assign this ID to each company code that communicates with SAP Business Network. Start by navigating to IMG (SPRO)  Integration with Other SAP Components  Business Network Integration  Integration with the Ariba Network  Application-Specific Set- tings  Assign Ariba Network ID to Company Code. Choose New Entries and enter the Ariba Network ID and Company Code as needed and save the entries.

sections.title: Schedule Job
sections.en: 10.4.8 Schedule Job Messages, which are quotes received in the SAP Business Network buyer account, will have to be picked up by the SAP S/4HANA system periodically. To achieve this, the fol- lowing background job is scheduled:  Program Name – ARBFND_FETCH_CXML_MESSAGES_NEW 10 External Sourcing 410  Variant attributes – SAP Business Network ID: <ID of the buyer account> – CXML Message Type: QTEM5 The batch job may be set up in the system to run every two minutes using Trans- action SM36.

sections.title: Output Parameter Determination and Use
sections.en: 10.4.9 Output Parameter Determination and Use In this customizing activity, settings needed for output determination for requests for quotation are made. Follow menu path IMG (SPRO)  Integration with Other SAP Compo- nents  Business Network Integration  Integration with the Ariba Network  Application- specific Settings  Define Message Output Control  Method 2: Use SAP S/4HANA-Based Output Management  Define Business Rules for Output Determination. The Output Parameter Determination screen is displayed, as shown in Figure 10.17. Under Select Business Rules, choose the following:  Show Rules for: Request for Quotation  Determination Step: Channel Figure 10.17 Output Parameter Determination Next, make the following entry in the table:  Output Type: EXTERNAL_REQUEST  Channel: XML  Exclusive Indicator: - (false) After entering these values, activate and save. © 411

sections.title: Configuring Flexible Workflow
sections.en: 10.5 Configuring Flexible Workflow 10.5 Configuring Flexible Workflow In SAP S/4HANA, the process owners—such as the person responsible for the sourcing process—are provided with the tools necessary to configure the approval workflow rel- evant to the business processes they own. They can configure the workflow needed for the business processes themselves without needing to go to the IT department. This strategy empowers the process owner and eliminates costs associated with develop- ment. The Manage Workflows app allows process owners to use this new flexible work- flow procedure in SAP S/4HANA. This approach also provides the flexibility to change the workflow as and when required to meet changing requirements. This section describes the configuration steps required for the Manage Workflows for Supplier Quotation app to work.

sections.title: Scenario Activation
sections.en: 10.5.1 Scenario Activation Workflow IDs are provided in the system for each scenario, such as release request for quotation, release supplier quotation, and so on. To activate the scenario relevant to the business process in question, follow menu path IMG (SPRO)  ABAP Platform  Appli- cation Server  Business Management  SAP Business Workflow  Flexible Workflow  Scenario Activation (see Figure 10.18). Figure 10.18 Scenario Activation The supplier quotation workflow scenario is activated by creating an entry as shown in Table 10.8. This setting makes the scenario visible in the Manage Workflows for Sup- plier Quotation app.

sections.title: Maintain Task Names and Decision Options
sections.en: 10.5.3 Maintain Task Names and Decision Options Each workflow ID is assigned a step ID, and possible decision keys such as approve and reject need to be maintained. The step ID determines the task, and the decision keys determine the possible decisions within the workflow. Begin by navigating to IMG (SPRO)  ABAP Platform  SAP Gateway Service Enablement  Content  Workflow Settings  Maintain Task Names and Decision Options. This opens the screen shown in Figure 10.20. sections.title: Summary
sections.en: 10.7 Summary Sourcing—more specifically, external sourcing—involves collaboration with suppliers outside the organization. SAP has strategically used SAP Ariba solutions as the way to achieve this external communication and collaboration. Tight integration optimizes the overall solution capability. In this chapter, we focused on the SAP S/4HANA side of the solution. The next chapter will explore new capabilities in SAP S/4HANA in product sourcing, including the use of sourcing projects for complex requests for quotation. ©

sections.title: What Is Product Sourcing?
sections.en: 11.1 What Is Product Sourcing? In the past, the automotive industry faced significant challenges with demand-driven lifecycles, particularly during the product design phase for traditional gasoline-powered cars. Lengthy lead times for design and manufacturing made it difficult to respond swiftly to changing market conditions or consumer preferences. The industry’s inflex- ible production lines and reliance on specific vehicle models hindered adaptability to shifts in demand, leading to large inventories and increased costs. Moreover, the risk of obsolescence loomed as consumer preferences shifted toward electric vehicles (EVs) due to environmental concerns. Automotive companies, facing pressure from stricter emissions regulations and market competition from innovative EV startups, needed to make a fundamental shift in design and manufacturing pro- cesses. As a result, many companies began investing heavily in EV technology, necessi- tating not only a redesign of their products but also a transformation of their supply chains and manufacturing methods to stay relevant in an era of electric mobility. This transformation underscored the importance of adaptability in an industry undergoing a profound shift toward sustainable transportation solutions. The transformations in the supply chain have a profound impact on procurement pro- cesses for several reasons. First, the emergence of global supply chains has expanded the pool of potential suppliers, increasing the complexity of supplier selection and evaluation. Second, advances in technology, such as supply chain automation and real- time data analytics, enable more efficient and data-driven procurement decisions. Third, the shift toward sustainable and responsible sourcing practices necessitates rig- orous monitoring and compliance checks. Finally, the growing emphasis on supply chain resilience, in the face of disruptions like the COVID-19 pandemic, compels pro- curement teams to reassess risk management strategies and supplier relationships, ultimately shaping the way they source goods and services. A similar situation exists in the industrial manufacturing and components (IM&C) industry. The heightened competition in this industry necessitates aggressive cost management and rapid responses to market dynamics. With a more competitive land- scape, companies must focus on cost efficiency to maintain profitability and remain competitive. Quick responses to market changes, such as shifts in customer demand or emerging trends, are vital for staying ahead of rivals and capturing new opportunities. Moreover, fluctuations in commodity prices can significantly impact production costs. Being able to swiftly adapt to these price changes, whether for raw materials or compo- nents, is crucial to maintain pricing competitiveness and profit margins. Failing to respond promptly to rising commodity costs, for example, can erode profitability or result in higher product prices, potentially driving customers to competitors. The role of procurement in IM&C is pivotal as it directly influences product quality, cost, and supply chain efficiency. Procurement teams are responsible for sourcing raw materials, components, and services, ensuring the timely delivery of materials to © 421 11.1 What Is Product Sourcing? support production. With innovations and process transformations, this role is grow- ing in significance. First, technological advancements in procurement, such as digital procurement plat- forms and data analytics, empower teams to make informed decisions, optimize sup- plier relationships, and identify cost-saving opportunities. Second, as these industries evolve with innovations like EVs and Industry 4.0, procurement becomes essential for securing specialized components and technologies. Third, sustainability and responsi- ble sourcing are gaining prominence, making procurement instrumental in meeting environmental and ethical standards in the supply chain. Finally, global supply chain complexities require procurement professionals to navigate international markets, logistics, and regulatory requirements, further emphasizing their role in driving oper- ational excellence and maintaining a competitive edge in these dynamic industries. As businesses transform their processes, they need modern ERP systems that can han- dle large amounts of data, optimize workflows, and incorporate machine learning and artificial intelligence. SAP is a popular choice for clients looking to upgrade their sys- tems. However, with the end of support for SAP SRM, businesses are searching for pro- curement solutions that align with their strategic vision. SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA (see Figure 11.1) is an excellent option for sourcing and commodity man- agement teams. It allows them to establish high-value agreements for direct materials, such as raw materials, components, and assemblies. This solution is particularly useful for industries with rapidly changing demand, as it improves supplier collaboration on product development, shortening time to volume and reducing direct materials sourc- ing costs. Moreover, because SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA is integrated with SAP S/4HANA, it supports comprehensive sourcing program management and native access to procurement execution systems, material masters, and contract management functionality. As shown in Figure 11.1, the processes for development of new products (forward sourc- ing) and product lifecycles encompass various stages from the initial design to the eventual manufacturing and possible contract renegotiation. Here’s an overview of each step: 1. Design product The process begins with the design of a new product. During this stage, product spec- ifications, features, and requirements are defined. Procurement teams collaborate closely with design and engineering departments to ensure that the product’s design is feasible and aligns with cost and sourcing considerations. 2. Develop procurement launch plan After finalizing the product design, a procurement launch plan is developed. This plan outlines the procurement strategy, supplier selection criteria, and sourcing requirements. It also includes timelines and key milestones for sourcing the neces- sary materials and components. 11 Product Sourcing 422 Figure 11.1 SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA 3. Source supply With the procurement launch plan in place, the next step is to identify and source the required materials, components, and suppliers. This involves supplier scouting, negotiations, and contract agreements to secure a reliable supply chain for the pro- duction of the new product. 4. Contract Procurement teams establish contractual agreements with selected suppliers. Con- tracts detail the terms and conditions of the supply, including pricing, delivery schedules, quality standards, and any other relevant terms. Contracts are legally binding and set the framework for the supplier-buyer relationship. 5. Procure supply Once contracts are in place, the procurement team executes the procurement pro- cess. This includes issuing purchase orders, managing supplier relationships, and ensuring that the supply of materials and components is in alignment with the pro- duction schedule. sections.title: Product Sourcing
sections.en: 11.2 Product Sourcing 6. Manufacture The sourced materials and components are integrated into the manufacturing pro- cess. The production of the new product begins, and quality control measures are implemented to ensure that the final product meets design specifications and cus- tomer expectations. 7. Renegotiate contracts Over time, as the product progresses through its lifecycle, it may become necessary to revisit supplier contracts. This can involve renegotiating terms, adjusting pricing, or accommodating changes in product design. The aim is to ensure that the supply chain remains efficient, cost-effective, and responsive to market demands. In the upcoming sections, we will explore each component of the integrated suite of product sourcing solutions from SAP (see Figure 11.2), providing a comprehensive understanding of how these tools can enhance procurement and sourcing processes in various industries. This deeper dive will highlight the specific features and benefits of each component, offering insights into their practical applications and value for busi- nesses. Figure 11.2 SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA: Extended Hybrid Landscape 11.2 Product Sourcing One of the pivotal aspects of new product development lies in effective sourcing man- agement. In the context of forward sourcing as shown in Figure 11.1, where high-value agreements for direct materials like raw materials, components, and assemblies are established, SAP’s cloud solutions offer transformative benefits to the automotive and IM&C industries.
