This tech- nology allows suppliers to bid on product development competitively, fostering a cul- ture of supplier-driven innovation. In turn, manufacturers use it to elevate the customer experience, curtail direct materials sourcing costs, and expedite time-to- market. Furthermore, SAP’s product sourcing solutions seamlessly integrate with SAP S/4HANA and SAP Business Technology Platform, granting them direct access to material mas- ters. This integration streamlines the creation of operational documents such as con- tracts and purchase orders, aligning them effortlessly with sourcing terms and conditions. This enhanced source-to-contract process not only simplifies operations but also enhances transparency. In the upcoming sections, we’ll delve into three essential subprojects within the pro- curement process. First, we’ll explore the intricacies of the sourcing project, where you can initiate supplier engagement and gather proposals. Following that, we’ll delve into the critical quotation evaluation phase, where you can assess supplier submissions to make informed decisions. Finally, we’ll discuss the vital step of transmitting awarded information to a central purchasing contracts system, ensuring seamless integration between the sourcing efforts and contract management processes. These subprojects collectively contribute to the efficiency and effectiveness of procurement operations.

sections.title: Sourcing Project
sections.en: 11.2.1 Sourcing Project The request for quotation (RFQ) process in materials management plays a vital role in procurement but has its limitations. It can be time-consuming due to manual steps involved, particularly when dealing with numerous vendors. It is worth noting that this document still requires completely manual intervention. For certain industries, this becomes critical due to the large number of suppliers, posi- tions, conditions, and the inability to compare large supplier quotations. Users can actively monitor their existing list of sourcing projects (see Figure 11.3). It’s essential to do so to stay informed about the current statuses, number of participants, and other information for each project. This monitoring ensures that procurement teams can proactively manage and optimize their sourcing efforts, make informed decisions, and address any issues or delays promptly. If you’re looking for a comprehensive solution for sourcing projects, SAP S/4HANA offers a powerful tool. This sourcing project tool offers similar functions to RFQ (see Figure 11.4), but with added features such as complex item and milestone management, demand planning, and access to supplier lists. © 425 11.2 Product Sourcing Figure 11.3 Manage Sourcing Projects Figure 11.4 Sourcing Project: General Information Managing sourcing projects can be made easier by defining specific timelines that only purchasers can see. One way to keep track of important dates related to your sourcing project is by using milestones (see Figure 11.5). Your system administrator or key user 11 Product Sourcing 426 can configure the types and statuses of milestones, and you can easily select the rele- vant milestones from a selection list to help you stay on track. Figure 11.5 Sourcing Project: Milestones From SAP S/4HANA Cloud 2208 and onward, SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA offers a highly useful fea- ture (see Figure 11.6 and Figure 11.7) that allows users to collect and manage cost break- down information for supplier quotations effectively. Collecting cost breakdown information during direct material sourcing is crucial for several reasons. First, it pro- vides transparency into the cost components of a product, enabling buyers to under- stand the cost structure and identify potential cost-saving opportunities. Second, it aids in supplier negotiations by allowing buyers to pinpoint areas for cost reduction and negotiate more effectively. Finally, cost breakdown information supports informed decision-making, helping organizations select the most cost-efficient suppli- ers and make strategic sourcing decisions that contribute to overall profitability and competitiveness. A preferred supplier list is a carefully selected group of suppliers or vendors that an orga- nization has chosen based on their proven reliability, quality, pricing, and compliance, making them the preferred options for procurement to simplify vendor selection and cultivate strong supplier partnerships. SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Auto- motive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA offers a tool to manage your preferred supplier lists (see Figure 11.8). © 427 11.2 Product Sourcing Figure 11.6 Cost Breakdown Template Figure 11.7 Cost Breakdown–Relevant Item of Sourcing Project 11 Product Sourcing 428 Figure 11.8 Preferred Supplier List As a purchaser, you can use this app to create and manage lists of suppliers recom- mended by your company during the sourcing process. These lists can include stan- dard suppliers available for all users, as well as suppliers you specify for your own use. You can use the supplier lists created with this app to assign suppliers to sourcing proj- ects (see Figure 11.9) in the Manage Sourcing Projects app. Figure 11.9 Sourcing Project: Supplier List © 429 11.2 Product Sourcing

sections.title: Quotation Evaluation
sections.en: 11.2.2 Quotation Evaluation Once suppliers submit their quotations via SAP S/4HANA for supplier quotation man- agement, they become accessible for evaluation and comparison within the sourcing project. The Supplier Quotations tab, as shown in Figure 11.10, displays up-to-date infor- mation about supplier responses. Users can efficiently compare multiple quotations, assess attachments and supporting documents, and monitor quotation statuses. This tab streamlines communication with suppliers, facilitates in-depth analysis, and empowers procurement professionals to make informed decisions that align with their organization’s strategic goals. A supplier quotation submitted in a sourcing project typically includes detailed infor- mation such as the supplier’s proposed prices and clear breakdown of pricing, includ- ing potential cost-saving discounts and payment terms. It also outlines delivery information and payment terms. In addition, suppliers may include any relevant terms and conditions and attachments required to meet the sourcing project’s specifi- cations. Figure 11.10 Sourcing Project: Supplier Quotations As a useful tool in the sourcing process, the sourcing manager can review supplier quo- tations and easily compare them by clicking the Compare Quotations button. This allows for a fair and thorough evaluation of each proposal, with the top contenders moving forward to the negotiation stage. The Compare Supplier Quotations app dis- plays an overview of all quotations for a sourcing project. Within the Compare Supplier Quotations app, as shown in Figure 11.11, you can stream- line the process of analysis and comparison in several ways: 11 Product Sourcing 430  Pin and compare You have the option to pin up to two quotations, enabling a side-by-side comparison against all other received quotations. This feature provides a convenient way to focus on specific supplier responses while considering the broader pool of quotations.  Total cost calculation The application facilitates the calculation of the total cost, taking into account all rel- evant factors, such as unit prices, quantities, and any associated discounts or sur- charges. This allows for a comprehensive assessment of the overall cost implications for each supplier.  Price breakdown You can delve into the price breakdown for each quotation, which provides a detailed analysis of how the total cost is distributed among various cost compo- nents. This breakdown helps in identifying areas of cost variance and understanding the drivers behind each supplier's pricing.  Create awarding scenarios The Compare Supplier Quotations app empowers you to create awarding scenarios tailored to your sourcing and procurement objectives.  Initiate negotiations If negotiations are required, the application allows you to initiate communication with suppliers directly from the platform. This functionality streamlines the negoti- ation process by providing a centralized platform for discussions, clarifications, and potential revisions to the quotations. Figure 11.11 Compare Supplier Quotations © 431 11.2 Product Sourcing In the negotiation process within the sourcing project, as shown in Figure 11.12, the sourcing manager plays a pivotal role by selecting several supplier quotations and ini- tiating negotiations to optimize material sourcing outcomes. This process allows for the exploration of various negotiation strategies to secure the best possible terms. Fur- thermore, you can find a similar negotiation process in the guided sourcing capability for SAP Ariba Sourcing, making it a best practice. This solution enables the selection of multiple items within supplier quotations for doing mass changes. For instance, a sourcing manager can swiftly reduce the target price by 15 percent across several items from one or multiple supplier quotations, enhancing efficiency in negotiation adjustments. In addition, the negotiation process is tracked with specific status assignments, provid- ing visibility into the negotiation’s lifecycle stage. In other words, this feature helps sourcing managers monitor the progress and status of negotiations, ensuring align- ment with category sourcing strategies and procurement goals. Like in guided sourcing capability for SAP Ariba Sourcing, SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA excels in facilitating these negotiation practices, enhancing procurement effectiveness and aligning with strategic objectives. Figure 11.12 Sourcing Project: Negotiation 11 Product Sourcing 432

sections.title: Award Decisions
sections.en: 11.2.3 Award Decisions Awarding scenarios (as shown in Figure 11.13) are used during the sourcing process to make strategic supplier selection and contract award decisions. They are particularly valuable when organizations want to align supplier choices with their category man- agement strategies, considering factors like cost savings, supplier performance, sus- tainability, and risk mitigation. Awarding scenarios enhance the decision-making process, improve efficiency, and contribute to strategic procurement practices. Figure 11.13 Manage Awarding Scenarios Figure 11.14 Awarding Scenario © 433

sections.title: Procurement Planning
sections.en: 11.3 Procurement Planning As part of the sourcing project, awarding scenarios (see Figure 11.14) can be prepared and submitted for approval prior to making the final decision. 11.3 Procurement Planning As shown in Figure 11.1, the process of product design and procurement planning is vital in any company. To ensure smooth operations, it is crucial to integrate procure- ment systems with product lifecycle management (PLM) systems. SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA offers an excellent cloud-based version of SAP Ariba Procurement Planning. This solu- tion provides various capabilities, including simplified importing of parts lists from different PLM systems, automated backward scheduling of critical milestones before product launch, and bundling of raw materials, parts, and assemblies across product lines to maximize benefits during sourcing processes. After the procurement launch plan is in place and necessary investments have been agreed upon, SAP Ariba Procurement Planning seamlessly integrates with SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA to kickstart sourcing projects and effectively manage ongoing milestones. This method guarantees that the sourcing strategy is continuously updated, thereby streamlining the sourcing process and enhancing productivity. Figure 11.15 Procurement Project In the procurement planning process, two key roles play a crucial part: the project man- ager and the investment planner. They are responsible for managing procurement projects with regard to the schedule and investment planning. With the help of the 11 Product Sourcing 434 Manage Procurement Projects app (see Figure 11.15), they can define projects, create subprojects, and assign a bill of materials (BOM) that contains the items that need to be planned. The project manager or investment planner can plan procurement activities well in advance, taking into consideration both the time schedule and investment planning of items based on a central bill of materials. SAP Ariba Procurement Planning empowers you to plan the sourcing of items from the early stages, ensuring timely procurement before the manufacturing process begins. In the following sections, we’ll explore three crucial aspects of procurement planning in SAP S/4HANA. First, we’ll delve into identifying necessary items for subprojects using the BOM. Then we’ll focus on creating reliable project timelines through mile- stones and task scheduling methods. Finally, we’ll discover how bundling similar items together enhances procurement efficiency. These topics are fundamental to effective procurement planning within SAP S/4HANA, providing practical insights for successful procurement projects.

sections.title: Parts Import and Assignment to Projects
sections.en: 11.3.1 Parts Import and Assignment to Projects In the BOM section (see Figure 11.16), the project manager or investment planner has the ability to identify the BOMs that include the necessary items for the subproject and are essential for planning purposes. Users can create a customized filter for each BOM to facilitate the initial import of items and for any manual BOM refreshes that you initiate. Figure 11.16 BOM Assignment © 435 11.3 Procurement Planning To manually create items for the subproject, the project manager or investment plan- ner has the option of choosing the Manually Create Items button in the BOM Assign- ments section. Doing so will automatically include the created items in the subproject item table, allowing users to conveniently manage them alongside other project items. To ensure that subproject users have the most up-to-date information on assigned items (see Figure 11.17), it’s recommended to trigger a BOM refresh. This will ensure that any recent updates or changes are reflected in the project’s BOM. Figure 11.17 Items of Procurement Project

sections.title: Milestones and Task Scheduling
sections.en: 11.3.2 Milestones and Task Scheduling To calculate a schedule at an item level, users need to assign a BOM to the subproject in the Manage Procurement Projects app. Once this is done, users can navigate to the sub- project and its item detailed page (as shown in Figure 11.18) and then access the Sched- ule section to trigger an item schedule calculation by selecting Calculate Schedule. The system will then calculate the time schedule and generate a list of its corresponding milestones, events, and tasks (including their dates) based on the assigned item sched- uling template, which is automatically selected by the system. It’s important to note that when calculating the schedule for the specification deadline or supplier award deadline event, the system will only calculate the planned date. This means that users can rely on the system to provide them with a reliable timeline for their procurement projects but should also be aware that some manual adjustments may be necessary based on factors such as unforeseen delays or changes in project scope. 11 Product Sourcing 436 Figure 11.18 Milestones and Task Scheduling

sections.title: Parts Bundling per Sourcing Needs
sections.en: 11.3.3 Parts Bundling per Sourcing Needs For users with the purchaser bundling role, the Manage Bundles app (see Figure 11.19) is a valuable tool that helps them group similar items together into bundles to achieve higher volumes of sourcing. With this app, purchaser bundling can easily create detailed bundles that can be passed on to the sourcing department. Once the bundles are complete, they are ready to be handed over to start the sourcing process. This effi- cient process can help streamline the sourcing workflow and increase productivity. An efficient way to organize items based on sourcing requirements is by utilizing the automatic bundling feature. The system performs this task by considering a specific bundling criterion, which could be any item attribute such as node type, material num- ber, or package. The automatic bundling process generates a preview of the bundles and assigns all unassigned items to them. After that, users can review and modify each bundle as needed before applying the preview changes. This feature helps streamline the sourcing process and saves users time and effort. When transferring a bundle to a sourcing application, the following objects are created automatically in the sourcing application:  Sourcing project  Procurement project  Project item  Invest item © 437

sections.title: Product Sourcing with Enterprise Contract Management
sections.en: 11.4 Product Sourcing with Enterprise Contract Management As shown in Figure 11.16, you can find the assigned BOMs in the appropriate section. Figure 11.19 Manage Bundles 11.4 Product Sourcing with Enterprise Contract Management By integrating SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Man- ufacturing in SAP S/4HANA and SAP S/4HANA for enterprise contract management with the ability to include Icertis part, you gain the advantage of being able to effort- lessly create, update, and assign legal transactions and documents from either a sourc- ing project or a supplier quotation. SAP S/4HANA for enterprise contract management plays a pivotal role in sourcing proj- ects by offering a comprehensive set of capabilities. Its primary purpose is to streamline and optimize contract management throughout the entire sourcing project lifecycle. First, SAP S/4HANA for enterprise contract management ensures contract standardiza- tion by providing templates and predefined clauses, ensuring that contracts align with legal and regulatory requirements, fostering consistency and compliance. Second, it expedites the contract authoring process, allowing the sourcing manager to cre- ate contracts swiftly and accurately using standardized templates. Moreover, SAP S/4HANA for enterprise contract management automates contract-related workflows, including approvals and notifications, reducing delays and manual intervention in sourcing projects. This automation enhances visibility and control over contract progress. Furthermore, SAP S/4HANA for enterprise contract management helps mitigate con- tractual risks by facilitating compliance with legal standards, aligning contracts with organizational policies, and reducing the likelihood of disputes. 11 Product Sourcing 438 Legal transactions, as shown in Figure 11.20 and Figure 11.21, encompass all the infor- mation and materials associated with legal documents. In SAP S/4HANA for enterprise contract management, legal transactions enable seamless integration between SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA capabilities and SAP S/4HANA for enterprise contract management. The linkage between supplier quotations and legal transactions can be established through either manual creation or assignment. Figure 11.20 Legal Transactions Figure 11.21 Details of Legal Transaction © 439

sections.title: Product Sourcing and Commodity Pricing Engine
sections.en: 11.5 Product Sourcing and Commodity Pricing Engine After creating a legal transaction in sourcing projects, you can do the following:  Create legal documents as attachments or virtual documents.  Categorize legal documents as important so that they are displayed as such in the sourcing projects.  Update and reassemble legal documents.  Update a legal transaction if there is any change in the sourcing project and supplier list. This step is mandatory before publishing the sourcing project. 11.5 Product Sourcing and Commodity Pricing Engine In a sourcing project that involves multiple commodities, it’s essential to have detailed information about each commodity’s quantity and cost. Once the procurement pro- cess is completed, a central purchase contract can be generated based on the supplier’s quotation. The commodities can be managed across sourcing projects, supplier quota- tions, and central purchase contracts. For materials, you can even specify the update cycle for each commodity, which determines the frequency of updating the commod- ity’s price conditions in the central contract. By integrating the optional commodity pricing engine within SAP S/4HANA for com- modity management for physical contracts, real-time commodity pricing becomes accessible through SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA. It’s worth noting that, as of now, this real-time pricing functionality is exclusively available for on-premise or private cloud deployments. This means that organizations using these deployment options can seamlessly access and leverage up-to-the-minute commodity pricing data, enhancing their procurement and sourcing activities with dynamic and current market insights. Commodity pricing plays a pivotal role in enhancing procurement strategies and contract negotiations. Leveraging this feature, organizations can access real-time commodity pricing data, historical trends, and market intelligence to inform their decision-making. During sup- plier negotiations, this data serves as an objective reference point, ensuring that pric- ing discussions are grounded in current market conditions, leading to more equitable and favorable agreements. Organizations can link contracts to specific commodity price indices or utilize pricing benchmarks to determine contract terms, resulting in contracts that are adaptable to market fluctuations. The commodity pricing engine streamlines the process of calculating prices for com- modities or products containing commodities traded at exchanges by integrating with external data sources, applying pricing algorithms, and supporting index-based pric- ing. 11 Product Sourcing 440

sections.title: Quotation Management and Supplier Quotations
sections.en: 11.6 Quotation Management and Supplier Quotations During the era of online collaboration with suppliers, essential business processes migrated to digital platforms. Since the era of SAP SRM, companies have begun to understand that interaction with suppliers online brings significant benefits and dra- matically changes the company’s procurement processes. This transformation occurred to bolster efficiency, streamline communication, and ensure real-time access to critical data, enabling companies to respond rapidly to market changes and enhance collaboration with suppliers across geographical boundaries. Integrating any supplier collaboration tools and establishing online collaboration with them is instrumental in optimizing sourcing processes, mitigating the risks of fraud, and ensuring data consis- tency. SAP S/4HANA for supplier quotation management, along with online collaboration with suppliers, offers substantial benefits for optimizing sourcing processes while mit- igating the risks of fraud and ensuring data consistency. This integrated approach enhances efficiency and transparency in procurement operations, notably by promot- ing the following:  Efficient supplier collaboration Online platforms facilitate real-time communication, document sharing, and bid submissions, streamlining information exchange between buyers and suppliers.  Enhanced decision-making Centralized digital platforms enable quicker, data-driven evaluations of bids, aiding in the selection of cost-effective and qualified suppliers.  Automation of contract renegotiation E-sourcing solutions automate periodic contract price renegotiations, ensuring con- tract terms remain aligned with market conditions.  Data consistency and accuracy Online collaboration tools maintain a single source of truth for sourcing data, reduc- ing the risk of inconsistencies or errors.  Risk mitigation Transitioning to digital platforms enhances transparency, audit trails, and authenti- cation mechanisms, reducing the risks associated with fraudulent activities in sourcing. The supplier quotation interface (see Figure 11.22) functions like a form in which suppli- ers provide details about their prices and products. It has sections for items, prices, delivery terms, and more. Suppliers fill in information like item descriptions, quanti- ties, and prices. This setup makes it easy for sourcing managers to compare and decide on supplier offers accurately. © 441

sections.title: Mass Price Update
sections.en: 11.7 Mass Price Update Figure 11.22 Supplier Quotation 11.7 Mass Price Update In the automotive industry, updating contract prices frequently holds paramount importance for several critical reasons. First, automotive manufacturers often engage in long-term contracts with their suppliers to ensure a stable and consistent supply of materials and components. However, the industry is marked by dynamic market con- ditions, including fluctuating commodity prices, currency exchange rates, and evolv- ing supply chain dynamics. These factors necessitate regular contract price reviews, typically on an annual or even more frequent basis. Manufacturers, known as original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), expect their suppliers to provide cost savings over time to maintain competi- tiveness. Frequent price renegotiation allows both OEMs and suppliers to adapt to changing market realities, optimize costs, and ensure that contract terms remain fair and reflective of current market conditions. Moreover, SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manu- facturing in SAP S/4HANA offers mass renegotiation of existing contracts (Figure 11.23) 11 Product Sourcing 442 and automates the update of new terms, streamlining this process to reduce adminis- trative workload and enhance efficiency. This capability ensures that all parties involved are on the same page regarding pricing and terms, reducing disputes and fos- tering stronger supplier-buyer relationships. In the automotive industry, frequent contract price updates are vital to align contracts with evolving market dynamics, maintain cost competitiveness, and foster collabora- tion between OEMs and suppliers. Automation and mass renegotiation capabilities fur- ther enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of this crucial aspect of contract management. Figure 11.23 Contract Price Renegotiation

sections.title: External Collaboration with Suppliers
sections.en: 11.8 External Collaboration with Suppliers The process of external collaboration with suppliers involves setting up digital chan- nels for communication and data exchange. This includes sharing purchase orders, invoices, and product specifications electronically, as well as issuing requests for quo- tations and managing orders digitally. These platforms offer real-time visibility into inventory levels and demand forecasts, helping suppliers plan production more effec- tively. © 443 11.8 External Collaboration with Suppliers Digital transformation has shifted the collaboration approach online due to its effi- ciency, transparency, cost savings, and accuracy benefits. It eliminates delays associ- ated with traditional methods like phone calls and letters, offering instant communication. In addition, digital collaboration reduces manual errors, enhances data analytics capabilities, and easily scales to accommodate a growing supplier net- work. Online collaboration with suppliers is particularly crucial for industries like automo- tive and IM&C for several compelling reasons:  Complex supply chains Both automotive and IM&C industries have intricate and global supply chains involving numerous suppliers and partners. Online collaboration tools provide real- time visibility into these complex networks, helping organizations manage their extensive supplier ecosystems efficiently.  Just-in-time manufacturing These industries often rely on just-in-time manufacturing processes, where compo- nents and materials must arrive precisely when needed to avoid disruptions. Online collaboration ensures timely communication, reducing the risk of delays or produc- tion stoppages.  Product customization Automotive and IM&C companies frequently engage in product customization to meet varying customer demands. Digital collaboration allows for swift communica- tion of design changes and specifications to suppliers, supporting customization without extensive lead times.  Quality assurance Maintaining stringent quality standards is paramount. Online collaboration plat- forms enable continuous monitoring of supplier performance, quality control, and compliance, helping organizations uphold product quality and safety.  Cost efficiency These industries are highly competitive, and cost-efficiency is critical. Online collab- oration reduces administrative overhead, streamlines procurement processes, and minimizes errors, contributing to cost savings.  Innovation and product development Collaboration tools facilitate collaboration on innovation and new product develop- ment with suppliers. They can share insights, prototypes, and technical specifica- tions, accelerating time-to-market for new products.  Sustainability Sustainability and environmental considerations are increasingly important in both industries. Online collaboration allows organizations to work closely with suppliers on sustainable sourcing practices and reduce the environmental impact of their supply chains. 11 Product Sourcing 444  Market dynamics Rapid changes in market demand and geopolitical factors can disrupt supply chains. Online collaboration enhances agility and enables organizations to quickly adapt to changing market conditions.  Regulatory compliance These industries are subject to strict regulatory requirements. Digital collaboration aids in documenting compliance and ensuring that all parties adhere to relevant regulations.

sections.title: SAP Business Network and Product Sourcing
sections.en: 11.8.1 SAP Business Network and Product Sourcing Enriching core SAP functionality with SAP Ariba solutions enables interaction with SAP Business Network and its extensive supplier base, providing clear benefits for current and future SAP solutions. SAP Business Network serves as a global digital marketplace and procurement platform that connects businesses with suppliers. The integration of SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA with SAP Busi- ness Network delivers significant value to the automotive and IM&C industries. First, utilizing the global network offers access to a diverse and extensive supplier ecosys- tem, fostering competition and enabling organizations to identify cost-effective and qualified suppliers globally. Second, it streamlines procurement processes, automates bid management, and enhances collaboration with suppliers, resulting in efficiency gains and reduced manual effort. Third, leveraging a global network enhances visibility into supplier performance and capabilities on a global scale, allowing for better- informed procurement decisions. Finally, it ensures compliance and risk mitigation by providing tools for monitoring supplier adherence to contractual agreements and reg- ulatory requirements, reducing supply chain risks. In contrast, relying solely on a local supplier database limits access, hinders global competitiveness, and may overlook potential cost savings and supplier diversification opportunities.

sections.title: Supplier Portal (Private Network)
sections.en: 11.8.2 Supplier Portal (Private Network) This is a common picture when companies have well-established supplier portals that they utilize for various reasons, especially prevalent in industries like automotive, where custom portals are common for supply chain management and collaboration with suppliers. SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA solutions, such as SAP Ariba supplier quotation and price renegotiation in SAP S/4HANA Cloud, offer a crucial advantage by seamlessly integrating with these existing supplier portals. This integration strategy allows organizations to leverage the robust capabilities of SAP’s sourcing solutions without the need to migrate suppliers to a separate platform © 445

sections.title: What Are Invoice and Payables Management?
sections.en: 12.1 What Are Invoice and Payables Management? In invoice management, all pertinent details of a supplier invoice are entered into the system, which are then verified against both the purchasing documents to which they reference and the quantities of goods or services that have been received to date. If the document details, such as the prices and quantities in the entered invoice, match the information contained in the SAP S/4HANA system, then the supplier invoice docu- ment is accepted and posted to the system. If discrepancies are found, then the docu- ments can be held or parked and the discrepancies addressed with the supplier and with the purchasing and receiving departments. Once the discrepancies are reconciled, then the supplier invoice document can be successfully posted in the system, with appropriate accounting documents created to reflect the general ledger impact of the invoice entry. 12 Invoice and Payables Management 452 In payables management, the accepted invoice becomes eligible for payment. A pay- ment proposal is generated by the system. Once the proposal is reviewed and approved, it is included in a subsequent payment run. Funds are then transferred from the enterprise to the supplier’s banking accounts via a variety of payment methods. The SAP S/4HANA system contains integrated capabilities to handle the complete invoice verification and payables processes. There are three main solution capabilities available in SAP S/4HANA:  Invoice processing Entry and validation of supplier invoices into the system  Accounts payable Processing of payments due to suppliers  Invoice collaboration Working with suppliers to integrate invoices and payables via SAP Business Network We’ll describe each solution’s capabilities in detail in the following sections.

sections.title: Invoice Processing
sections.en: 12.2 Invoice Processing The invoice processing capability of SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement is focused on the entry, validation, and posting of supplier invoice details in the SAP S/4HANA system. The information contained in the invoice presented by the supplier is checked for accuracy against the customer’s referenced purchasing documents and the goods receipts that have been logged into the system. Price, quantity, tax, and accounting information are all checked. If the total invoice amount is in balance with the reference documents, then the invoice document can be posted successfully in the system. The appropriate financial postings are also posted at the same time due to the integration of invoice processing with financial accounting. If the total invoice amount isn’t found to be in balance or additional information or expertise is needed to process the invoice document, then the invoice entry can be held or parked by the invoice entry processor for later processing by knowledgeable personnel. Entry of supplier invoices that reference purchasing documents is supported, as are financial invoices without a specific purchase document reference. SAP S/4HANA brings many innovations to invoice processing. Managing supplier invoices in classic SAP ERP involved a good deal of transferring back and forth between multiple screens. First, selection criteria had to be entered on an invoice listing screen. The resulting report listed all invoice documents that satisfied the entered selection criteria. Detecting issues and resolving them involved moving back and forth between © 453 12.2 Invoice Processing the invoice list screen and the invoice details screen. If you needed to change the selec- tion criteria of the invoice list, you needed to fully regenerate the invoice list first. With SAP S/4HANA, the dynamic search capabilities in the Manage Supplier Invoices app provide a streamlined way of selecting and managing invoices of concern. The many apps available to support invoice processing make the job of entering sup- plier invoices streamlined and simple. The following native SAP Fiori apps for invoice processing are available:  Manage Supplier Invoices  Create Supplier Invoice  Supplier Invoices List  Display Supplier Balances Note The following SAP GUI for HTML transactional apps for invoice processing are also available from SAP:  Create Supplier Invoice (Advanced) (MIRO)  Display Supplier Invoice (Advanced) (MIR4)  Park Supplier Invoice (MIR7)  Release Blocked Invoices (MRBR)  Clear GR/IR Clearing Account (MR11)  Display/Cancel Account Maintenance (MR11SHOW)  Create Consignment and Pipeline Settlement (MRKO)  Create Evaluated Receipt Settlement (MRRL) We’ll take a deep dive into invoice processing in the next sections. First, we’ll look at the different types of supplier invoice documents available in SAP S/4HANA. Then we’ll describe the results of a successfully processed supplier invoice. Next, we’ll describe the two types of supplier invoice processing available. The methods of entering supplier invoices into SAP S/4HANA are described, along with detailed descriptions of the apps supporting invoice entry and reconciliation. Finally, we will describe supplier invoice reporting apps and useful object pages for this area.

sections.title: Supplier Invoice Documents
sections.en: 12.2.1 Supplier Invoice Documents The supplier invoice document in SAP S/4HANA is a representation of the presentation and acceptance of a bill from a supplier to a customer. It also passes information needed to complete the procure-to-pay cycle to financial accounting. Entry of a sup- plier invoice document is a necessary step in most procure-to-pay processes; it ensures that a supplier will be paid for the goods or services provided. 12 Invoice and Payables Management 454 There are four types of supplier invoice documents supported by the SAP S/4HANA system:  A supplier invoice is a document presented by a supplier for reimbursement of goods or services rendered. It contains details about the supplier, bank information, iden- tification of items and quantities purchased, supplier pricing, unplanned delivery costs, and tax and account determination information.  A credit memo is a document used to record the entry of an invoice for a credit claimed from the supplier. This document arises from a return of defective goods, a reduction of an invoice, or for other reasons. These documents can be considered debits for the vendor. The accounting postings for credit memos typically are the reverse of a normal supplier invoice posting. Credit memos can be entered directly into the system or can be generated automat- ically via evaluated receipt settlement (ERS).  A subsequent credit invoice document is posted when you’ve entered and settled an invoice for which the supplier has billed you at too high a price. The subsequent credit memo entered is a value-only document and doesn’t affect the quantities originally invoiced. It’s valuable to enter subsequent credits when needed in the sys- tem to preserve the invoice history.  A subsequent debit invoice document is posted when you’ve entered and settled an invoice for which the supplier has billed you at too low a price. The subsequent debit memo entered is value-only as well and doesn’t affect the quantities originally invoiced. Invoice documents can be created automatically in the system, based on regularly scheduled settlements of procurement processes. These include ERS, consignment or pipeline settlement, or billing based on invoicing plans. These processes produce invoice documents based on data in your SAP S/4HANA system, rather than relying on a bill submitted by the supplier directly.

sections.title: Results of Invoice Processing
sections.en: 12.2.2 Results of Invoice Processing The following actions take place on successful posting of an invoice document in SAP S/4HANA:  A logistics invoice document is created to reflect the supplier billing details.  One or more financial documents are created based on the data entered. These finance documents reference and are traceable to the logistics invoice document. These documents post the amounts entered for the invoice line items to the appro- priate general ledger accounts.  The purchase order history in the referenced purchasing document line items is updated, which provides a complete audit trail of activities linked to line items.  If required, the prices on the material master are adjusted. © 455 12.2 Invoice Processing

sections.title: Types of Supplier Invoice Verification
sections.en: 12.2.3 Types of Supplier Invoice Verification There are two types of supplier invoice verification supported by the SAP S/4HANA sys- tem. They differ in the data that is proposed during the entry of the invoice document. These two types are purchase order-based invoice verification and goods receipt-based invoice verification. Purchase Order–Based Invoice Verification In the purchase order–based invoice verification technique, illustrated in Figure 12.1, the system generates one invoice line for each referenced purchase order item. The quantities proposed during invoice entry are determined by the difference between the total delivered quantity and the total invoiced quantity. If the quantities and amounts on the supplier invoice differ from those proposed, as in the case of a partial goods receipt, these items will need to be adjusted by the invoice processor. Figure 12.1 Purchase Order–Based Invoice Verification Goods Receipt–Based Invoice Verification In the goods receipt–based invoice verification technique, illustrated in Figure 12.2, the quantities and amounts proposed on the invoice entry must match one or more goods receipts recorded in the SAP S/4HANA system. With goods receipt–based invoice verification, the invoice can’t be entered without a goods receipt reference. This procedure is useful if you want to ensure that goods have been received prior to posting a supplier’s invoice. PO 4151599002 100 pieces GR-based IV Invoice For purchase order 4151599002 40 pieces Delivery 1 Delivery 2 Delivery 3 Delivery note AX123 50 pieces Delivery note AX456 40 pieces Delivery note AX789 10 pieces Entry Clerk Selection via purchase order Selection via delivery note Item List 4151599002: 100 pieces X 12 Invoice and Payables Management 456 Figure 12.2 Goods Receipt–Based Invoice Verification The invoice lines created are proposed from each partial delivery connected to the ref- erenced purchasing documents or delivery notes. This allows goods receipts and invoice receipts to be aligned in the purchase order history. This function is controlled by setting the GR-based Invoice Verification indicator on the purchasing organization views for the supplier business partner role. The value here is adopted into the purchasing document. If desired, this same setting can be made at the purchasing organization and plant levels as well by maintaining alternate purchasing data for the business partner. The setting at the plant level supersedes the value from the purchasing organization view. The GR-based Invoice Verification indicator can be set or unset on a purchasing info record (PIR) as well. This setting for a PIR is adopted into the purchasing document pref- erentially over the settings maintained in the supplier master.

sections.title: Entry of Invoice Documents
sections.en: 12.2.4 Entry of Invoice Documents A supplier’s invoice can be entered via a variety of techniques into the SAP S/4HANA system. It’s possible to utilize all types of invoice entry techniques, depending on the supplier and your business requirements:  Invoice entry online, using SAP Fiori apps  Invoice entry via EDI  Invoice entry via the SAP Business Network You also have a couple of additional options during online invoice processing in SAP S/4HANA: invoice reduction and simulation of invoice postings, which we will look at as well. PO 4151599003 100 pieces GR-based IV Invoice For purchase order 4151599003 Delivery note BX456 40 pieces Delivery 1 Delivery 2 Delivery 3 Delivery note BX123 50 pieces Delivery note BX456 40 pieces Delivery note BX789 10 pieces Entry Clerk Selection via delivery note Selection via purchase order Item List 41515990023: 40 pieces Item List 4151599003: 50 pieces X X X 4151599003: 40 pieces X 4151599003: 10 pieces X © 457 12.2 Invoice Processing Online Invoice Entry Using SAP Fiori Apps Use the available online SAP Fiori apps to enter a supplier invoice when the document is presented to you via normal delivery methods, such as the postal service or email. The SAP S/4HANA system automatically adopts referenced documents to minimize data entry, and it verifies that the prices and quantities presented by the supplier match the information in your system. Basic header data about the invoice is entered into the system, such as the invoice date, invoice reference from the supplier, and total invoice amount. A tax code can be entered here if needed. References to purchasing documents such as purchase orders, scheduling agreements, or service entry sheets are then entered. The system will adopt key information from these documents such as quantities, prices, and tax information, thereby speeding up invoice data entry and reducing errors. The system checks that the invoice data from the supplier matches the information in the reference documents. If the total amount doesn’t balance or is outside of config- ured tolerances, then the system will flag the invoice and won’t allow posting until cor- rections are made. Sometimes freight charges passed onto you from the supplier are present on an invoice. If these weren’t planned for in the purchase order itself, this amount can be added to the invoice in the form of unplanned delivery costs. The invoice can be held, parked, saved as complete, or posted by the invoice processor as needed. Figure 12.3 shows these invoice statuses. Figure 12.3 Supplier Invoice Statuses Holding a document lets you save the invoice document in its current state, with only the minimum amount of validation. The system only checks for the existence of the Invoice Park Save as complete MM document FI document info Invoice items Change Post FI Document Vendor 100 − GR/IR 100 + GR/IR account Vendor account Purchase Order History • Goods receipts • Invoices • Parked invoices 12 Invoice and Payables Management 458 company code and supplier. A logistics invoice document is created during hold, but no financial documents are posted and no updates to purchase order history are per- formed. Held invoices need to be monitored and subsequently processed for the procure-to-pay process to continue. Parking an invoice document is useful if you’re missing data needed for posting and you don’t want to have to reenter the data. The invoice document doesn’t have to be in balance to be parked. A logistics invoice document is created, and the purchase order history is updated as well. An open, parked supplier line item is also generated and finance document numbers assigned. A duplicate invoice check also occurs during parking. Parking a document can trigger a workflow to commence further processing on the invoice document. Save as complete is another option that you can use if you have a complete, balanced document but don’t want to post the document at that point. Like parked documents, a logistics invoice document is created, and the purchase order history is updated as well. An open, saved-as-complete supplier line item also is generated and finance document numbers assigned. A duplicate invoice check also occurs when saving as complete. The SAP Fiori apps used to enter an invoice into the SAP S/4HANA system are described in more detail in the following sections. If required, entered invoices can go through an approval process. There are standard workflows available in the SAP S/4HANA system to route a supplier invoice document to approvers based on your company’s requirements. Posting a supplier invoice in SAP S/4HANA will typically result in the following post- ings:  Debit to the supplier subaccount of the invoicing supplier partner on the invoice  Credit to the GR/IR account Invoice Entry Using Electronic Data Interchange EDI can be used between two trading partners to facilitate the exchange of documents. Transmitting a supplier invoice and the subsequent posting of that document in the system is a key process often enabled via this technique. The system validates the data sent by the supplier and, if acceptable, posts the invoice into the system without the need for human intervention. SAP S/4HANA supports multiple EDI protocols for the transmission and acceptance of supplier invoice documents. Invoice Entry via SAP Business Network SAP Business Network is a cloud-based business-to-business marketplace in which buyers and suppliers can connect and do business on a single, networked platform. Exchange of supplier invoices is just one of the standard integrations built into SAP Ariba that can be integrated into the SAP S/4HANA system. © 459 12.2 Invoice Processing Invoice Reduction If you dispute the values or quantities on the supplier invoice presented, you can reduce the invoice entered to match what you think is correct. This is known as invoice reduction in SAP S/4HANA (see Figure 12.4). To reduce an invoice, take the following steps:  Mark the line item as Vendor Error: Reduce Invoice.  Enter the reduced value or quantity (or both) into the reduction fields provided.  Verify the values and quantities given on the supplier invoice and enter them in the fields provided. The system posts two documents when invoice reduction is used. First, an invoice doc- ument for the invoiced quantities and values is created. Second, a credit memo is gen- erated for the difference quantities and values. Optionally, you can also generate a complaint document that can be transmitted back to the supplier in this situation. Figure 12.4 Invoice Reduction Simulation of Invoice Postings SAP S/4HANA can simulate the accounting postings for an invoice prior to the actual posting of the invoice document. This capability allows the invoice processor to observe the general ledger account postings based on the entered data. Click the Simulate button to see the resulting simulated postings. You can also post the invoice directly from the simulation if you wish. sections.title: Invoice Processing
sections.en: 12.2.5 Invoice Processing There are a variety of SAP Fiori transactional apps available to enter and process sup- plier invoice documents in SAP S/4HANA:  Create Supplier Invoice  Create Supplier Invoice—Advanced  Import Supplier Invoices  Release Blocked Invoices  Print Supplier Invoices  Clear GR/IR Clearing Account  Display/Cancel Account Maintenance Document  Create Consignment and Pipeline Settlement  Create Evaluated Receipt Settlement We’ll examine these apps in the following sections. Create Supplier Invoice This native SAP Fiori app allows you to create a supplier invoice based on information received from your supplier. You can reference one or more purchase order items to which this invoice refers. Once entered, SAP S/4HANA compares the quantity and amount data for each supplier invoice item with the data of the related purchase order item. If goods receipt–based invoice verification has been defined for a purchase order item, the system compares the supplier invoice data with the related goods receipt data as well. If the quantities or amounts lie outside defined tolerances, the invoice is posted as automatically blocked for payment. An invoice approval process also can be triggered by the system based on your company’s requirements. When looking at the details, you can reverse a posted supplier invoice or release a blocked invoice. These features are available in the Create Supplier Invoice app (as shown in Figure 12.5 and Figure 12.6):  Create a new supplier invoice document. You can create credit memos, subsequent credits, and subsequent debits as well.  Edit fields on the invoice document, which the system then transfers to financial accounting.  Change the currency exchange rate displayed, if allowed by customization.  Enter invoice line items and reference them to one or more purchase orders for which the invoice was received. You can deselect items that are not relevant. These referenced items can also have multiple account assignments.  It’s possible to create a supplier invoice without a purchase order reference. In this case, additional data will need to be entered manually in the invoice document, such as currency, baseline date, terms of payment, and invoicing party.  Create additional general ledger account items as required.  Enter and check tax data for the invoice. © 461 12.2 Invoice Processing  Edit payment terms if the payment terms pulled from the purchase order need to be altered.  Enter unplanned delivery costs presented on the supplier’s invoice.  Add one or more attachments to the invoice document.  Simulate, hold, or post the supplier invoice.  Reduce the invoice, which generates a credit memo alongside the invoice document for the reduced amount.  Output specific business documents, such as letters of complaint to the invoicing party arising due to invoice reduction. The Create Supplier Invoice app is assigned to the accounts payable accountant— procurement and purchasing manager standard authorization roles. Figure 12.5 Create Supplier Invoice App Figure 12.6 Create Supplier Invoice App: Purchase Order Reference 12 Invoice and Payables Management 462 Create Supplier Invoice—Advanced App The Create Supplier Invoice—Advanced app (see Figure 12.7) is used when the supplier invoice is too complex to enter using the Create Supplier Invoice app. Figure 12.7 Create Supplier Invoice—Advanced App This situation can occur, for example, if you need to make direct postings to materials or assets. See SAP Note 2690969 for a complete list. The Create Supplier Invoice—Advanced app runs directly on the backend SAP S/4HANA system and is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Transaction MIRO. The Create Supplier Invoice—Advanced app is assigned to the accounts payable accountant—procurement standard authorization role. Import Supplier Invoices The Import Supplier Invoices app allows you to import multiple supplier invoices into the SAP S/4HANA system at once. You download a spreadsheet template file, enter the invoice details, then upload the completed file back into the app (see Figure 12.8 and Figure 12.9). The entered information is verified. You may then post the invoices from the app. You can also navigate to the Create Supplier Invoice app to view invoice details, correct any errors, or post the invoice. Extensive documentation on the invoice entry template can be found in the app docu- mentation available at the SAP Help site. Up to 2000 invoice line items may be imported in one execution of the app. © 463 12.2 Invoice Processing Figure 12.8 Import Supplier Invoices App Figure 12.9 Import Supplier Invoices Template The Import Supplier Invoices app is assigned to the accounts payable accountant— procurement standard authorization role. Several other SAP GUI for HTML invoice processing apps are available within the SAP S/4HANA system:  Release Blocked Invoices  Print Supplier Invoices  Clear GR/IR Clearing Account  Display/Cancel Account Maintenance  Create Consignment and Pipeline Settlement  Create Evaluated Receipt Settlement We’ll discuss these in the following sections. Release Blocked Invoices Invoices may be blocked in SAP S/4HANA for a variety of reasons, such as exceeding invoice tolerances or a stochastic (random) block. 12 Invoice and Payables Management 464 The Release Blocked Invoices app allows you to obtain a list of all blocked invoice doc- uments and selectively release any documents that were blocked and for which the root cause of blocking (e.g., a missing goods receipt) has been addressed. Invoices that were manually blocked during invoice entry can be released using this app as well (as shown in Figure 12.10 and Figure 12.11). Figure 12.10 Release Blocked Invoices App: Selection Screen Figure 12.11 Release Blocked Invoices App: Worklist © 465 12.2 Invoice Processing This app runs on the backend SAP S/4HANA system and is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Transaction MRBR. The Release Blocked Invoices app is assigned to the accounts payable accountant—procurement standard authorization role. Print Supplier Invoices This app allows you to print outputs from invoice processing in real time (see Figure 12.12 and Figure 12.13). These outputs include complaint communications from invoice reduction and ERS documents. Figure 12.12 Print Supplier Invoices App: Selection Screen Figure 12.13 Print Supplier Invoices App: Worklist Screen 12 Invoice and Payables Management 466 This app runs on the backend SAP S/4HANA system and is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Transaction MR90. The Print Supplier Invoices app is assigned to the accounts payable accountant—procurement standard authorization role. Clear GR/IR Clearing Account The goods receipt/invoice receipt (GR/IR) clearing account is a general ledger account used for clearing quantities and amounts from goods receipts and supplier invoices. The GR/IR account is cleared if the delivered quantity and the invoiced quantity for a purchase order line item are the same. If there are quantity differences between goods receipts and invoice receipts, then items will remain open in GR/IR. If further deliver- ies, return deliveries, invoices, or credit memos don’t clear the differences and you don’t expect any additional goods receipts or invoice receipts, then you must then maintain the GR/IR account manually (as shown in Figure 12.14 and Figure 12.15). Figure 12.14 Clear GR/IR Clearing Account App: Selection Screen The Clear GR/IR Clearing Account app allows you to clear leftover quantities from the GR/IR general ledger account as needed. The system creates an account maintenance document to record this transaction. © 467 12.2 Invoice Processing Figure 12.15 Clear GR/IR Clearing Account: Worklist Screen This app runs on the backend SAP S/4HANA system and is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Transaction MR11. The Clear GR/IR Clearing Account app is assigned to the accounts payable accountant—procurement standard authorization role. Display/Cancel Account Maintenance Document The Display/Cancel Account Maintenance Document app allows you to show or cancel a GR/IR account maintenance document that was previously posted to the database. You may need to cancel these documents if, for example, the documents were posted in error. This app is shown in Figure 12.16 and Figure 12.17. This app runs on the backend SAP S/4HANA system and is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Transaction MR11SHOW. The Display/Cancel Account Maintenance app is assigned to the accounts payable accountant—procurement standard authoriza- tion role. Figure 12.16 Display/Cancel Account Maintenance Document App: Selection Screen 12 Invoice and Payables Management 468 Figure 12.17 Display/Cancel Account Maintenance Document App: Worklist Screen Create Consignment and Pipeline Settlement The Create Consignment and Pipeline Settlement app allows you to periodically settle consignment and pipeline liabilities that occur during normal business. This app is shown in Figure 12.18 and Figure 12.19. Figure 12.18 Create Consignment and Pipeline Settlement App: Selection Screen Because consignment and pipeline withdrawals are made in the system in inventory management, a supplier liability record is recorded in the system with a price that is valid at the date of withdrawal. This price isn’t on record in the referenced purchase © 469 12.2 Invoice Processing order; it’s obtained from the price maintained in the consignment or pipeline PIR that is valid on the settlement date. Figure 12.19 Create Consignment and Pipeline Settlement App: Selection Screen This settlement function will post an invoice document in the system automatically for any supplier consignment or pipeline liabilities that it finds based on the selection criteria entered into the SAP S/4HANA system. This app runs on the backend SAP S/4HANA system and is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Transaction MRKO. The Create Consignment and Pipeline Settle- ment app is assigned to the accounts payable accountant—procurement standard authorization role. Create Evaluated Receipt Settlement The Create Evaluated Receipt Settlement app allows you to automatically create invoice documents for purchase order items that have been received from ERS-enabled suppliers. The supplier doesn’t send an invoice for its shipments; rather, you create invoices based on the goods receipt quantities and the purchase price found on the purchase order line items. Figure 12.20 Create Evaluated Receipt Settlement App: Selection Screen 12 Invoice and Payables Management 470 You must have good pricing in your system, along with a trusted relationship with the supplier, in order for the ERS process to be successful. You can generate a message to the supplier informing it of the invoices generated via this procedure. This app is shown in Figure 12.20 and Figure 12.21. This app runs on the backend SAP S/4HANA system and is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Transaction MRRL. The Create Evaluated Receipt Settlement app is assigned to the accounts payable accountant—procurement standard authorization role. Figure 12.21 Create Evaluated Receipt Settlement App: Worklist Screen

sections.title: Reporting in Invoice Processing
sections.en: 12.2.6 Reporting in Invoice Processing There are three tactical reporting apps delivered with SAP S/4HANA for use in invoice processing:  Supplier Invoices List  Supplier Invoice Items by Account Assignment  Display Supplier Invoice—Advanced We’ll discuss each app in the following sections. Supplier Invoices List The Supplier Invoices List app (see Figure 12.22) allows you to search for supplier invoices and use the resulting search result as a worklist to display and process details for these invoices. This is very useful for day-to-day invoice management because you can, for example, display a list of blocked supplier invoices and release or reverse these documents easily. Once you’ve selected a document, you can drill into it to see all the details for that transaction. The system automatically knows if the invoice can be displayed via the native SAP Fiori app or if the Display Invoice Document—Advanced app is required. Certain complex invoices can’t be rendered in the native SAP Fiori app. SAP S/4HANA automatically detects these documents and displays them in the appropriate app. © 471 12.2 Invoice Processing In the header section of the worklist, you can filter invoices in the list by entering filter values in the selection fields. You can also create your own variants or hide the filter bar if you wish. You can also do the following:  Sort supplier invoices by different criteria  Hide or show columns in the worklist  Navigate to the details for a specific supplier invoice, including approval and block- ing details Note that this app no longer displays account assignment information. Use the Sup- plier Invoice Items by Account Assignment app to see this information. The Supplier Invoices List app is assigned to the accounts payable accountant— procurement standard authorization role. Figure 12.22 Supplier Invoices List App Supplier Invoice Items by Account Assignment The Supplier Invoice Items by Account Assignment app (see Figure 12.23) is used to dis- play supplier invoice item details based on their account assignments, such as cost cen- ters. For each supplier invoice item, details such as the account assignment type, company code, posting date, amount, and quantity are shown. You can navigate to the Supplier Invoices List app if you need additional details. 12 Invoice and Payables Management 472 The Supplier Invoice Items by Account Assignment app is assigned to the accounts pay- able accountant—procurement standard authorization role. Figure 12.23 Supplier Invoice Items by Account Assignment App Display Supplier Invoice—Advanced The Display Supplier Invoice—Advanced app shows all details available for a supplier invoice document in the system. This app is useful for viewing invoices that were cre- ated in both the Create Supplier Invoice and Create Supplier Invoice—Advanced apps, or through SAP Business Network (as shown in Figure 12.24 and Figure 12.25). The Display Supplier Invoice—Advanced app runs directly on the backend SAP S/4HANA system and is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Transaction MIR4. The Dis- play Supplier Invoice—Advanced app is assigned to the accounts payable accountant— procurement standard authorization role. Figure 12.24 Display Supplier Invoice—Advanced App: Selection Screen © 473 12.2 Invoice Processing Figure 12.25 Display Supplier Invoice—Advanced App: Details Screen

sections.title: Object Pages
sections.en: 12.2.7 Object Pages There are two object pages available in the invoice processing capability of the invoice and payables management area:  Supplier Invoice  Journal Entry (supplier accounting document) Many of the transactional SAP Fiori apps allow you to click a supplier invoice document or a journal entry to obtain details for these items. Supplier Invoice Object Page The Supplier Invoice object page displays detailed information about an individual sup- plier invoice document stored in the SAP S/4HANA system. This object page is called in a variety of ways in the SAP Fiori system: from context-sensitive links in the List Sup- plier Invoices app, for example, or from global search. Use the Supplier Invoice object page to obtain details for an invoice document of inter- est. You can also link to the Purchase Order object page from this app. You can display an overview of the supplier invoice header data, such as the supplier and bank details, referenced purchasing document, and key facts, such as gross invoice amount, fiscal year, and payment status. You can also obtain details about related busi- ness partners, master data and purchasing documents (see Figure 12.26, Figure 12.27, and Figure 12.28). 12 Invoice and Payables Management 474 The Supplier Invoice object page is assigned to the accounts payable accountant—pro- curement standard authorization role. Figure 12.26 Supplier Invoice Object Page: General Information Figure 12.27 Supplier Invoice Object Page: Purchasing Document References © 475 12.2 Invoice Processing Figure 12.28 Supplier Invoice Object Page: Purchase Order History Journal Entry Object Page The Journal Entry object page is used to display information about supplier accounting documents. These documents are produced when accounting postings are made during supplier invoice document processing in SAP S/4HANA. Use the Manage Journal Entries app (see Figure 12.29) to obtain a list of supplier accounting documents that you wish to view. You can drill into an individual document (see Figure 12.30) to obtain an overview of its information, including the supplier, amount, document status, and document posting date. You also can navigate to its related business objects, such as purchase order or supplier. The Journal Entry object page is assigned to the accounts payable accountant, accounts payable manager, warehouse clerk, and inventory manager standard authorization roles. 12 Invoice and Payables Management 476 Figure 12.29 Manage Journal Entries App—Selection Screen Figure 12.30 Manage Journal Entries App: Details Screen © 477

sections.title: Accounts Payable
sections.en: 12.3 Accounts Payable 12.3 Accounts Payable Accounts payable is the second capability provided by the invoicing and payables func- tionality in SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement. Accounts payable departments handle invoice entry and payment processes so that an enterprise’s suppliers are paid while optimizing cash flow. There is tight integration between the invoice processing and payables processing components of SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement: one feeds the other. There are three major areas of accounts payable that the SAP S/4HANA system supports:  Supplier payment processing  Supplier account management  Correspondence

sections.title: Supplier Payment Processing
sections.en: 12.3.1 Supplier Payment Processing Supplier payment processing apps assist the accounts payable accountant in running the operational payables function and assure that payments are made to the suppliers at the optimal time. The following native SAP Fiori apps for supplier payment processing are available:  Post Outgoing Payments  Clear Outgoing Payments (Manual Clearing)  Manage Payment Blocks  Manage Automatic Payments  Revise Payment Proposals  Monitor Purchase Order Down Payments  Manage Supplier Down Payment Requests  Create Single Payment  Manage Payment Media  Approve Bank Payments  Monitor Batches and Payments Note The following transactional apps for supplier payment processing are also available:  Create Supplier Down Payment Requests (F-47)  Post Supplier Down Payments (F-48)  Schedule Automatic Payments (F110)  Post Supplier Outgoing Payments (F-58) We’ll discuss these apps in the following sections. 12 Invoice and Payables Management 478 Post Outgoing Payments The Post Outgoing Payments app (see Figure 12.31) allows you to post and clear a single outgoing payment in one step. Normally, enterprises process outgoing payments auto- matically based on payment proposals. However, if you want to issue a payment to a supplier immediately, you need to enter the payment data manually. You can clear these outgoing payments with open supplier line items. You can also post an outgoing payment to a general ledger account. The following features are available in the Post Outgoing Payments app:  List open items that can be cleared with the outgoing payment.  Add or change the discount to be applied to each invoice.  Create residual items by entering a residual amount and assigning one or more rea- son codes and reference information about the business partner. You can define in configuration if a new item is to be posted to the business partner account or if the difference is to be cleared.  Post an outgoing payment to a general ledger account, if required with account assignment.  Post an outgoing payment on account, which means to a customer or supplier account without reference to a specific item if clearing isn’t possible.  Search for open items of selected suppliers or of all suppliers via fuzzy logic.  Create notes and affix attachments while posting the clearing document. Figure 12.31 Post Outgoing Payments App © 479 12.3 Accounts Payable  Enter characteristics for profitability-related postings to assign profitability seg- ments in profitability analysis.  Arrange open items using an invoice reference.  Simulate the resulting journal entry.  Clear the payment with the selected open items. The Post Outgoing Payments app is assigned to the accounts payable accountant stan- dard authorization role. Clear Outgoing Payments (Manual Clearing) Normally, the system will clear outgoing payments automatically. However, if you’ve paid your supplier manually without reference to an open item, you can use this app to find the matching items and clear the payment manually. The Clear Outgoing Payments (Manual Clearing) app (see Figure 12.32) can provide the following functions:  View open outgoing payments in your area of responsibility in My Worklist.  List open items to clear the open payments.  Apply or change the discount to be applied to each invoice.  Create residual items by entering a residual amount and assigning one or more rea- son codes and reference information about the business partner.  Post an outgoing payment to a general ledger account, if required with account assignment.  Post an outgoing payment on account—that is, to a customer or supplier account without reference to a specific item—if clearing isn’t possible.  Search for open items of selected suppliers or of all suppliers via fuzzy logic.  Enter characteristics for profitability-related postings to assign profitability seg- ments in profitability analysis.  View the withholding tax posted for each open item.  Create notes and attachments while posting the clearing document.  Simulate the resulting journal entry.  Clear the open payment with the selected open items that match the payment.  Clear open items for a supplier account instead for a payment.  Clear open items for down payments. The Clear Outgoing Payments (Manual Clearing) app is assigned to the accounts pay- able accountant standard authorization role. 12 Invoice and Payables Management 480 Figure 12.32 Clear Outgoing Payments (Manual Clearing) App Manage Payment Blocks Payment blocks on invoices or supplier accounts can be set or removed using the Man- age Payment Blocks app (see Figure 12.33). You can use the search and sort functions to select and display invoice documents that are blocked. Figure 12.33 Manage Payment Blocks App The Manage Payment Blocks app provides the following functions:  Search for open invoices by supplier, purchase order, invoice number, or journal entry.  Display supplier accounts and open invoices and view their blocking status. © 481 12.3 Accounts Payable  Display open invoices with payment details and related documents.  View the status of invoices and supplier accounts.  Select supplier accounts and invoices to block them for payment or unblock them.  Enter payment block reasons and comments. The Manage Payment Blocks app is assigned to the accounts payable accountant stan- dard authorization role. Manage Automatic Payments The Manage Automatic Payments app (see Figure 12.34) allows you to schedule pay- ment proposals or payments. You then can obtain an overview of the status of the pro- posals or payments. Figure 12.34 Manage Automatic Payments App The Manage Automatic Payments app has the following features:  Schedule payment proposals or payments directly.  Automatically create payment media after scheduling payment runs. You can find the created payment media in the Manage Payment Media app.  Create payment advices.  Search proposals and payments by identifier, run date, user ID, and company code.  Check for completeness via the log. 12 Invoice and Payables Management 482 The Manage Automatic Payments app is assigned to the accounts payable accountant standard authorization role. Revise Payment Proposals The Revise Payment Proposals app (see Figure 12.35) allows you to check and revise pay- ment proposals and the details of open items. This app helps you ensure that all sup- plier payments are made in a timely and accurate manner and that these payments remain compliant with company policies. You can perform the following using the Revise Payment Proposals app:  Display open payment proposals.  Edit payment proposals to change payment methods, partner bank account, or other payment-related information if needed.  Block and unblock items in payments and reallocate items among payments.  Mass block items in payments.  Calculate the total payment amount by payee, currency, and other criteria.  Check the exceptions log.  Navigate to the Manage Payment Proposals app. The Revise Payment Proposals app is assigned to the accounts payable accountant standard authorization role. Note The key performance indicator shown on the Revise Payment Proposals tile displays only the number of outgoing payments; it doesn’t include incoming payments that could be part of a payment proposal. Figure 12.35 Revise Payment Proposals App Monitor Purchase Order Down Payments The Monitor Purchase Order Down Payments app (see Figure 12.36) is used to keep tabs on supplier down payment information maintained in purchase orders. © 483 12.3 Accounts Payable Figure 12.36 Monitor Purchase Order Down Payments App This app can be used for the following tasks:  View purchase order items using filter criteria such as down payment due date.  Create a new down payment request.  Monitor item counts by category, due date interval, and status.  See purchase order item details.  Drill down to see additional down payment details. The Monitor Purchase Order Down Payments app is assigned to the accounts payable accountant standard authorization role. Manage Supplier Down Payment Requests Ordinarily, down payment requests are generated in the SAP S/4HANA system based on information entered in the purchase order document. However, there are times when you may need to create a down payment request manually. Use the Manage Sup- plier Down Payment Requests app (see Figure 12.37) in these cases to create down pay- ment requests as needed. Once the payment run has made the down payment, the payment run also automatically clears the corresponding down payment request. In 12 Invoice and Payables Management 484 some cases, you may need to clear the down payment request manually. The Manage Supplier Down Payment Requests app allows you to perform the following tasks:  View existing down payment requests from suppliers.  Change existing down payment requests.  Create new down payment requests.  Add notes and attachments to down payment requests.  Export the table of existing down payment requests to a spreadsheet. The Manage Automatic Payments app is assigned to the accounts payable accountant standard authorization role. Figure 12.37 Manage Supplier Down Payment Requests App Create Single Payment The Create Single Payment app (see Figure 12.38) lets you make direct payments to sup- pliers that have open supplier line items and have not yet presented an invoice. Supplier and bank information and amounts to be paid are entered, and a payment is created. This payment posts as a down payment request. This document is used to trigger a pay- ment run. The open items selected are cleared when the payment run completes. This app allows you to perform the following tasks:  Execute one-off payments in one step without an invoice.  Trigger the payment process for specified open supplier line items. © 485 12.3 Accounts Payable  Add attachments to the payment.  Get a log of the results when payment is made. The Create Single Payment app is assigned to the accounts payable accountant stan- dard authorization role. Figure 12.38 Create Single Payment App Manage Payment Media The Manage Payment Media app (see Figure 12.39) enables you to transfer data required for electronic payment transactions to banks via a data medium. A payment medium is created with each successful payment run. The Manage Payment Media app allows you to perform the following tasks:  View existing payment media along with their processing statuses.  Download payment media.  Delete payment media.  Display and analyze payment summary information.
