sections.en: 13.3.7 Operational Supplier Evaluation Supplier scores can also be reviewed in a graphical fashion side by side in the Supplier Evaluation/Operational Supplier Evaluation app, shown in Figure 13.18. Here, the oper- ational scores and weighted averages for time, price, and quantity are displayed, along with an overall operational score. Figure 13.18 Operational Supplier Evaluation As noted in the SAP Fiori apps reference library and as of SAP S/4HANA 1909, there is a further reporting app available for supplier evaluation in the form of the Supplier Evaluation Score History app. As the name implies, this app allows users to view the 13 Supplier Management 542 historical evaluations by suppliers, which are updated via a job. Finally, supplier eval- uation data is, as of SAP S/4HANA 2022 FPS 1, available in real time with no data repli- cation required, meaning that the reports update as documents and data are generated in the system.

sections.title: Configuration
sections.en: 13.4 Configuration In addition to installing the supplier evaluation apps outlined in Section 13.3, you need to complete some basic configuration to enable both supplier and category manage- ment in the SAP S/4HANA system.

sections.title: Supplier and Category Management Configuration
sections.en: 13.4.1 Supplier and Category Management Configuration First, follow IMG menu path Materials Management  Purchasing  Supplier and Cate- gory Management  Purchasing Categories, as shown in Figure 13.19. Figure 13.19 Supplier and Category Management © 543 13.4 Configuration Next, select Define Number Ranges as shown in Figure 13.20. Figure 13.20 Define Number Ranges for Purchasing Categories Once you’ve defined your number ranges, save and move to IMG menu path Materials Management  Purchasing  Supplier and Category Management  Purchasing Catego- ries  Define MIME Types for Attachments and Define Maximum Size for Attachments. MIME here stands for Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions, which allows you to fur- ther define which types of attachments are allowed, as well as their maximum size. Next, proceed to Materials Management  Purchasing  Supplier and Category Manage- ment  Supplier Portfolio Management  Supplier Attribute Settings  Define Qualifica- tion Levels. sections.title: Summary
sections.en: 13.5 Summary A procurement operation run without any kind of reflection or analysis of its supply base is unable to make improvements over time, much less realize the true potential in SAP S/4HANA or its marketplace. Never before have supplier evaluation, classification, segmentation, and analysis been as deeply embedded and dynamic as in the SAP S/4HANA environment today. Organizations can segment and classify their suppliers, assign KPIs, and perform analysis while executing transactions simultaneously in a fluid manner, knowing that the data they’re viewing is current and that the compari- sons they’re making between suppliers are underpinned by sound classification and segmentation of their major spend areas, completely in real time as of SAP S/4HANA 2022. But what happens when the suppliers are spread across multiple ERP systems? In the next chapter, we will review SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition, a solution that can orchestrate procurement activities in multiple ERP systems and can integrate with SAP Business Network. ©

sections.title: What Is Centralized Procurement?
sections.en: 14.1 What Is Centralized Procurement? In the context of procurement, centralized procurement refers to the consolidation and central management of purchasing activities within an organization. This involves centralizing procurement functions such as vendor management, purchase requisi- tions, sourcing procedures, purchase orders, and contract management in a single department or location. A centralized procurement model means that an organization has a central purchasing organization that handles most or all purchasing and sourcing decisions for all its departments or business units. This team acts as a hub for strategic purchasing, making the procurement process more efficient and streamlined across the organization. SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition is a product within SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement. SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition rep- resents a solution for SAP ERP customers with multiple ERP systems to manage their procurement activities in a centralized manner while realizing the advantages of SAP’s procurement solutions in the cloud, such as the SAP Ariba and SAP Ariba Direct Mate- rials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA. SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition represents both a transformation 14 Centralized Procurement 548 path from SAP SRM and a future-ready, intelligent ERP platform for connecting to and consuming SAP cloud solutions to seamlessly augment the process agility, capabilities, and user experience in the overall landscape. Not only is SAP S/4HANA an ERP plat- form, but it can also be deployed as a central procurement system integrated with mul- tiple backend ERP systems, including older versions of SAP ERP, down to SAP ERP 6.0 EHP 6, and non-SAP systems. For simplicity, we can call these connected systems. Many companies have found SAP SRM to be a trustworthy tool for managing supplier relationships in the past. However, the advent of SAP S/4HANA has opened up a world of possibilities and allowed businesses to fully realize their potential. This innovative solution provides unparalleled agility, real-time insights, and streamlined operations, empowering customers to achieve their goals. With SAP’s introduction of SAP S/4HANA as the digital core and the discontinuation of SAP SRM, for which maintenance expires in 2027, organizations are searching for ways, solutions, and software to augment and transform their procurement processes and ensure an orderly migration from SAP SRM. One of the most obvious challenges for a migration from SAP SRM was ensuring like-for-like capabilities in the eventual replace- ment system. One important value proposition of SAP SRM was its capability to act as the central procurement hub instance in front of multiple (ERP) backends, providing the procurement department with the capability to organize, govern, and control their tasks from within a central environment. Procurement departments especially valued SAP SRM’s capability to manage workload, documents, and approvals centrally, in a procurement-focused manner, above the fray and complexities of ERP environments. When the sunsetting of SAP SRM was announced, a natural question from the SAP SRM customer base was, What is SAP proposing to replace its multi-ERP-management func- tionality? In an ideal world, every organization would only have a single ERP instance, but this is often not the case. Many companies and organizations running SAP ERP accumulate more than one system instance. Whether through the acquisition of another company in which the SAP ERP environment wasn’t consolidated or a division that created its own SAP ERP instance due to specific requirements, ERP systems in large, multina- tional organizations sometimes proliferate. Distributed procurement landscapes with numerous backend systems are quite common across larger companies. For example, nearly two-thirds of large enterprises in Europe, the Middle East, and Africa with an SAP SRM system are using it as a procurement hub in front of their diverse, multibackend landscapes. Merely removing SAP SRM and upgrading the ERP backends to SAP S/4HANA creates challenges in multiple areas, but procurement is particularly impacted by this lack of centralization in an ERP landscape. As a business function, procurement benefits from scale and volumes. The more volume you put through a supplier or into purchasing an item, the bigger the cost savings and efficiencies. Not only can you conduct fewer trans- actions, saving time and effort, but you also realize the volume discount most suppli- © 549 14.1 What Is Centralized Procurement? ers offer for saving them from the piecemeal efforts of fulfilling individual orders. Managing procurement in a centralized manner also provides a platform from which to understand your procurement activities holistically, creating a virtuous cycle whereby each procurement iteration becomes more efficient than the last in obtaining the goods and services your organization needs from the best supplier mix possible for operations and to orchestrate your organization’s value creation for the marketplace. When faced with a distributed environment, the first impulse of problem-solving IT executives of yore was to attempt to consolidate multiple ERP systems into one. This proved time-consuming and very complex in some cases. Master data from an acquired company’s ERP environment and overall structure may not have matched the receiving environment. Processes may have been different. The expense of consolida- tion may have outweighed the upside or, from a budgeting standpoint, lacked a suffi- cient business case to prioritize the consolidation. SAP’s strategic direction is now focused upon cloud solutions such as SAP Ariba, SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA, SAP Fieldglass, and SAP Concur, leveraging SAP S/4HANA for the digital core. SAP SRM will be supported until 2027, and much of its procurement capabilities are being rolled into SAP S/4HANA and SAP Ariba. The capability to tie together multiple connected systems for procurement is now available in SAP Ariba Central Procure- ment, private cloud edition. In addition, SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition allows for the coupling of more SAP Ariba solutions and SAP Ariba Direct Mate- rials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA on top, to further leverage cloud solutions and advanced capabilities. The diagram on the left in Figure 14.1 shows the current scenario, which is SAP SRM managing a distributed land- scape. Figure 14.1 From SAP SRM to SAP Ariba Central Procurement, Private Cloud Edition On the right in Figure 14.1, you see the target environment for customers migrating from SAP SRM managing procurement for multiple backend ERPs. Here, SAP Ariba acts as the gateway for all indirect procurement, providing users with a guided approach married with a wide spectrum of organization-specific controls, functionality, and con- tent. In turn, SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manu- Current Scenario: SAP SRM Target Scenario: SAP S/4HANA SAP SRM SAP ERP SAP ERP SAP ERP SAP ERP SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA SAP ERP SAP S/4HANA SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition SAP Ariba 14 Centralized Procurement 550 facturing in SAP S/4HANA acts as a powerful solution for direct procurement. Connected to SAP Ariba and SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA is SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition, which in turn coordinates central requisitioning, central purchasing, central sourcing, central contracts, and central analytics with various ERP systems, including SAP S/4HANA and SAP ERP versions. With this migration path from SAP SRM and set of capabilities, the SAP procurement portfolio provides customers with the tools and platform to not only cope and keep up with the ever-faster pace of change in procurement, but also to drive innovation and disruption by leveraging new technologies such as machine learning and blockchain or enabling the Internet of Things. SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition distributes purchase orders to the respective ERP systems connected in the landscape, as per Figure 14.2. It still allows leveraging of ERP-specific data and processes to continue. For example, a PO created in the SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition hub could use country- specific localization in ERP1, customer-specific process optimization in ERP2, or company- specific legal nuances in ERP3. SAP S/4HANA is the digital core in SAP’s present and future landscapes. From this plat- form, SAP customers can leverage a diverse array of SAP cloud solutions, as well as cen- tralize the management of procurement activities in further SAP S/4HANA and SAP ERP instances. Figure 14.2 SAP S/4HANA as Integrated Platform SAP SRM ERP ERP SAP ERP Market and Sell Source and Contract Request and Buy Reconcile and Pay Bill and Collect Network Digital Core SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement Sales Delivery Warehouse Management Transport Management Quality Management Financial Accounting Asset Management Production Planning Project System SAP Ariba Cloud Soutions Digital Core SAP S/4HANA Procure Digital Core SAP S/4HANA Procure Digital Core SAP S/4HANA Procure Further SAP S/4HANA Environments SAP Fieldglass SAP Concur SAP Business © 551 14.1 What Is Centralized Procurement? Figure 14.2 includes connections to SAP Fieldglass for contingent labor management, SAP Concur for travel and expense management, SAP Ariba/SAP Business Network, and additional SAP S/4HANA, SAP SRM, SAP ERP, and non-SAP environments. SAP customers may only use a portion of these options for their procurement landscape, but the options are there in the event you need to deploy further functionality. Figure 14.3 details the numerous solution options available in this regard. SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition is a “hub” system, and it provides organizations with a centralized platform to manage their procurement processes. This hub system offers several advantages, including enhanced visibility and control over procurement activities across multiple entities or subsidiaries. By creating a centralized software system that functions across buying channels with- out reworking them, procurement teams can pull all their disparate data sets into one place. Cloud, on-premise SAP systems, and non-SAP systems can be integrated, and sys- tems can be added or removed as transactions due to mergers and acquisitions occur, without disrupting procurement operations. When we refer to a centralized platform, we are talking about the ability to manage and coordinate different procurement processes. Currently, there are four scenarios: requi- sitioning, purchasing, contracting, and sourcing. A central analytical tool also enables analyzing and monitoring procurement processes centrally. Figure 14.3 Central Procurement Scenarios SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition represents a comprehensive solution within the SAP S/4HANA suite, tailored to streamline and optimize central procurement scenarios:  Central requisitioning provides centralized, self-service requisitioning across multi- ERP-system landscapes.  Central purchasing provides visibility and actionability on purchase requisitions across indirect and direct spend channels. Follow-up actions can be triggered from NATIVELY INTEGRATED WITH… Central Requisitioning Centrally create requisitions for all connected backends extended by SAP Ariba Buying for SAP S/4HANA Central Purchasing Manage purchase orders centrally while executing locally Central Contracting Create, manage, and distribute central contracts Central Sourcing Bundle purchase requests into central requests for quotations Central Analytics Track central purchase contract consumption and global spend SAP Ariba Buying for SAP S/4HANA SAP Business Network SAP Ariba Sourcing SAP Ariba Contracts SAP for Commodity Management SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA 14 Centralized Procurement 552 the central hub layer, converting requisitions into purchase order transactions exe- cuted in connected ERP systems.  Central sourcing enables central purchasers to aggregate all purchasing demands across various ERP systems and plants and to drive central sourcing events. This sce- nario optimizes the procurement process and increases savings. And the result of the central sourcing is purchase orders or central purchasing contracts executed in connected systems.  With central contracting, you can match what you’re buying against a centrally held contract, you can track global compliance with local specifications, you can apply appropriate pricing and terms to regional POs, and you can manage a distribution of your contracts across multiple ERP systems.  Central analytics provides users with insights into procurement operations across multi-ERP-system landscapes. Strategic buyers can analyze the consumption of cen- tral contracts across entire organizations, as well as identify where global contracts are not being properly utilized. In addition, monitoring global purchasing spend using drill-down capabilities pinpoints the spend volume across the entire organiza- tion. In the next sections, we’ll dive deeper into the various scenarios for central procure- ment, beginning with central requisitioning.

sections.title: Central Requisitioning
sections.en: 14.2 Central Requisitioning In central requisitioning, sourced requisitions from catalogs, material or service mas- ters, or free text items are created and approved via central procurement for a backend ERP system. Central requisitioning leverages online backend search helps, central approval of self-service procurement for requisitions, and pushing approved requisi- tions to connected systems, where they can be converted automatically to a PO. In Fig- ure 14.4, the demand originates in the central procurement instance of SAP S/4HANA in the form of a requisition. In Figure 14.5, the first two steps take place in SAP Ariba Buying for SAP S/4HANA, and the follow-on steps then occur in SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition and the respective backend ERP systems. Figure 14.5 Central Requisitioning with SAP Ariba Buying for SAP S/4HANA With SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition, the requisitioning scenario includes the following:  Using the Create Purchase Requisition app to search for items and create a purchase requisition  Using the My Inbox app to approve or reject the purchase requisition  Replicating the purchase requisition to the connected system  Using the My Purchase Requisitions—New app (see Figure 14.6) to view the status of the purchase requisition  Using the My Purchase Requisitions—New app to confirm the received goods  Using the My Purchase Requisitions—New app to return the received goods After a purchase requisition gets approved, it’s replicated to the connected system. While processing the purchase requisition, you can make any necessary adjustments, like adding a new position. These modifications get synchronized instantly to the hub for approved purchase requisitions, enabling you to work with the most current infor- mation from a single, centralized platform. sections.title: Central Purchasing
sections.en: 14.3 Central Purchasing The central purchasing scenario of SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edi- tion provides a workplace for the purchaser to create and manage all of the purchase documents for connected backend systems. The purchaser can monitor, display, access, and change the purchasing documents irrespective of whether they are created centrally by an employee using central requisitioning or in any of the connected sys- tems. Central purchasing allows the purchaser to manage and organize the daily tasks and workload to ensure that demands are met, sourced, and converted into purchase orders. Once the purchase orders are released and sent to the supplier, they can then be monitored for follow-on processes such as goods receipts and invoicing processes. In Figure 14.7, purchase requisitions extract from connected systems for processing in the hub system. With SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition, the purchas- ing scenario includes the following:  Using the Process Purchase Requisitions Centrally app to manage purchasing and initiate a central sourcing process across connected systems © 555 14.3 Central Purchasing  Closing and deferring purchase requisitions in the Process Purchase Requisitions Centrally app  Synchronizing with the connected system the critical changes in delivery date, material, quantity, price, and deletion of purchase requisitions in the central pur- chase requisition  Assigning, changing, or unassigning a source of supply for extracted purchase requi- sitions  Converting a purchase requisition to a purchase order  Adding a purchase requisition to an existing purchase order  Assign or unassign processors for the selected purchase requisition items  Ability for casual user to change a scenario themselves, as well as edit the plant and company code, in the User Defaults app  Search help integrated with purchasing organization and accounting value in con- nected systems Figure 14.7 Central Procurement Process Flow: Purchasing Organizations can decide to block their purchase requisitions in the hub system, enabling centralized oversight and validation before they are converted into purchase orders and distributed to connected systems and then to suppliers. This approach ensures that all requisitions adhere to company procurement policies and compliance standards, facilitating better control over spending, enhancing cost-effectiveness, and minimizing potential errors in the procurement process. By blocking purchase requisi- tions in the hub system, organizations can make informed decisions, prioritize pro- curement requests, and optimize their overall procurement operations for increased efficiency and accountability. If the Process Centrally switch is on, as in Figure 14.8, the purchase requisition item is blocked from automatic purchase order conversion in the backend. Valid Source of Supply Process PR and Create PO Assign Source of Supply Manage Purchase Orders Centrally Approve PO Invoice Posting Confirm GR PO status update Create PO Approve PR Create PR Connected System PO Extraction PR Extraction No Yes SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition 14 Centralized Procurement 556 Figure 14.8 Process Centrally Switch in Process Purchase Requisitions Centrally App The block ensures that after a source of supply is assigned to the requisition, it can con- tinue to be processed manually by the purchaser and not be immediately picked up by conversion jobs running in the backend and converted into a purchase order. Figure 14.9 Manage Purchase Orders Centrally App © 557 14.3 Central Purchasing Previously, purchase orders were generated manually or through SAP SRM in each ERP system. These orders had to undergo an approval process, adding complexity to the company's order management due to the multiple ERP systems. Purchase orders that are created in the hub system or the ones that have been extracted from other con- nected systems can be managed, as in Figure 14.9, in the Manage Purchase Orders Cen- trally app. The Manage Purchase Orders Centrally app provides the following main features:  Search and filter purchase orders from different connected systems—for example, by approval status or overdue items  Display purchase order details  Create purchase order manually from scratch directly in the connected system  Open and change the purchase order directly in the connected system Central procurement apps such as Manage POs Centrally and Process Purchase Requi- sitions Centrally leverage a data cache of so-called proxy tables for fast searches and to make use of the capabilities of the SAP HANA in-memory database. The original docu- ments still reside in the backend, and data validation, checks, and enrichment happen directly in the backend system. SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition facilitates the integration of attachments linked to the line-item level of a purchase order in the connected system into central purchasing processes. This is achieved through the inclusion of the back- end attachment's document info record in the centrally managed purchase order's object page and the online retrieval and display of the original file from the connected system's content server when the user selects a specific attachment. This integration offers several advantages, including increased transparency in han- dling line-item attachments from connected systems without the necessity of dupli- cating the original files within the hub system. Moreover, it significantly enhances the efficiency of purchase order output from the hub system, encompassing line-item attachments, instead of generating output individually from each connected system. Due to this architecture, the business document IDs remain the original IDs of the backend document. Unlike in other integrated systems, such as SAP SRM and SAP ERP, in which there are sometimes external and internal numbers required for the same PO document, no separate IDs are created for external purchase requisitions or purchase orders in central procurement and there is no need to sync number ranges or define extensive ID mappings. Each procurement document keeps its number assigned by the number ranges in the connected system, making them clearly identifiable to all parties, regardless of whether they are accessing the document from within the Manage Pur- chase Orders Centrally app or directly in the connected system. Even in a single ERP instance, analyzing procurement activities often requires data from disparate areas, such as materials management and accounts payables. In an 14 Centralized Procurement 558 environment with multiple ERPs, this complexity can increase exponentially. Central analytics for SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition allows for procure- ment activities to be analyzed throughout the SAP S/4HANA and SAP ERP connected systems. Section 14.6 explains the basic concepts and introduces the available analytics within SAP S/4HANA and SAP Analytics Cloud.

sections.title: Central Sourcing
sections.en: 14.4 Central Sourcing The central sourcing scenario within SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edi- tion aims to enhance procurement efficiency by consolidating purchasing activities across different divisions or entities within an organization. This strategy optimizes pro- curement processes, capitalizes on collective purchasing power, and enforces standard- ized terms. Integrating with SAP Ariba and SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA complements this approach by providing a comprehensive platform for supplier engagement, negotiation, and con- tract management. This integration allows organizations to extend their procurement capabilities in the central purchasing organization, access an extensive supplier network, and facilitate end-to-end procurement workflows that encompass sourcing, purchasing, and supplier collaboration. If your purchase requisitions don't have a source of supply, the central purchasing organization may start the sourcing process to find a new supplier or contract. By using the Manage Central RFQs app (see Figure 14.10), you can create a central request for quotation (central RFQ) that includes those purchase requisitions without a source of supply. There are two types of central RFQs: internal and external. The organization's internal policy and the accepted sourcing strategy determine which type of central RFQ to select:  The external request is suitable for scenarios where the organization needs to source products or services that are not readily available internally. It involves inviting external suppliers to provide quotations and bids for the required items or services.  The internal request is suitable for scenarios where external suppliers cannot be involved for some reason. In that case, the central purchasing organization acts as a supplier to submit the supplier's quotation. You can perform the following processes in central sourcing:  Using the Process Purchase Requisition Centrally app to create a central RFQ for pur- chase requisitions without a source of supply  Using the Process Purchase Requisition Centrally app to create central supplier quo- tations in the hub system on behalf of suppliers and award the best quotation  Creating purchase orders or central purchase contracts from the awarded central supplier quotation © 559

sections.title: Central Purchase Contracts
sections.en: 14.5 Central Purchase Contracts Figure 14.10 Manage Central RFQs App 14.5 Central Purchase Contracts The purpose of central purchasing contracts is to consolidate an organization's pro- curement efforts by establishing standardized terms, conditions, and agreements with suppliers. This approach streamlines the procurement process, enabling cost savings through bulk purchasing, improving supplier relationships, and enhancing transpar- ency and compliance. Ultimately, central purchasing contracts aim to optimize pro- curement efficiency, reduce costs, and ensure consistent and strategic sourcing practices across the organization. The central purchase contracts scenario allows users to centrally create, modify, and view contracts in the hub system. These contracts can then be distributed to connected systems for use as a source of supply. This feature enables purchasers from different organizational units to benefit from the negotiated terms and conditions. Central pro- curement supports both contracts and scheduling agreements. The configuration steps for central contracts are delineated further in Section 14.8.4. Once these configuration steps have been completed, you can perform the following processes in central contracts:  Create central contracts in the central hub system via the Manage Purchase Con- tracts app, including partial distribution of the central contract to the connected ERP systems by company code, quantity, and/or percentage levels. At the central con- tract item level, you can create items from imported material masters, free text 14 Centralized Procurement 560 materials, and lean service items. Using lean service items is only possible for a free text service and results in the creation of a line item with the item category D in the central contract. However, central contracts limit their creation to item category Standard at the header level.  Approve contracts via the My Inbox app.  Distribute the contracts to connected ERP systems.  Create release orders in an individual ERP system against the distributed contract directly.  Import these release orders into the central procurement system via the Schedule Import of Release Orders app. You can start the job immediately or at a specified time, as well as set up the job to be reoccurring or one-time only. You can set the job to do a full, delta, or ad hoc import of the release orders. With release orders imported into central contracts, purchasers have an overview of all of the release orders released against the central contract in the Manage Central Pur- chase Contracts app (see Figure 14.11). Figure 14.11 Manage Central Purchase Contracts In SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA (for more information, see Chapter 11), buyers and producers collaborate to streamline the process of soliciting a group of suppliers. By consolidating and effec- tively managing information, they aim to secure specific components, plan deliveries, and secure the most favorable pricing. The sourcing project and ensuing quotations © 561

sections.title: Central Analytics
sections.en: 14.6 Central Analytics encompass comprehensive details on commodities, their quantities, and preferred commodity pricing engine (CPE) formulas, especially when dealing with materials involving commodities. An awarded quotation can then serve as the foundation for generating a central purchase contract. Commodity procurement is an empowering tool that allows for a user-friendly, formula- based approach to commodity pricing applicable even for future dates, as well as for col- lecting and managing market data rooted in derivative contract specifications (DCS). Users can input and allocate price fixations and perform end-of-period valuations, mak- ing it easier to oversee purchasing documents across diverse industries. Through commodity pricing integration, as shown in Figure 14.12, it becomes feasible to specify the commodities in use and compute item prices by incorporating the com- modity values. Users also have the flexibility to regulate the update cycle of a specific commodity within a central purchase contract based on individual negotiations with the respective supplier, maintaining price data for materials over varying timeframes. These update cycles can range from monthly and quarterly to semiannual or annual, allowing for a more effective way to adapt to external market fluctuations in central contract commodity prices. Figure 14.12 Commodities in Central Purchase Contracts 14.6 Central Analytics Central analytics for SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition provides the user with centralized analysis and capabilities for understanding procurement areas holistically, as well at the individual, granular, connected system level with KPIs. The Monitor Purchase Requisition Items Centrally app allows you to monitor purchase requisition items that were created in the hub and purchase requisition items that were extracted from the connected systems (see Figure 14.13). 14 Centralized Procurement 562 Figure 14.13 Monitor Purchase Requisition Items Centrally You also have the Manage Purchase Order Items Centrally app to analyze all your pur- chase orders created throughout the organization (see Figure 14.14). Figure 14.14 Monitor Purchase Order Items Centrally © 563 14.6 Central Analytics Central purchase contract analytics apps provide transparency of purchase contract consumption across an entire organization and enable you to identify where global contracts are not being utilized or being underutilized in areas of the organization. As of SAP S/4HANA Cloud 2308, there are two main apps for central analytics: Central Pur- chase Contract Consumption (see Figure 14.15) and Monitor Central Purchase Contract Items (see Figure 14.16). Figure 14.15 Central Purchase Contract Consumption App Figure 14.16 Monitor Central Purchase Contract Items App 14 Centralized Procurement 564 The central purchase contract consumption key performance indicator shows the val- ues for central contract target versus released amount that are available for the per- sona buyer and analyzes the release versus target spend amounts on contracts by various dimensions:  Supplier  Backend purchasing group  Backend purchasing organization  Backend plant  Material group  Document  Trend  Trend by supplier The user can click a supplier to use it as a filter for analyzing other dimensions for that specific supplier, such as material group, as per Figure 14.17. Figure 14.17 Central Purchase Contract Consumption by Material Group The end user can display the data in central purchase contract consumption using pre- delivered visualizations, dimensions, and measures, as well as sorted by individual set- tings and visualizations, by using the configuration options listed in the dropdown menu shown in Figure 14.18. The document view in Figure 14.19 provides the buyer with the complete release his- tory of all central purchase contracts. By sorting the release percentage, the user can © 565 14.6 Central Analytics view the most consumed contracts on top. If the buyer wants to see the details of a spe- cific contract, drilldown capability is provided. The Price History for Central Purchase Contract Items app shown in Figure 14.20 provides:  A detailed analysis of price trends within central contract line items, tracing their origins from the passage of time down to specific price-condition factors.  The ability to distinguish between plant-independent and plant-specific price condi- tions, enabling a more granular understanding of pricing dynamics.  Access to the rationales behind price adjustments at the price-condition level, con- veniently stored within the historical records of each line item in the central con- tract. sections.title: Integration with SAP Ariba and SAP Business Network
sections.en: 14.7 Integration with SAP Ariba and SAP Business Network As per Figure 14.21, SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition serves as a nexus layer for accessing numerous SAP Ariba solutions:  SAP Ariba Supplier Lifecycle Performance and SAP Ariba Supplier Risk Management for supplier management  SAP Ariba Sourcing and SAP Ariba Contracts for identifying and transacting with the optimal suppliers for the various spend categories  SAP Business Network for PO/invoice collaboration and automation, financing, and payment facilitation with SAP Pay © 567 14.7 Integration with SAP Ariba and SAP Business Network  Content management with SAP Ariba Catalog  Direct procurement with SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration  Analytics with SAP Analytics Cloud Figure 14.21 Procurement Reference IT Landscape for SAP S/4HANA and SAP Ariba The main focus area for central requisitioning is SAP Ariba Buying for SAP S/4HANA, which provides a consumer-grade buying experience on top of SAP Ariba Central Pro- curement, private cloud edition. SAP S/4HANA supports this integration from a rela- tive position of strength. SAP S/4HANA has an expanding prebuilt portfolio of native integrations that can take advantage of solutions in SAP Ariba. In central procurement’s standard integration with SAP Ariba Buying for SAP S/4HANA, the latter has to send a requisition to the former and have the remainder of the process for converting the requisition to a purchase order occur in central procurement and/or the respective backend systems. The requisition created in SAP Ariba Buying for SAP SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration Procurement Collaboration Logistic Collaboration SAP Ariba Strategic Sourcing Sourcing Contracts SLP SAP Ariba Buying for SAP S/4HANA Requisitioning Catalogs Asset Management Collaboration SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network Config Wizard Test Central Monitoring SAP S/4HANA for Supplier Quotation Management Supplier Quotations SAP Integration Suite Mapping Transformation Open Connectors Messaging Mapping Repository SAP MDG for Suppliers (Optional) Master Data Governance Master Data Consolidation Sourcing Renegotiations SAP S/4HANA SAP ERP Central Requisitioning Central Purchasing Central Contracts Central Sourcing SAP Ariba SAP BTP SAP S/4HANA, SAP ERP SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA SAP Ariba Central Procure- ment, private cloud edition 14 Centralized Procurement 568 S/4HANA is updated with the purchase order document created in central procurement. This is along the lines of what’s called a classic scenario in SAP SRM connected to a back- end ERP system. SAP SRM creates a requisition/shopping cart and then sends a requisi- tion down to SAP ERP for PO conversion once the SAP SRM shopping cart has been approved. The follow-on processes for PO creation and invoice reconciliation/accounts payable occur in the backend ERP system, with SAP SRM reflecting the follow-on docu- ments. The leading documents after the SAP SRM shopping cart are effectively in SAP ERP. SAP SRM also has an extended classic scenario, whereby the requisition and the pur- chase order are created in SAP SRM and managed there. In SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition, you can start the sourcing process for requisitions that do not have valid sources of supply, similar to what we did for shopping carts in SAP SRM. For indirect procurement, the sourcing process can be initiated in SAP Ariba as a part of the central sourcing scenario. This is done by process- ing requisitions extracted from multiple connected systems and then creating the external central request for quotation for them. The other challenge is the data model. Central procurement is flexible in terms of man- aging multiple backend systems and some duplication in the data. If the same supplier record appears in two different forms in two different backend systems, central pro- curement running without SAP Ariba can still route documents to the correct ERP envi- ronment because central procurement creates the document directly in the ERP environment. When adding SAP Ariba Buying for SAP S/4HANA and SAP Business Network for pur- chase order and invoice processing, a one-to-one relationship is needed for supplier data. SAP Ariba Buying for SAP S/4HANA cannot maintain this duplication of supplier records easily. A supplier logging into SAP Business Network expects one login and not multiple ones based on the backend origin of the supplier record. Maintaining a single catalog for the organization quickly breaks down with the complexities of presenting a single catalog item tied to multiple versions of a supplier, depending upon which com- pany code and backend SAP ERP system will ultimately receive this order. Add in part- ner functionality/supplier hierarchies for multiple invoice locations of a supplier from an SAP ERP environment, and a seemingly simple integration can quickly encounter challenges. In these situations, a further data harmonization step is often required via SAP Master Data Governance (SAP MDG), which is a project (and license) of its own.

sections.title: Configuring SAP Ariba Central Procurement, Private Cloud
sections.en: 14.8 Configuring SAP Ariba Central Procurement, Private Cloud Edition From an architectural standpoint, SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edi- tion is an integrated part of the SAP S/4HANA system and code and can be activated and implemented on any SAP S/4HANA instance in parallel with the existing © 569 14.8 Configuring SAP Ariba Central Procurement, Private Cloud Edition processes, subject to the purchase of the additional license. This means that any existing SAP S/4HANA instance can be converted into the procurement hub system and that there is no need to purchase additional hardware. Existing processes in this central instance remain untouched and can be run simultaneously without interfer- ing. Within this system you could run the existing SAP S/4HANA procurement pro- cesses, often also referred to as local procurement, and connect them to the central processes of SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition. These local pro- cesses are mostly treated like any other backend. In the upcoming sections, we will explore the fundamental setup of the hub system, including establishing connectivity between the hub system and the ERP system, con- figuring the system, and integrating SAP Ariba Buying for SAP S/4HANA with central procurement.

sections.title: Prerequisites
sections.en: 14.8.1 Prerequisites With its cloud-first strategy, SAP introduced a concept for SAP S/4HANA in which new developments are designed, developed, and deployed based on cloud principals but then are also made available on premise. Similarly, central procurement as an inte- grated part of SAP S/4HANA can be deployed in the cloud or on premise. Although there are huge differences between these deployment models, especially with regards to ease of consumption, upgrade speed, and software lifecycle, both options provide the same set of functionalities. Differences exist, due to the nature and requirements of the cloud, in how the connection to the backend landscape is realized. The following systems are supported as backends, as shown in Figure 14.22:  SAP ERP EHP 6.06 or greater with add-on HUBERPI  SAP Business Suite on SAP HANA  SAP S/4HANA 1709 or later with add-on HUBS4IC  SAP S/4HANA Cloud system release 2208 Figure 14.22 Versions of Backend Systems Connected to SAP Ariba Central Procurement for SAP S/4HANA SAP S/4HANA SAP S/4HANA Cloud SAP ERP EHP 6 or greater SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition SAP Business Suite on SAP HANA 14 Centralized Procurement 570 For communication with the backends, OData or SOA services are used. Transactional data, such as data in purchase requisitions, is usually transferred via asynchronous SOA services, whereas data validation, lookups, or actions are usually performed with synchronous OData service calls to the backends. The needed interfaces are provided for the on-premise backends as part of an integra- tion add-on—an additional software component that needs to be installed in the back- end systems. This component can be installed easily in the backend and decouples the lifecycle of the interfaces from the complex and costly lifecycle of underlying SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA systems. For any business process that is spread across multiple systems, the biggest challenge is master data. In case of procurement, this data includes materials, suppliers, and accounting information, but also organizational information like material groups or the purchasing organization. In the case of a central system architecture, as with any central procurement hub system, two options can be distinguished: either all master data, business logic, and all business objects can be consolidated into the central sys- tem, or the workplace and business object access and workload organization can be centralized. Consolidation can be a tedious and arduous task. It requires a companywide under- standing of which processes and process-specific data needs to be incorporated into the central process flow, master data harmonization across many systems, or the cre- ation of a mapping and data governance infrastructure. It comes with high TCO, and consolidated processes are usually error-prone and require constant maintenance effort, especially if the backend processes are very heterogenous. In addition, it can slow down innovation cycles in the backends, as well as in the hub, and new features need to be introduced synchronously in the central system and the backend. As shown in Figure 14.23, centralization keeps the business logic and all business docu- ments in the backends, which reduces the need to harmonize or map master data sig- nificantly. Only very few master data elements need to be harmonized or mapped. Mainly these are material groups and purchasing organizations. For central contract management alone, harmonized material master data is required across the backend landscape at this point in time. SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition is not merely a consolidated pur- chase order creation app but a purchasing control center, which allows customers to (remotely) control a global, distributed, and diverse operational procurement ecosys- tem while maintaining analytical and operational transparency and compliance. Before embarking on an SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition imple- mentation or any other implementation, it’s important to review the online documen- tation for the latest information, as well as the version release notes. For SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition, the release note is SAP Note 2649491. It is © 571 14.8 Configuring SAP Ariba Central Procurement, Private Cloud Edition highly advisable to thoroughly review the public configuration guide before com- mencing any configuration activities for SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition. This practice ensures that configuration efforts are well-informed and aligned with the system's intended capabilities, thereby minimizing the risk of costly errors or misconfigurations that could potentially disrupt crucial procurement processes. Figure 14.23 Centralizing of Procurement Workplace and Workload It's important to note that new customers who start with SAP S/4HANA Cloud 2011 or a later version use SAP Central Business Configuration as their configuration environ- ment. For those customers who have a different version of the cloud system, they can use the Manage Your Solution app. However, customers who have an on-premise ver- sion can still use Transaction SPRO for functional configurations. For additional infor- mation on the necessary paths for the Manage Your Solution app and Transaction SPRO, refer to the SAP Best Practices for SAP S/4HANA Cloud documentation.

sections.en: 14.8.2 Establishing Connectivity to ERP Systems The first step is setting up connectivity to the necessary ERP systems to be managed by SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition. This is a cross-scenario configu- ration activity for SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition. With the SAP_ BR_BPC_EXPERT and SAP_BR_ADMINISTRATOR roles or their equivalents assigned to your user, you first need the Basis team to create RFC connections to each ERP environment using Transaction SM59. The Basis team should create ABAP and HTTPS connection RFCs along with an SAP Gateway system alias in table /IWFND/V_DFSYAL. The Basis team then needs to create the logical system references in your hub environment for each connected ERP system using Transaction BD54. Finally, the Basis team ties the RFCs to the logical systems’ BAPI calls in Transaction BD97 by entering the RFC connection in the field shown in Figure 14.24. sections.title: Validating Data and Identifying Gaps
sections.en: 14.8.3 Validating Data and Identifying Gaps With SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition utilizing centralization as its key principal, the need to synchronize data, including master data, is greatly reduced. To provide fast access, easy search capabilities, and analytical functions, SAP Ariba Cen- tral Procurement, private cloud edition uses the underlying SAP HANA in-memory database technology. Information about the business documents from the different backends is updated continuously into SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition, and all read access to any document happens via this cached data within the SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition solution. Via OData interfaces in the backends, changed or newly created business objects are updated as per Figure 14.27. Figure 14.27 Overview of SAP Ariba Central Procurement, Private Cloud Edition Architecture and Data Flow The update cycles can be customized, and programs for initially filling the cache tables in the hub are available. The option to restrict the business objects to be transferred to the central system is also available. The data import is consistently tracked and moni- tored by appropriate logging functionality so that errors can be identified and resolved. With the ad hoc import functionality, it’s also possible to manually import only specific documents at any given point in time. sections.en: 14.8.4 Configuring SAP Ariba Central Procurement, Private Cloud Edition Scenarios SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition covers a wide array of function- alities that can be used to manage procurement activities in a distributed ERP environ- ment. Customers can choose to deploy all the available central procurement scenarios or only select ones. The central procurement scenarios available include requisition- ing, purchasing, sourcing, contracts, and analytics. The following sections detail further steps required for configuring individual scenarios, beginning with requisitioning, for SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition. For the most current setup doc- umentation for all available versions, including cloud versions, visit http://s-prs.co/ 500313. The steps for activating the SAP S/4HANA procurement hub after completing the gen- eral connectivity steps are as follows: 1. Log into the SAP S/4HANA hub system and execute Transaction SPRO. 2. Navigate to the Activate SAP S/4HANA Procurement Hub and Scenarios configura- tion activity. 3. In the Change View “Hub Activation” Overview screen, shown in Figure 14.31, choose New Entries and then check the Activate HUB checkbox. 4. Choose Save. Note that once saved, the SAP S/4HANA environment becomes a hub for central procurement. This step is a permanent step, so be sure that you have con- firmed the environment prior to saving. © 579 14.8 Configuring SAP Ariba Central Procurement, Private Cloud Edition Figure 14.31 Hub Activation The following sections describe how to activate and perform basic settings for the hub scenarios. sections.title: Summary
sections.en: 14.9 Summary SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition has evolved significantly since its inception, positioning itself as the future-proof platform for orchestrating procurement activities across diverse ERP systems. This evolution showcases not only advanced capa- bilities surpassing those of previous SAP SRM solutions but also ongoing efforts to enhance integration with SAP Ariba solutions or SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA, addressing process and functionality limitations. By adopting this robust solution, customers stand to gain a multitude of benefits. One of the primary advantages is the streamlining of procurement operations, result- ing in heightened efficiency and cost-effectiveness. Central procurement empowers organizations to centralize procurement activities, fostering transparency and simpli- fying complex procurement processes. Furthermore, the integration potential with SAP Ariba and SAP Business Network opens new avenues for collaboration and supplier management. This synergy allows companies to optimize supplier relationships, enhance supplier diversity, and imple- ment strategic sourcing initiatives. The result is a more agile and responsive procure- ment function, capable of adapting to changing market conditions and delivering exceptional value to customers. ©

sections.title: Spend Visibility
sections.en: 15.1 Spend Visibility Like finance and controlling, a procurement department has a strong focus on spend- ing. Unlike finance, the chief interests of which are cash flow and controlling costs, pro- curement seeks to understand what is being bought and whether more optimal approaches exist for categorizing and grouping this spend, as well as supporting it via Procurement Analytics Real-Time Reporting and Monitoring Spend Visibility Spend Reporting 15 Sourcing and Procurement Analytics 594 agreements with suppliers. Spend visibility, also called spend analysis, provides the procurement team with reporting in this area, combining financial/transactional reporting in which payments are being made to suppliers with the upstream areas, meaning the requisitioning, sourcing, and contracting areas of the transaction. The dif- ference between a classic approach to spend visibility and the approach in SAP S/4HANA is detailed in Figure 15.2. Figure 15.2 Classic versus SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement Spend Visibility In a classic approach for spend visibility, the SAP ERP system didn’t conduct an extraction in real time, and there were no KPI options. Because the data had been extracted to another environment, drilling down into the minutia of a transaction or supporting financials wasn’t always possible, either. For this, you had to return to the transaction system to further query data and/or rebuild your data cubes in your busi- ness warehouse to show the sought-after data. SAP S/4HANA still allows for extraction of data to a business warehouse if required, but you can also conduct KPI-based analy- sis in real time in the transacting system. This makes the view into your spending up to date and actionable in an immediate timeframe when required. With its multidimensional spend report, SAP S/4HANA Cloud offers further extensions for spend reporting in later releases. The multidimensional purchasing spend report in SAP S/4HANA Cloud allows for purchasing spend to be analyzed dynamically by com- pany code, region, plant, and other variables. The user can drag and drop dimensions, as well as change and adopt filters, dimensions, and measures in rows and columns. Users can flip between a table, bar, or split chart display. As with multidimensional spend reporting, users can also move between table, bar, or split chart displays for monitoring and reporting in SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procure- ment. Buyers and executives can analyze and report on spend, contracts, and suppliers, as well as monitor business-critical situations in the procurement overview page using analytical cards and worklists. Analytical cards are screen elements in an overview page. An overview page can show many charts and figures on one page, and the user can navi- gate to further applications by clicking the figures and/or charts contained in the card. Optional: Data extraction Classic SAP S/4HANA Traditional With SAP S/4HANA Process Excellence Data extraction SAP ERP SAP SRM SAP Business Warehouse SAP S/4HANA analytical apps Drill downs into documents Batch Job SAP S/4HANA Direct access SAP BW © 595 15.1 Spend Visibility The Procurement Overview Page app provides a graphical dashboard display of key procurement and supplier management reports, as in Figure 15.3. Figure 15.3 Procurement Overview Page App As of SAP S/4HANA 1909, you can also analyze the efficiency of your approval work- flows with the Purchase Requisition Average Approval Time (Flexible Workflow) app, using a KPI to monitor approval time for flexible workflow–based requisitions. You can also use the Purchase Order Item Changes app, which allows you analyze what types of changes are being made in the POs, as shown in Figure 15.4. This insight allows you to further optimize processes to address areas causing frequent updates to POs. Figure 15.4 Purchase Order Item Changes App 15 Sourcing and Procurement Analytics 596

sections.title: Contract Expiration
sections.en: 15.2 Contract Expiration The first step in the evolution of contract reporting is to get contracts out of filing cabi- nets and into the SAP S/4HANA system. Once contracts are in a system, instead of shuf- fling through paper files and hoping that you still have enough room and time on a contract to execute another purchase, you can begin to report on these contracts and identify ones that are expiring. Both the cloud and on-premise editions of SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement shipped with this functionality early on, via the Quantity Contract Consumption app. This app provides a comprehensive overview of all con- tracts in the system and all data related to them, such as validity timeframe, current released and target amounts, and material group. Another app is the Contract Expiry app, which shows the target value and consump- tion, providing a clear visual indicator of the amount left on a contract, as shown in Fig- ure 15.5. Figure 15.5 Contract Expiry App SAP S/4HANA has a mandate to raise process intelligence using its new, real-time reporting capabilities. The Quantity Contract Consumption app not only reports on existing expiration trajectories for contracts but also makes predictions using the pre- dictive analytics algorithm in the system. This algorithm leverages historical consump- tion data to make predictions about when a contract will be completely consumed. The algorithm’s predictive capability was further enhanced in SAP S/4HANA 1909 to include situational and contextual awareness capabilities, allowing the purchaser to start renewal negotiations at the optimal time and ensure that the purchaser also con- sumes the existing contract in the most efficient manner possible. To tune the default © 597

sections.title: Sourcing
sections.en: 15.3 Sourcing notifications on contract expirations, you access the Manage Situation Types app. This app notifies designated users of specific situations, such as contract expiry, for which follow-up is required. 15.3 Sourcing The sourcing cockpit and functionality in SAP S/4HANA remains similar to that in pre- vious versions of SAP ERP, and this is by design. For further innovation in sourcing top- ics, the go-to solution area is SAP Ariba. In SAP Ariba Strategic Sourcing Suite, the collaboration and reporting capabilities are more robust than in SAP S/4HANA. Still, if you’re evaluating sourcing from an existing supplier in SAP S/4HANA, you do have sev- eral supplier performance reports at your disposal, such as the following SAP S/4HANA apps:  Manage Sources of Supply  Operational Supplier Evaluation Last 365 Days  Overall Supplier Evaluation Last 365 Days  Supplier Evaluation by Quantity Last 365 Days  Supplier Evaluation by Price Last 365 Days  Supplier Evaluation by Time Last 365 Days  Supplier Evaluation by Questionnaire Last 365 Days Because these analytics and reports are being generated in real time in the transaction system, they also can be brought to bear on the transactions taking place. For example, in SAP S/4HANA Cloud, analytical information about the supplier is available at the transaction level. Rather than choosing a name and number for a supplier, by using simple product offerings to determine the supplier eligibility, this approach allows the user to look at the supplier’s record holistically and not just at a supplier record. This allows a user to choose a supplier with eyes wide open, rather than grabbing the first eligible supplier off the list. A user now sees scores and other data that differentiate suppliers and can drive purchasing patterns of the organization toward the best- performing suppliers rather than ones that managed to appear at the top of the list based on their name or numerical code. This new approach toward real-time purchasing analytics can be summarized at func- tionality, value-proposition, and capabilities levels:  Functionality When assigning a source of supply to an open purchase requisition in the Process Purchase Requisitions app, analytical information is embedded. The user can click the supplier record and review supplier details prior to assigning the supplier the business, as shown in Figure 15.6. 15 Sourcing and Procurement Analytics 598 Figure 15.6 Process Purchase Requisitions: Supplier Drill Down  Value proposition Provides the purchaser additional information (spend by supplier and supplier eval- uation score) about available sources of supply to support the decision, as shown in Figure 15.7. Figure 15.7 Spend Variance © 599

sections.title: Supplier Performance
sections.en: 15.4 Supplier Performance  Capabilities For each valid source of supply, SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement shows additional information via embedded analytics (price, evaluation score, and spend). As of SAP S/4HANA 1909, you can access additional analytics capabilities in the Request for Quotation Types app. Here you can leverage real-time analysis about sourcing events and compare different types of sourcing events, such as internal and external ones, as well as external price requests, as in Figure 15.8. Figure 15.8 RFQ Target Value and Types Both the guided sourcing capability for SAP Ariba Sourcing and the SAP Ariba Strategic Sourcing Suite solutions offer additional sourcing and reporting capabilities. The key difference between the two versions is that SAP Ariba Strategic Sourcing Suite offers support for direct materials sourcing and direct procurement document types, such as scheduling agreements. 15.4 Supplier Performance Suppliers can also be evaluated in real time, providing instant insight into performance issues or improvements. From these reports, a user can then drill further into individ- ual purchase orders and other documents, including surveys, to obtain a complete, real-time view. Figure 15.9 shows such a performance report for suppliers over time in the Operational Supplier Evaluation app. Suppliers with steep drop-offs in recent per- formance need to be analyzed further for financial difficulties and supply chain rele- vance, and transactions correspondingly must be moved to more reliable performers. 15 Sourcing and Procurement Analytics 600 Figure 15.9 Operational Supplier Evaluation Because these analytics capabilities are now available directly in the SAP S/4HANA environment, they can be embedded at the document level for additional insight at the time of a transaction. This is the subject of the following section.

sections.title: Purchasing Document Reports and Embedded Analytics
sections.en: 15.4.1 Purchasing Document Reports and Embedded Analytics Monitoring purchasing documents in the SAP Business Suite was done using SAP GUI transactions such as Transaction ME3L or ME4L, among others. With SAP S/4HANA, these legacy reports are transformed and harmonized using the SAP Fiori UX, with additional charts and visual filters to support the user in analyzing specific business sit- uations, such as overdue orders or next-scheduled items on a scheduling agreement. The user can navigate seamlessly from tables to object pages, or download a report to Excel. This embedded analytics approach extends to other transactions and documents in SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement, such as contracts. In the Monitor Purchase Contracts Items app, a user can navigate from line items in the contract to their release history and to an option to renew the contract. Without having to go into another app, the user can review the contract consumption and extend the validity or increase the value of the contract where required, as shown in Figure 15.10. In this app, a user also can see an overview of all of the contracts by spend type, select an individual contract to see how much remains of it, and then review consumption patterns over time to get an idea of fluctuations in spending on this contract. © 601 15.4 Supplier Performance Figure 15.10 Monitor Purchase Contract Items App You can also schedule a job and store supplier evaluation scores on a specific date for reporting purposes in the Supplier Evaluation Score History app, as shown in Figure 15.11. Figure 15.11 Supplier Evaluation Score History App In the Operational Supplier Evaluation KPI, there are two new views to visualize the top and bottom 10 suppliers and their corresponding purchase order net amounts.

sections.title: Predictive Analytics
sections.en: 15.4.2 Predictive Analytics As mentioned earlier in this chapter, contract reporting uses predictive analytics capa- bilities in recent releases of SAP S/4HANA. Predictive analytics is an exciting new area, combining traditional historical data and AI-driven, algorithm-based analysis to drive further accuracy in forecasting. 15 Sourcing and Procurement Analytics 602 In SAP S/4HANA Cloud and SAP S/4HANA, SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement reporting also boasts predictive capabilities on top of providing the historical report- ing, with capabilities to predict the following:  Purchase order spend based on open purchase requisitions  Predictive analytics for contract consumption  Delivery date for PO items The next section looks at other reporting apps available in SAP S/4HANA.

sections.title: Reporting
sections.en: 15.5 Reporting The UI platform for analytics and reporting in SAP S/4HANA is app-centric, with over- view apps such as the Purchasing Spend Dashboard providing a holistic overview for reporting, as shown in Figure 15.12. Figure 15.12 Purchasing Spend Dashboard This Purchasing Spend Dashboard app and others are typically displayed under Pur- chasing Analytics and Supplier Evaluation, as shown in Figure 15.13. These apps show actionable values on their respective tiles, whether for contract con- sumption, leakage, volumes, PO values, price variance, or order cycles. The user can set KPIs, and the apps refresh their data automatically. These analytics apps also can be refreshed manually without going into the app itself by clicking the Refresh icon in the lower-left-hand corner. Note that some measures appear in green and others in red. The red measures indicate that the KPI threshold set has been exceeded. A user thus is notified instantly in a simplified manner if something is going off target, without need- ing to enter the report itself. © 603 15.5 Reporting Figure 15.13 Purchasing Analytics and Supplier Evaluation SAP S/4HANA analytics and reporting apps extend the entire process flow for procure- to-pay. On the payment side, there are a comparable number of analytic options and reports, to provide accounts payable and invoice users with up-to-the-second insight into payables and cash flow position. There is a variety of analytic apps for use by accounts payable roles in the SAP S/4HANA system. These apps include the following:  Aging Analysis View payables across the organization by net due and overdue amounts  Overdue Payables Check overdue amounts to your suppliers by company code, supplier group, sup- plier, and reason for payment block  Future Payables Analyze payables for predefined due periods  Cash Discount Forecast Predicts all available cash discounts in the short-term future period  Cash Discount Utilization Allows for monitoring of cash discount utilization in real time  Days Payable Outstanding Provides information to analyze and understand the accounts payable key perfor- mance indicator (KPI)  Invoice Processing Analysis Reports on invoices processed in a period, such as the total number of posted invoices and posted line items  Supplier Payment Analysis (Manual and Automatic Payments) Used to get insight into payments made in the last 365 days  Supplier Payment Analysis (Open Payments) Used to get insight into open payments Accounts payable apps provide up-to-the-second information and analysis in a con- sumable format to optimize account payable’s understanding of key metrics and cash position. As with procurement apps, SAP S/4HANA boasts a wide array of analytics apps and approaches for AP that weren’t available, or in some cases even possible, in 15 Sourcing and Procurement Analytics 604 previous versions of SAP ERP. If a user requires an app that isn’t available as a standard part of SAP S/4HANA, there’s an option to build your own app or extend the existing standard ones. The next section looks at the generative artificial intelligence and machine learning functionality of SAP’s analytics apps.

sections.title: Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence
sections.en: 15.6 Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence As detailed in Chapter 5, augmented decision-making is the latest type of analytics tool- set to be provided in SAP S/4HANA. There are two types of machine learning apps and functionality currently available in SAP S/4HANA: embedded machine learning and side-by-side machine learning. Embedded ML leverages SAP Analytics Cloud and sup- ports more basic machine learning approaches, such as clustering, regression, classifi- cation, and time-series, whereas side-by-side ML leverages SAP BTP and supports more CPU-intensive processing for sophisticated modeling, deep learning, and image or lan- guage processing. The SAP framework enabling you manage lifecycle management in both of these ML approaches is called intelligent scenario lifecycle management. Intelligent scenario lifecycle management is a self-service tool for handling various operational require- ments of machine learning use cases. Intelligent scenario lifecycle management allows you to create, display, train, deploy, activate, and harvest inference results of machine learning/intelligent scenarios within the framework. The procurement machine learn- ing scenarios/functionality supported by the intelligent scenario lifecycle manage- ment framework as of SAP S/4HANA 2022 are listed in Table 15.1. Further scenarios that aren’t yet supported by the intelligent scenario lifecycle man- agement framework and the Intelligent Scenario Management app include reducing off-contract spend, material group proposals, catalog item proposals, and intelligent approval of purchase requisitions. Machine learning functionality is embedded in everyday SAP S/4HANA apps and func- tionality in sourcing and procurement, such as workflow approvals and estimating Scenario Intelligent Scenario Consumption Data for Slow or Non-Moving Materials MMSLO_CONSUMPTION_02 Stock Level Data for Slow or Non-Moving Materials MMSLO_STOCK_LEVEL_02 Predictive Scenario for Blocked Invoices with Quantity Vari- ance MMIV_INVC_QTY_BLCK Quantity Contract Consumption QTY_CONTRACT_CNSMPN Table 15.1 Intelligent Scenario Lifecycle Management-Supported Machine Learning Scenarios for Procurement © 605 15.6 Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence actual delivery times. For operational procurement, these additions include predicted delivery in the Monitor Purchase Order Items app. Here you can show orders that are likely to experience delays by using the Predicted Delivery field, as shown in Figure 15.14.
