sections.title: SAP Ariba Category Management
sections.en: 15.7 SAP Ariba Category Management Originally called material groups, SAP procurement solutions have focused on catego- rizing, grouping, and applying a strategic approach to acquiring key items for an orga- nization based on these categorizations. Categorization is essentially the grouping of similar products and services into a definition. In many procurement organizations, there is now a designated role or group tasked with managing the categories deemed essential to the organization. SAP Ariba Category Management allows a category manager to define a category profile, which may not be simply a product group in SAP S/4HANA but may span multiple, simi- lar product groups relevant for procurement. Once a category and grouping has been SAP AI Launchpad Operations Manager Main Tenant Namespace Workflow Templates Serving Templates Resource Group Namespace Workflows Model Servers SAP AI Launchpad Services AI API Connector SAP AI Launchpad SAP AI Core AI API Business App (with ILSM, for example) Git Repository Docker Repository Data Storage (Hyperscaler Object Stores) AI API Other AI Runtime © 607

sections.title: Configuration
sections.en: 15.8 Configuration defined, SAP Ariba Category Management provides guided, industry-standards-based strategy frameworks and recommendations. These identified opportunities can then be cascaded and monitored at a KPI level via SAP Ariba Category Management. Figure 15.17 provides an overview of SAP Ariba Category Management and its functionality. Figure 15.17 SAP Ariba Category Management Leveraging SAP Ariba Spend Analysis for enriched categorization spend data, SAP Ariba Category Management provides embedded analytics and visualization tools with view and multidimensional drilldown capabilities. Once the categories have been identified, SAP Ariba Category Management brings to bear segmentation, market dynamics, cost structure, SWOT analysis, risk assessment, and further tools and templates to identify goals and execute category strategies. SAP Ariba Category Management leverages the guided sourcing capability for SAP Ariba Sourcing, converting initiatives into sourcing projects or events. SAP Ariba Category Management includes a workbench with a plan- ning calendar, goal monitoring, and initiative status tracking to monitor the category strategy execution. The initiative status capabilities of SAP Ariba Category Manage- ment comprise system-based recommendations around tail spend, supplier fragmen- tation, price variances, and supplier diversity. SAP Ariba Category Management is uniquely suited for category management in sev- eral areas, with the key insights and functionality leveraging the breadth of SAP’s pro- curement portfolio, as well as SAP Business Network and its ecosystem for additional benchmarking and insights. 15.8 Configuration Analytics apps can be assigned in a dashboard form for a user or a general role that then gets assigned to a user group. Once this role is assigned, you then have several options E x e c u t e O p p r t u n i t i e s SAP Ariba Category Management Identify Value Levers Category Strategy Development Category Definition & Profiling Performance Management Savings & Benefits Tracking Trigger Sourcing Projects Initiate category-strategy-aware follow-on guided sourcing events based on identified initiatives Track spend, savings, and supplier optimization from the undertaken initiatives Manage performance against the plan’s investment, benefit target, schedule, and commitment Shortlist opportunities based on system recommendations Create category specific strategies through guided frameworks: Porters 5 Forces, Kraljic Matrix, and so on Create a category profile with segmentation: identify spend, suppliers, benchmarks, and cost drivers D e fi n e C a t e g o r y S t r a t e g y P i p l i n e T r a c k a n d M o n i t o r P e r f o r m a n c e 15 Sourcing and Procurement Analytics 608 for the reporting app for display and further analysis. The Legend button in analytics apps allows you to display or hide the legend. You can also zoom in and out and display the report in full-screen mode. This is especially useful when communicating reports during meetings, akin to putting a PowerPoint deck in display mode and removing the extraneous control icons to show the audience the essential report. You can also dis- play graphs as tables and export to Excel. The next sections outline how to create a key performance indicator, configure real- time reporting and queries, explore virtual data models, and integrate SAP S/4HANA and SAP Ariba, as well as further integration topics with other cloud applications such as SAP Fieldglass and SAP SuccessFactors.

sections.title: Creating a Key Performance Indicator
sections.en: 15.8.1 Creating a Key Performance Indicator You can set KPIs to allow dashboard tiles to visually alert business users that their KPI thresholds have been crossed (indicated with red). Green displays mean the KPI thresh- old hasn’t been crossed and the business metric/area is operating as per budget/plan. To set a KPI, you must have the analytics specialist role assigned. With this role, you now have multiple tiles available and corresponding options for working with KPIs. Using this role, complete the following steps to set up a KPI: 1. Create a KPI Define the data source and measure. 2. Create an evaluation Set evaluation criterion, prompt, values, and so on. 3. Create a tile Choose the drilldown type and catalog to be saved. 4. Configure a drilldown Set the dimensions/measures and visualization type.

sections.title: Configuring Real-Time Reporting/Queries
sections.en: 15.8.2 Configuring Real-Time Reporting/Queries There are a multitude of procurement-centric analytics apps available in stock SAP S/4HANA. There are also nonstandard, custom reports you can build, as well as other analytics tools in the deep and wide analytics tools portfolio from SAP that you can use for procurement reporting and analytics. There is also an SAP Fiori–based set of apps called report design modeler apps available in SAP S/4HANA Cloud. These apps allow users of SAP S/4HANA Cloud to create and manage reports. For SAP S/4HANA and SAP S/4HANA Cloud, there are two main types of users: key users, or IT users creating reports; and business users, who consume the reports. In some instances, business users also create the reports they’re consuming, thereby © 609 15.8 Configuration playing both roles. Key users aren’t quite technology users, but they aren’t business users either. Key users build reports for business users with various tools and may span multiple departments and divisions of business users with their reports and analysis. To build reports, key users leverage the tools outlined in the following sections.

sections.title: Exploring the Virtual Data Model and Core Data Services in SAP S/4HANA
sections.en: 15.8.3 Exploring the Virtual Data Model and Core Data Services in SAP S/4HANA SAP S/4HANA embedded analytics tools consume core data services (CDS) views, which comprise the virtual data model (VDM) of SAP S/4HANA. Analytic queries leverage the analytic engine, which must be set up as part of the overall enablement of the SAP S/4HANA environment. The analytic engine is used to evaluate and execute analytical queries. SAP Analytics Cloud sits external to SAP S/4HANA and allows you to create interactive dashboards for SAP S/4HANA. Here too, setup is required to connect the two environments. Figure 15.18 provides an overview of the SAP S/4HANA architecture, including the analytics-dependent areas such as CDS views and the intelligent scenario lifecycle management predictive engine supporting the machine learning apps and general analytics apps that leverage the analytics engine. Figure 15.18 SAP S/4HANA Architecture, Flow, and Integration Additional Reading For general information on analytics available in SAP S/4HANA, visit http://s-prs.co/ v500333. There are two SAP Fiori app browsers available for understanding and exploring the VDM and CDS views. The VDM is a structured representation of SAP S/4HANA database views. It follows consistent modeling rules and provides direct access to SAP data via SQL and OData requests. To take advantage of this shift, SAP has introduced CDS, a data-modeling architecture that allows database models to be defined and con- sumed at the database level instead of the app server level, taking advantage of SAP HANA’s speed. CDS views aren’t persistent; they are defined as the projection of other entities. The query browser is part of a toolset aimed at business users, and the view browser is part of the kit for key users. Drilling into the query browser shows possible fields for query and details for running a selected analytical query with SAP Lumira, designer edi- tion for multidimensional analysis. Once on the overview screen, you can select which query you want to review. On the detailed screen of the query, you can review the details of the selected analytic view, including its attributes and measures. The view browser shows input fields and output of CDS views and can display the data of the selected CDS views. SAP Lumira, designer edition is part of the View Browser app and supports analytic queries and multidimensional analysis. The Custom CDS Views app in Figure 15.19 allows you to take the following actions:  Display a list of all predelivered data sources and existing custom CDS views  Preview details of available data sources and custom CDS views  Create a CDS view Figure 15.19 Custom CDS Views App Similar to the Custom CDS Views app, you can also create custom analytical queries in the Custom Analytical Queries app, shown in Figure 15.20. In this app, you can take the following actions: © 611 15.8 Configuration  Create and manage analytical queries  Create calculated or restricted measures  Create additional parameters  Define which dimensions will be shown in rows and columns or as free dimensions Figure 15.20 Custom Analytical Queries App The reports can be viewed in the Analytics and Report Gallery app, shown in Figure 15.21. sections.title: Integration with Cloud Applications
sections.en: 15.8.5 Integration with Cloud Applications Especially for hybrid environments, in which you’re leveraging both SAP S/4HANA as the digital core and SAP Ariba and/or SAP Fieldglass to drive your procurement trans- formation, you’ll need to look at analytics and at where data is stored and analyzed. SAP Fieldglass SAP S/4HANA natively integrates with SAP Fieldglass. This integration can be activated via guided configuration; middleware is not required. If you do require mediated con- nectivity for technical or policy reasons, you can leverage SAP BTP to mediate the data transfers. Master data can be transferred, including purchasing organizations and SAP BusinessObjects Web Intelligence Key users and/or IT users leverage SAP BusinessObjects Web Intelligence to create reports using Query Panel and SAP BusinessObjects Web Intelligence document defini- tion for business user consumption. SAP Crystal Reports IT users leverage SAP Crystal Reports to create reports for business users. SAP Analytics Solution Description/Application Table 15.2 SAP BusinessObjects Tools for SAP S/4HANA Reporting and Analytics (Cont.) 15 Sourcing and Procurement Analytics 614 plants, as well as transactional data such as supplier-initiated invoices. As such, you can integrate and incorporate the supplier-initiated invoices in SAP Fieldglass into overall spend reporting and analysis apps found in the accounts payable and purchasing areas of SAP S/4HANA, outlined earlier in this chapter. SAP Ariba For SAP Ariba, you can integrate the spend management solutions bidirectionally, transferring data between SAP Ariba and SAP S/4HANA. The main mechanisms for this are as follows:  Direct connectivity or mediated connectivity with SAP. Here, you implement ABAP transports to send and receive SOAP-based data files directly to and from the SAP Ariba system. The mediated connectivity approach makes use of SAP Process Orchestration (SAP PO) to broker the transaction.  Manual import and export of files from the spend management UI. This approach entails identifying what data you wish to export from SAP Ariba, locating the source using SAP Ariba resources and documentation, and exporting and importing the data manually into SAP S/4HANA’s reporting tools and data structures.  Automated file transfer using the SAP Ariba data transfer tool. You can automate the transfer of CSV files between spend management and external systems. The data transfer tool includes a command-line utility that facilitates CSV transfer in batch mode to SAP S/4HANA, as well as a database connector, a command-line utility that connects the SAP Ariba data transfer tool with a JDBC-based ERP system.  Real-time transfer using SOAP APIs. You can create webservices to transfer data between systems using SOAP-based protocols. When deciding where to conduct an analysis, it helps to consolidate the data from all applicable transactions and systems. In the case of SAP Ariba, if your buyers are con- ducting most of their business in an SAP Ariba area, then it can make the most sense to extract SAP S/4HANA data and perform a comprehensive analysis in the cloud. Con- versely, if you’re running the procurement operations mostly in SAP S/4HANA, with some SAP Ariba solutions involved and SAP Fieldglass for contingent labor, it may make the most sense to bring the cloud data into SAP S/4HANA, then analyze it com- prehensively using the apps and extensibility on offer.

sections.title: Summary
sections.en: 15.9 Summary The apps-based approach of SAP Fiori in SAP S/4HANA, the topic of the next chapter, extends to analytics, as does the real-time, in-system processing of analytics and reporting in the transacting system. For SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement, there are extensive reporting and analytics apps on offer from the initial stage of the © 615 15.9 Summary process all the way through to accounts payable. SAP’s use of machine learning—and AI-powered predictive analytics and deep learning models can aid you in real time decision-making and automation during individual transactions—transactions such as supplier analysis predicting on-time delivery for an order, as well as comprehensive analysis, such as workflow analysis for the least risky approvals in an approver’s queue. Finally, users can extend their views and analysis via SAP BusinessObjects tools and integrated tools, as well as build customized reports. Integrated tools such as the Report Design Modeler apps in SAP S/4HANA Cloud, browsers, and customization options create a further platform from which to drive real-time insight and, ultimately, better performance in SAP S/4HANA analytics and reporting in general and in SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement in particular. Next, we’ll review SAP S/4HANA integration approaches with SAP Signavio, SAP Ariba, SAP Business Network, and SAP Fieldglass. © 617 Chapter 16 Integrating SAP S/4HANA with SAP Signavio, SAP Ariba, SAP Business Network, and SAP Fieldglass This chapter explains some of the core integration topics for SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement with SAP Ariba, SAP Business Network, and SAP Fieldglass solutions, as well as the business process management and optimization capabilities of SAP Signavio, providing approach overviews and process definitions. As discussed in previous chapters, SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement has expanding integration options with other SAP cloud solutions—SAP Ariba, SAP Busi- ness Network, and SAP Fieldglass in particular. Most SAP S/4HANA customers are deploying cloud solutions, whether public or private cloud editions, to support their digital core. Nonetheless, integrating further SAP cloud solutions into SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement, such as SAP Ariba, SAP Business Network, and SAP Fieldg- lass, still requires setup steps, mappings, and, in thankfully fewer and fewer cases, cus- tomizations/enhancements. For many processes and solution areas in SAP Ariba, financials and master data, such as supplier data, reside in the connected SAP S/4HANA digital core environment. SAP S/4HANA also relies on SAP Ariba, SAP Business Network, and SAP Fieldglass to address supplier collaboration and third-party service provider resource manage- ment. To make the handoffs and data updates seamless between the environments, there are multiple integration points and approaches. In addition to indirect procure- ment areas, SAP Business Network also supports direct procurement via SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration. Finally, in order to understand and further opti- mize your procurement processes, SAP has introduced SAP Signavio. This chapter outlines the various approaches and tools available for integrating SAP Ariba, SAP Business Network, and SAP Fieldglass with SAP S/4HANA, as well as the key procurement integration scenarios and processes applicable to SAP Signavio in these types of environments.

chapters.title: Integrating SAP S/4HANA with SAP Signavio, SAP Ariba, SAP Business Network, and SAP Fieldglass

sections.title: SAP Ariba and SAP Business Network Integration Projects and
sections.en: 16.1 SAP Ariba and SAP Business Network Integration Projects and Connectivity Options Every integration project is different. Like a fingerprint, no two customer datasets are the same. Each integration must take into account its customizations and unique cus- tomer landscape. SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement often will have built out procurement processes on the planned procurement side for direct procurement in manufacturing and production operations running in SAP S/4HANA. With regard to integration, many standard integrations are now native between SAP S/4HANA and SAP Ariba using prebuilt webservices, whereas others still require a build out using the core integration platforms and technologies available. The main integration solution is SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network, consolidating the previous options embodied by SAP Process Orchestration/SAP Pro- cess Integration (SAP PO/SAP PI), SAP Cloud Integration, and SAP Ariba Cloud Integra- tion Gateway. SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network is the platform-to-be for all future integration approaches and invest- ment at SAP, while SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway, SAP Cloud Integration, and SAP PO continue to be used at many organizations within the integration layer. Note Before embarking on an integration effort, visit the SAP Best Practices area for the lat- est SAP Ariba integration documentation by scenario and SAP Ariba solution, at http:// s-prs.co/500329. This URL takes you to all available integration packages for SAP Ariba. To visit the general SAP Best Practices area, go to https://me.sap.com/processnavigator. The general connectivity options between SAP S/4HANA and SAP Ariba focus on SAP Business Network and SAP Ariba Sourcing. Web service-based connections exist for the following:  SAP Ariba Strategic Sourcing Suite and guided sourcing capability for SAP Ariba Sourcing  Purchase order to invoice automation between SAP Business Network and SAP S/4HANA  SAP Pay and the discounting capability  SAP Ariba Buying for SAP S/4HANA In addition to integrating directly via web services, integration can also support medi- ation for the web service via cloud integration or SAP PO (SAP PI mediation is possible for on-premise implementations of SAP S/4HANA). The main supported documents are as follows:  RFQ and quote  Purchase order  Order confirmation  Advance ship notice © 619 16.1 SAP Ariba and SAP Business Network Integration Projects and Connectivity Options  Goods receipt notice  Supplier invoice  Invoice update  Payment proposal  Proposal acceptance  Remittance advice and update The data flows between SAP S/4HANA and SAP Business Network are thus bidirec- tional, whether underpinned via SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network, SAP Cloud Integration, SAP PI/SAP PO, or directly via web services connectivity. There are thus multiple integration scenarios applicable or tangential to the SAP S/4HANA to SAP Business Network integration topic. The deciding factors include the following:  Dominant system landscape Is the SAP S/4HANA environment on premise or in the cloud? What are the plans for transforming SAP S/4HANA to a cloud environment?  Prepackaged content availability What is the integration path requiring the least amount of custom work?  Total cost of ownership How much investment will be required to maintain the linkages and integrations going forward? Are there additional upgrades in either SAP Business Network or SAP S/4HANA that can impact the integration and require rework?  Go-live timelines Which approach will yield the quickest integration?  Connectivity options Are there firewall constraints, or a lack thereof, which can influence or impact the options available? A thorough analysis of the processes/solution areas you wish to integrate between SAP Ariba/SAP Business Network and SAP S/4HANA also should be conducted. There are three core solution areas in particular to evaluate. First is the PO/invoicing automation with SAP S/4HANA and SAP Business Network. This scenario is the most common and can yield immediate results and ROI, as transactions are issued out of SAP S/4HANA and processed in SAP Business Network, then finally sent back to SAP S/4HANA. The second integration area is SAP Ariba Strategic Sourcing Suite connected to SAP S/4HANA. If something needs to be sourced during a transaction in SAP S/4HANA, you can leverage the rich sourcing functionality in SAP Ariba Strategic Sourcing Suite to find the optimal supplier(s) and then revert the item back to SAP S/4HANA for concluding the transaction (or convert to a purchase order in SAP Ariba, depending on your process). Finally, for direct procurement scenarios between SAP S/4HANA and SAP Business Net- work, you have SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration, which has addi- tional integration requirements. Regarding the integration team itself, to underpin a successful implementation, a strong integration lead is required. The integration lead role requires a consultant or 16 Integrating SAP S/4HANA with SAP Signavio, SAP Ariba, SAP Business Network, and SAP Fieldglass 620 subject matter expert with a solid understanding of the master data and transactional integration points and methods, as well as the vernacular of both SAP S/4HANA (ABAP, master data, transaction codes, tables) and SAP Ariba/SAP Business Network (including topics such as SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network, commerce automation, SAP Ariba Strategic Sourcing Suite, SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing, SAP Ariba Buying for SAP S/4HANA, SAP Ariba Catalog, SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration, and SAP Business Network). Often an SAP customer will assume that the integration with SAP S/4HANA is included in SAP Business Network’s subscription or that it will be handled as part of the delivery of SAP Business Network. Rather than assuming and hoping that the integration will fall into place, this area needs to be defined, scoped, and understood by all of the project partic- ipants. Even with a standard, native integration between SAP S/4HANA and SAP Ariba, SAP Business Network, or SAP Fieldglass, the customer data fingerprint may be unique enough to require further integration. The project should eventually reach a cutover stage, in which the newly built integra- tions are moved to production. Here, a clear strategy for the impacted legacy systems, such as SAP SRM, is required to minimize business disruptions. A poorly planned strat- egy, or not having a cutover strategy altogether, can cause significant issues on an SAP Ariba/SAP Business Network integration project, especially a project impacting finan- cials. Some other common issues affecting integration projects include the following:  Understaffed project teams.  Not budgeting adequate resources for both the project team and the customer’s IT department (ABAP developers, SAP PI experts, and Basis team members are key par- ticipants to have on board).  Taking shortcuts and hoping SAP Ariba Customer Support or SAP Preferred Care for SAP Ariba solutions will bail out the project if there are integration difficulties will likely cause delays and frustration.  Not being on the latest SAP Integration Suite or hotfix release. Not being on the lat- est hotfix release can cause delays when attempting to resolve an error with SAP Support. SAP Support expects your organization to be on the latest hotfix release. Perhaps the most popular integration between SAP Business Network and an SAP S/4HANA environment is for purchasing document exchanges between SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement and SAP Business Network, as discussed in the next section.

sections.title: SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend
sections.en: 16.2 SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network The tradition of ERP integration continues with the latest, most comprehensive inte- gration platform, called SAP Integration Suite. You can download SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network via SAP Service © 621 16.2 SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Marketplace as an add-on at service.sap.com. Even prior to being acquired by SAP, SAP Ariba had long been integrating agnostically with backend ERP systems. Post acquisi- tion, SAP used to refer the integration between SAP Ariba and the backend ERP envi- ronments as the Cloud Integration Platform. Then SAP changed the solution name to SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway. Finally, SAP has landed on the name SAP Integra- tion Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. Irre- spective of the long naming convention, standard documentation and bug fixes are still delivered via SAP Notes at support.sap.com. SAP Integration Suite, managed gate- way for spend management and SAP Business Network provides self-service tools to quickly configure, test, and extend processes; incorporate automated upgrades via Software Update Manager; and monitor with tools such as SAP Solution Manager to provide an integration solution that fits seamlessly in your SAP landscape, thus mini- mizing TCO expenses and ensuring a smooth transaction flow. Many of the linkages are also built out directly in SAP S/4HANA. Depending on your approach and requirements, there are numerous options available. The latest and future go-to integration approach for SAP Ariba is SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network, as illustrated in Figure 16.1. Figure 16.1 SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Busi- ness Network SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Net- work provides a fast, flexible solution to integrate with backend systems, trading part- ners, and SAP Ariba solutions. There are three main areas in SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend man- agement and SAP Business Network: the backend SAP S/4HANA area, the integration layer, and the SAP Ariba cloud solutions area. SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway Add-On for ERP SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway Add-On for ERP • Add-on configuration • Enhanced API • Managing customization • Monitoring HTTPS SAP Cloud Connector Middleware • SAP Cloud Platform (messaging, data mapping, and transformation • SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway user interface (configuration wizard mapping repository test central, monitoring) • SAP Ariba Commerce Automation • Ariba Network • SAP Ariba Supply Chain Collaboration for Buyers • SAP Ariba Payables • SAP Ariba Discounting • SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing • SAP Ariba Sourcing • SAP Ariba Contracts SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway SAP Ariba Solutions 16 Integrating SAP S/4HANA with SAP Signavio, SAP Ariba, SAP Business Network, and SAP Fieldglass 622 On the SAP Ariba solutions side, once you’ve enabled SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network as an admin and an end point, you can push as well as pull data from the backend systems, leveraging asyn- chronous webservices and enhanced message contents to avoid having to look up a message in SAP. Setting up SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network entails three steps. First, you configure the buy-side account for SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network and install and configure the integration add-on for SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA. Next, you extend it using the extension framework in the add-on interfaces in SAP; the cus- tom eXtensible Stylesheet Language Transformations (XSLTs) can be used for addi- tional data mapping. Finally, you test the integration using the predefined scripts and any customized test cases required.

sections.en: 16.2.1 Configuring SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Manage- ment and SAP Business Network The technical and scenario configuration can be accessed in SAP S/4HANA via Transac- tion SPRO under Integration with Other SAP Components  SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway  Global Settings for the technical configuration and Integration with Other mySAP Components  Ariba Cloud Integration  Ariba Network Integration for scenario configuration, as in Figure 16.2. sections.title: SAP Ariba Strategic Sourcing Suite Integration
sections.en: 16.2.2 SAP Ariba Strategic Sourcing Suite Integration A key integration option for customers running SAP S/4HANA and looking to take advantage of SAP Ariba cloud solutions to bolster their procurement operations is SAP Ariba Strategic Sourcing Suite integration. Here, a user can generate a request for a quo- tation, information, purchase, or other solicitation type (collectively called RFx) and send this RFx for sourcing in the SAP Ariba Strategic Sourcing Suite tool. SAP Ariba Stra- tegic Sourcing Suite enables the customer suppliers on SAP Business Network to seam- lessly collaborate on bidding and identifying the best option for the customer’s needs, and then allows for ordering and fulfillment of the item to occur within the SAP ERP and/or SAP Ariba environment. SAP Ariba provides the crucial linkage to and media- tion with a huge array of suppliers during this process, which an ERP-based sourcing event would not be able to replicate easily alone, as connecting to suppliers and setting up protocols is simply too laborious to scale. The integration connects the digital core of SAP S/4HANA with SAP Ariba Strategic Sourcing Suite, with the following key process steps (see Figure 16.3): 1. The purchaser creates an RFQ for SAP S/4HANA purchase requisitions and automat- ically sends this RFQ to SAP Ariba Strategic Sourcing Suite, triggering a sourcing request. 2. The sourcing manager in SAP Ariba Strategic Sourcing Suite accesses their worklist and converts sourcing requests into sourcing projects, inviting suppliers to bid. 3. Suppliers process the RFQ. Figure 16.3 Digital Core SAP S/4HANA to SAP Ariba Strategic Sourcing Suite to SAP Business Network and Back Purchase Requisition Initiate Sourcing Project Create RFQ or Auction Receive Supplier Response Award-Winning Response Sourcing Completed SAP Business Network Role: Supplier SAP Ariba Collaborative Sourcing Role: Purchaser SAP S/4HANA Role: Purchaser Request for Quotation Create Purchase Order Receive Award Receive RFQ or Auction Notification Create Supplier Notification 16 Integrating SAP S/4HANA with SAP Signavio, SAP Ariba, SAP Business Network, and SAP Fieldglass 624 4. The sourcing manager can then monitor sourcing projects and supplier responses, as well as support projects that result in (reverse) auctions or requests for quota- tions, by adding suppliers to SAP Business Network as required. 5. Finally, once the sourcing process is complete, the sourcing manager can award one or more bids in SAP Ariba Strategic Sourcing Suite. These awarded bids are sent auto- matically or directly by the sourcing manager to SAP S/4HANA, where purchase orders and/or contracts are created as follow-on documents for the original RFQ. From a scenario standpoint, the initiating steps occur in SAP S/4HANA. The prerequisites for starting the SAP Ariba Strategic Sourcing Suite integration steps in SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network are as follows: 1. You must have an enabled SAP Ariba Strategic Sourcing Suite realm connected to an active buyer account and valid trading buyer/supplier relationship on SAP Business Network. 2. A buyer account must have access to SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network and be set up to send documents back and forth from SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend manage- ment and SAP Business Network. 3. You need access to SAP Marketplace to download the SAP Integration Suite, man- aged gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network add-on for SAP S/4HANA. 4. Certificates and add-ons must be configured in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. 5. A sourcing realm needs to be added to a buyer organization under Feature Availabil- ity by SAP Ariba Customer Support. Note For SAP Ariba Strategic Sourcing Suite integration, you only need to enable SAP Integra- tion Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network through the SAP Ariba Strategic Sourcing Suite realm. For transactions such as quote requests, awards, and contracts, you need to enable SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network from SAP Business Net- work as well. To initiate this scenario, a buyer logs into SAP S/4HANA and creates an RFP, either directly or by referencing an open requisition, as shown in Figure 16.4. You can verify on the Output Details tab that the RFP is being sent to SAP Ariba for the sourcing event, as shown in Figure 16.5. When a buyer logs into SAP Ariba Sourcing, the first area they see is their dashboard, as shown in Figure 16.6. © 625 16.2 SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Figure 16.4 Create RFP in SAP S/4HANA Figure 16.5 Output Details in SAP S/4HANA RFP Figure 16.6 Buyer Dashboard in Guided Sourcing Capability for SAP Ariba Sourcing 16 Integrating SAP S/4HANA with SAP Signavio, SAP Ariba, SAP Business Network, and SAP Fieldglass 626 From the dashboard, the buyer can then search for the RFP, as shown in Figure 16.7. Figure 16.7 Search for RFP in Guided Sourcing Capability for SAP Ariba Sourcing Two actions need to be completed prior to issuing the RFP. The first is preparing the RFP for issuing, and the second is an approval step. You access these steps under Tasks, as shown in Figure 16.8: 1. In selecting the first task for preparing the sourcing of the request, you mark this step as complete once you’ve reviewed it. There is also the option to mark this as started as an interim status. Once you’ve reviewed the two steps and the approvals are completed, your RFP is ready to be converted to an SAP Ariba Sourcing RFP, as shown in Figure 16.8. Figure 16.8 Guided Sourcing Capability for SAP Ariba Sourcing: Tasks 2. With the tasks complete, you then select Create and convert the sourcing request as an SAP Ariba Sourcing RFP. 3. Once the tasks are completed, you create a sourcing project as in Figure 16.9. 4. The next step is to add bidders to the RFP event, as shown in Figure 16.10. 5. During these steps for creating an RFP, you also can define and refine the team and the content, finally arriving at the summary page, as shown in Figure 16.11. © 627 16.2 SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Figure 16.9 Create Guided Sourcing Capability for SAP Ariba Sourcing Project Figure 16.10 Adding Bidders Figure 16.11 Publish RFP 16 Integrating SAP S/4HANA with SAP Signavio, SAP Ariba, SAP Business Network, and SAP Fieldglass 628 6. Once you’ve published the RFP, you can monitor the event as in Figure 16.12, and suppliers can review the request in SAP Business Network under Proposals and Questionnaires. Figure 16.12 Event Monitor in SAP Ariba Buying for SAP S/4HANA 7. The invited supplier is able to review the RFP by logging into their supplier portal on SAP Business Network at supplier.ariba.com. In Ariba Proposals and Questionnaires, a supplier has a dropdown menu that includes their proposals, as shown in Figure 16.13. Figure 16.13 Ariba Proposals and Questionnaires Section: Suppliers 8. Drilling into the RFP event, the supplier can review the information as shown in Fig- ure 16.14. 9. The Proposals section lists the bids in the Completed, Pending Selection (where the sup- plier has already put in a bid), and Preview (new RFxs) statuses, as shown in Figure 16.15. © 629 16.2 SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Figure 16.14 Event Details: RFP Figure 16.15 SAP Ariba Supplier Bidding 10. Once the supplier has selected and opened the invitation, the supplier can either decline to participate or review the prerequisites and accept them. In Figure 16.16, the supplier selects the line items they wish to bid upon. Figure 16.16 Supplier Selecting Lots/Line Items 16 Integrating SAP S/4HANA with SAP Signavio, SAP Ariba, SAP Business Network, and SAP Fieldglass 630 11. This allows the supplier to select some or all of the items requested in the RFx and respond as shown in Figure 16.17. During the response, the supplier can also send a message to the customer (see Figure 16.18). Figure 16.17 Select Lots Figure 16.18 Supplier Submits Bid 12. Next, the buyer reviews the bids as in Figure 16.19. The buyer then consolidates and compares the bids, selecting, presumably, the best bid that meets their target goals for quality, timing, and price. As shown in Figure 16.20, it is possible to compare the bids side by side. You can completely or partially award an RFx to a supplier, depending upon what is optimal/preferred. This means a supplier could receive a © 631 16.2 SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network partial award of the tender, while another supplier could receive the rest of the order. Figure 16.19 Buyer Bid Comparison in Guided Sourcing Capability for SAP Ariba Sourcing Figure 16.20 Award-Winning Bid 13. In Figure 16.20, you confirm the award(s) for the RFx prior to generating them in the backend SAP S/4HANA environment in Figure 16.21. 16 Integrating SAP S/4HANA with SAP Signavio, SAP Ariba, SAP Business Network, and SAP Fieldglass 632 Figure 16.21 Bid Awarded Once the bid is awarded, you can generate purchase orders referencing the terms and pric- ing agreed to in the RFx and issue the purchase orders from SAP S/4HANA as in Figure 16.22. Figure 16.22 Backend Document Created in SAP S/4HANA from Guided Sourcing Capability for SAP Ariba Sourcing Event Depending on the scenario and customer preference, integrating SAP S/4HANA and SAP Ariba Sourcing enables you to address sourcing requirements originating in SAP ERP, with a much larger array of suppliers and functionality than is available in SAP © 633 16.2 SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network S/4HANA by itself. Many times, a single successful sourcing event can deliver substan- tial savings to the bottom line of an organization. Integrating SAP S/4HANA with SAP Ariba Sourcing greatly increases the odds of this type of sourcing success occurring.

sections.title: SAP Business Network Commerce Automation
sections.en: 16.2.3 SAP Business Network Commerce Automation In a hybrid procurement environment, where purchasing processes take place in both SAP S/4HANA and SAP Ariba solutions, operational procurement can span both sys- tems. A typical set of steps for an SAP S/4HANA–based requisition or PO moving to SAP Business Network and back is called commerce automation. The steps for converting a purchase order to an invoice while leveraging both systems and both the buyer and the supplier using SAP S/4HANA and SAP Business Network, respectively, follows ahead. The buyer (either a professional buyer or a casual user) creates a purchase order in SAP S/4HANA. Here, in Figure 16.23, the buyer creates a service purchase order. Figure 16.23 Purchase Order Create Advanced Then the buyer can describe the item, select a material/service master, or shop in a cat- alog. Here, the buyer enters a service PO for repairing a motor. SAP S/4HANA can be configured to automatically convert sourced requisitions to pur- chase orders, or a buyer can create a PO directly using the app. The purchase order is then transmitted to SAP Business Network for processing by the supplier. Now that the document is up in SAP Business Network, it’s time for the supplier to begin collaboration with the customer, reviewing and processing the purchase order. The supplier logs in to SAP Business Network using their login information and reviews the PO as shown in Figure 16.24. The Activity Feed area in Figure 16.24 reveals the PO has arrived in the supplier’s docu- ments, and the supplier can drill into it further by clicking the document. Once the sup- plier reviews, she confirms receipt of the purchase order as in Figure 16.25. 16 Integrating SAP S/4HANA with SAP Signavio, SAP Ariba, SAP Business Network, and SAP Fieldglass 634 The supplier has confirmed the PO and now sets about delivering the services. Once the service has been delivered, the supplier updates the customer by creating a service sheet as in Figure 16.26. Figure 16.24 SAP Business Network: Supplier Dashboard Figure 16.25 Confirming PO in SAP Business Network as Supplier Figure 16.26 Supplier Creates Service Sheet in SAP Business Network © 635 16.2 SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network This service sheet updates from SAP Business Network into the SAP S/4HANA environ- ment to the Purchase Order History tab directly, as shown in Figure 16.27. Figure 16.27 Purchase Order History Tab in SAP S/4HANA The buyer can then review this service sheet in SAP S/4HANA by clicking the link pro- vided in the Purchase Order History tab, as shown in Figure 16.28. Figure 16.28 Service Details The buyer can then accept or reject the service sheet. In Figure 16.29, the status moves to Will Be Accepted after the buyer confirms, and then to green (Accepted), shown in Figure 16.30, once saved. 16 Integrating SAP S/4HANA with SAP Signavio, SAP Ariba, SAP Business Network, and SAP Fieldglass 636 Figure 16.29 Accepted Service Entry Sheet Figure 16.30 Service Entry Sheet Accepted in SAP S/4HANA by Buyer This updates the purchase order in SAP S/4HANA with the additional service entry sheet document as in Figure 16.31. © 637 16.2 SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Figure 16.31 Service Entry Sheet Document Updates PO History The supplier in SAP Business Network now has the option to create an invoice for ser- vices rendered, as in Figure 16.32. Figure 16.32 Supplier Creates Invoice The supplier creates and submits the invoice on SAP Business Network, as shown in Fig- ure 16.33 and Figure 16.34 respectively. 16 Integrating SAP S/4HANA with SAP Signavio, SAP Ariba, SAP Business Network, and SAP Fieldglass 638 Figure 16.33 Invoice Creation in SAP Business Network Figure 16.34 Invoice Submitted Once these steps are complete, an invoice transmits back to SAP S/4HANA for reconcil- iation and can be matched against not only the PO, but also the service entry sheet, as shown in Figure 16.35. This is called a three-way match, which is more solid than relying on just the PO and the invoice (a two-way match). Finally, the buyer can see all three documents, the confir- mation/goods receipt, the service entry sheet, and the invoice, in the Purchase Order History tab, as shown in Figure 16.36 . Invoices created in a supplier’s system—or worse, written out on paper and faxed over to the customer—create all kinds of processing challenges for the customer. By using SAP Business Network to submit an invoice and other documents, the supplier and cus- tomer save valuable iterations in this process, outlined ahead, making the submission much more accurate and the processing cycles faster. © 639 16.2 SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Figure 16.35 Invoice in SAP S/4HANA Figure 16.36 Purchase Order History Tab with Confirmation/Goods Receipt, Service Entry Sheet, and Invoice The next section focuses on SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration, another native integration available in SAP S/4HANA. 16 Integrating SAP S/4HANA with SAP Signavio, SAP Ariba, SAP Business Network, and SAP Fieldglass 640

sections.title: SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration
sections.en: 16.3 SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration offers enhanced visibility and effi- ciency for direct material/merchandise/supply chain collaboration in SAP Business Network. Direct procurement is driven from multiple SAP S/4HANA areas and is typi- cally used to manage and control manufacturing, sales and distribution, production planning, and the ever-present financial aspects. However, direct procurement bene- fits as much from collaboration with suppliers as these other areas, if not more. This supplier collaboration is supported in multiple areas of SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration. In the following sections, we’ll look at the functionality of this solution and then how to configure it.

sections.title: Product Functionality
sections.en: 16.3.1 Product Functionality SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration connects SAP S/4HANA processes and scenarios in direct procurement and integrated business planning with SAP Busi- ness Network and its multitude of suppliers for collaboration, as shown in Figure 16.37. Figure 16.37 SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration comprises the direct processes of source-to-contract, planning, buy and make, and invoice-to-pay. In each instance, SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration and the corresponding area in SAP S/4HANA combine to provide complete coverage of the process, as detailed in Figure 16.38. In most instances, the demand originates and then is sourced or acquired in SAP Busi- ness Network Supply Chain Collaboration, returning then to SAP S/4HANA for receipt and further processing/usage within the production process. Forecast/Demand SMI Demand/Inventory Purchase Order Component Ship Notice Goods Receipt Notice Consignment Inventory Self-Billing/ERS InSvtaotiuces Payment Quality Notification Quality Inspection Request Quality Review/Batch Record Quality Notification Invoice Advance Ship Notice Manufacturing Visibility Component Consumption Component Receipt Notice PO Confirmation SMI Planned Shipments Forecast/Upside Commit Quality Inspection Response Quality Review/Batch Record Schedule Agreement Release Forecast Supplier-Managed Inventory Order Discrete Subcontract Consignment Scheduling Agreement Quality Supplier/Contract Manufacturer Buyer/Planner © 641 16.3 SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration Figure 16.38 SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration Process Coverage The processes covered between the buyer and supplier under SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration fall into three categories: planning, buy and make, and invoice/payment processes. Viewed another way, SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration’s capabilities are clustered in planning, execution, and quality. In planning, SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration provides forecast and inventory collaboration. In supply chain execution, the supplier and buyer use SAP Business Network Supply Chain Col- laboration to collaborate on direct items and services, multitier items and services, scheduling agreements, and subcontracting and consignment orders. In quality man- agement, suppliers and buyers leverage SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collabora- tion for notifications, inspections, reviews, and certificates. Supply chains in manufacturing are particularly complex. Whether a high-tech manu- facturer or a life sciences one, each industry has its own nuances and overlay processes, with a core need for collaboration between suppliers and buyers throughout. Here the buyer is a manufacturer, and the supplier can be a raw materials supplier, a third-party logistics provider, a subassembly supplier, a contract manufacturer, or a component supplier. SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration provides manufacturers and their supply chain stakeholders with the following:  Collaboration simplicity with a single business network  Embedded supplier onboarding services  End-to-end process orchestration across all supplier channels to validate and enforce compliance  Network intelligence, data, and insights to reduce supply chain risk Table 16.1 outlines the functionality added in SAP Business Network Supply Chain Col- laboration to support the direct procurement processes through SAP Business Network and back. SAP Ariba Strategic Sourcing Suite SAP IBP SAP PLM APS SAP ERP ERP SAP S/4HANA Supplier and risk management Contract Source Design Make Order Request Pay Manage Receive Commit Forecast Plan Source and contract Buy and make Invoice and pay Speed time to market, lower cost of goods sold, avoid supply chain disruptions SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration 16 Integrating SAP S/4HANA with SAP Signavio, SAP Ariba, SAP Business Network, and SAP Fieldglass 642 To keep documents consistent between SAP Supply Network Collaboration and SAP Business Network, you must perform the business processes for purchase orders and ship notices through the SAP Business Network user interface exclusively, and not through the SAP Supply Network Collaboration application. Not all functions available in supplier collaboration are supported by SAP Supply Net- work Collaboration integration with SAP Business Network. Table 16.2 shows the five functions supported and their related SAP Supply Network Collaboration components and starting screens. SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration Function Description Forecast The forecast collaboration component aims to avoid supply shortfalls and reduces and optimizes supply chain stock lev- els. It compares and displays the buyer’s firm or planned net demands and the supplier’s firm or planned receipts. The buyer and supplier have the same view of the planning situa- tion and can quickly obtain a quick overview of critical situa- tions. This functionality is integrated with SAP Integrated Business Planning (SAP IBP). Work order The work order collaboration component provides a consoli- dated view of the production demands and the current pro- duction progress. It offers customers early insight into changes affecting shipping dates and final quantity. Replenishment The replenishment collaboration component offers suppliers a value-added service by performing the replenishment planning task for their business partners. By increasing visi- bility into actual consumer demand, as well as customer inventory levels, suppliers can make better decisions on how to distribute goods across various customers, which in turn leads to increased customer service levels, lower transporta- tion costs, reduced inventory, and lower sales cost. Inventory The inventory collaboration component ensures greater visi- bility of the inventory, as well as the supply-and-demand planning situation in a cross-tier environment. Quality Suppliers and customers can use the new quality collabora- tion component to notify each other of quality problems (or other issues with products or subcontracting components) during the manufacturing process, or after delivery, so that the customer or supplier can quickly react to the complaint. Table 16.1 SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration Functionality © 643 16.3 SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration includes several features and func- tions crucial to many direct procurement processes. Buyers and suppliers have access to many direct, specific processes and fields for ship notices, scheduling agreements, and order collaboration. As part of the SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration setup process, suppli- ers need to be enabled via an adapter in SAP Integration Suite as a prerequisite to sup- port the collaboration processes. This is coordinated via the supplier enablement service. The steps for deploying the SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration exten- sion start with the buyer: 1. The buyer enables the supplier for particular SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration features. 2. Fields of data supporting enhanced functionality, such as the ordering of direct materials, are passed from the buyer’s SAP S/4HANA system to SAP Business Net- work. 3. Through an enhanced SAP Business Network user interface, the enabled supplier makes use of the additional fields and enhanced functionality to collaborate with the buyer on documents such as purchase orders, invoices, and ship notices. To prepare a supplier record in SAP S/4HANA for SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration activities, a relationship flag must be set. This functionality is standard and doesn’t require additional installation or configuration. Once the flag is set, industry- specific functionality can be configured. To complete both these activities, your user role must have supplier enablement task management permissions. Buyers do not require further enablement for SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration. As an admin- istrator, you can disable SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration functionality for suppliers. Integration Function Component Starting Screen Forecast Demand Order Forecast Monitor Replenishment Replenishment Replenishment VMI Monitor Work Order Work Order Collaboration Work Order List Inventory Supply Network Inventory Supply Network Inventory Quality Quality Collaboration Quality Notification Overview Table 16.2 Comparison Table: SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration Functions with SAP Supply Network Collaboration 16 Integrating SAP S/4HANA with SAP Signavio, SAP Ariba, SAP Business Network, and SAP Fieldglass 644 Once a supplier has been appropriately flagged, they can be directed to the SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration supplier user interface portal. This portal contains all existing SAP Business Network supplier functionality, plus SAP Business Network Sup- ply Chain Collaboration and industry-specific SAP Business Network Supply Chain Col- laboration functionality. When suppliers are enabled for SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration, they are directed to the supplier portal, where they can access the various SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration features. Previously, the sup- plier portal was referred to as the Supply Chain Management (SCM) portal. Suppliers and buyers often collaborate on the creation of purchase orders, invoices, and ship notices for direct material orders. This collaboration requires the exchange of information specific to direct material orders. These features facilitate the collabora- tion process by allowing more detailed descriptions of materials being procured. These features also allow the supplier to collaborate through the SAP Business Network user interface. This is particularly helpful for suppliers that do not have EDI, cXML, or other integrated business-to-business mechanisms in place. Direct material fields for order and invoice collaboration facilitate the collaboration process for purchase orders, invoices, and ship notices by allowing for more detailed descriptions of materials being procured. This SAP Business Network feature is applica- ble to all supplier users. The buyer’s industry type needs to be set as retail to enable this functionality. The ship notice business rules feature for order confirmation and ship notice rules sup- ports the direct material collaboration process. This SAP Business Network feature is applicable to all supplier users. Direct material includes all items, such as raw materials and parts, required to assemble or manufacture a complete product. A rule may be implemented based on customer and market requirements or may be driven by indi- vidual needs. A rule can be applied to many suppliers or to a predefined group of sup- pliers (even if the group only contains one member). Tooltips in the user interface indicate when ship notice rules have been enabled. Scheduling agreement releases are visible in the SAP Business Network user interface. Buyers can periodically communicate releases to their suppliers, and suppliers can cre- ate ship notices for materials requested through scheduling agreement releases. From the new Items to Ship tab, a supplier can create a single ship notice containing items from several purchase orders that all are due by the same date. It is important to note that scheduling agreement releases do not support order confir- mations or most invoices. You cannot use scheduling agreement release collaboration for invoices, except for invoices that have been created as carbon copies by direct mate- rial buyers. Also, you cannot use scheduling agreement releases for order confirma- tions. The processing of nonscheduled items is not affected by scheduling agreement releases. These are not restrictions of SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collabora- tion so much as general restrictions in the scheduling agreement process. © 645 16.3 SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration Scheduling agreement release collaboration is disabled by default, but the buyer can enable it by following these steps: 1. Log on as a buyer. 2. Click Manage Profile. 3. On the Configuration page, click Default Transaction Rules. 4. Under Scheduling Agreement Release Setup Rules, check the box next to Allow Scheduling Agreement Release Collaboration. Suppliers view scheduling agreement releases in the list of documents on the Orders and Releases tab and can choose whether to search for only scheduling agreement releases. Suppliers can then create ship notices from scheduling agreement releases. To support these new functionalities, the following types of messages have been enhanced or added for direct materials buyers and contract manufacturers:  Subcontracting purchase order A subcontracting purchase order is a purchase order that is sent from a buyer to a contract manufacturer to request the production and delivery of finished goods. The subcontracting purchase order has been enhanced to carry not only item level and schedule line level information, but also subcontracting component informa- tion. Subcontracting components are the raw materials that are used for manufac- turing the finished goods specified at the item level.  Component ship notice A component ship notice is a type of ship notice that informs the contract man- ufacturer of the shipment of subcontracting components.  Component receipt A component receipt is a type of goods receipt that informs the buyer of the receipt of subcontracting components. The contract manufacturer can issue the compo- nent receipt against one or more component ship notices.  Component consumption (backflush) message The ship notice message has been enhanced to include consumption details in a back- flush component message. A backflush component consumption message is a type of ship notice request that informs the buyer of the completion of finished goods from subcontracting components. Unlike real-time component consumption reporting, backflush reporting is done only once, at the end of the production process.  Component consumption (real-time) message A real-time component consumption message informs the buyer of consumption of components at any phase of the production cycle.  Component inventory message A component inventory message has been added to inform suppliers about quanti- ties of components available for manufacturing. 16 Integrating SAP S/4HANA with SAP Signavio, SAP Ariba, SAP Business Network, and SAP Fieldglass 646  SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration limitation If a subcontracting purchase order has been uploaded or downloaded via a CSV file, a supplier will not see the component level on the downloaded subcontracting pur- chase order.

sections.title: Configuration
sections.en: 16.3.2 Configuration To establish basic connectivity between the SAP S/4HANA environment and SAP Busi- ness Network Supply Chain Collaboration, verify the applicability of these steps in the Configuration Guide for Business Network Collaboration at http://s-prs.co/500330. Similar instructions are available for connecting SAP IBP, which replaces SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization, and SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration. SAP IBP is the planning tool of choice used in SAP S/4HANA and in conjunction with SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration on forecast collaboration topics. Now, execute the (high-level) steps described next. To begin, verify access to an SAP Ariba buyer account/SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration account by logging in using the credentials provided. If you can’t log in, you’ll need to request access from SAP Business Network and your account team. Once verified, invite suppliers to SAP Business Network via the launchpad navigation. These suppliers are those that will be conducting direct procurement transactions and confirmations with your organization. To invite suppliers, navigate to Business Net- work  Integration Configuration  Invite Suppliers to Ariba Network. The next step requires setting up a shared secret. This is a security step to ensure that your suppliers are who they say they are upon login. To maintain a shared secret, pro- ceed as follows: 1. Log into your SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration account. 2. Choose Administration  Configuration  cXML Setup. 3. Under Authentication Method, select Shared Secret and enter your shared secret. Once you have the security settings in place with the shared secret, it’s time to enable your suppliers: 1. Log into your SAP Ariba buyer account and go to the Supplier Enablement tab. 2. Go to the Active Relationships tab. If your supplier is in the Active Relationships table, jump to the next set of steps and assign a private ID. If the supplier isn’t in the Active Relationships table, search for the suppler and add it to Selected Suppliers. Via Selected Suppliers, click the supplier and choose Request a Relationship. The sup- plier must accept the request prior to proceeding to the next instructions. © 647

sections.title: SAP Business Network for Logistics
sections.en: 16.4 SAP Business Network for Logistics In the next steps, you’ll create a private ID for a supplier so that the supplier can log in: 1. Log onto SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collaboration with your SAP Ariba buyer account. 2. In the Supplier Enablement Tab, choose Supplier Relationships  More Actions  Edit  Edit Preferences for Supplier  Enter Supplier Identifiers for Procurement Application  Add. 3. If tying the supplier to only one ERP system, enter the supplier ID in the first field. 4. If tying the supplier to multiple ERP backends, choose each system and enter the supplier ID. 5. Save. You’ve now set up your suppliers for SAP Business Network Supply Chain Collabora- tion. Note An additional setting is available for suppliers in the Forecast area to further define whether a supplier can view and forecast data, which is set as a default. In the Forecast area, you can override the default forecast rules and determine whether a supplier is allowed to view and commit forecast data. Save your preferences for the supplier by clicking the Save button on the screen. 16.4 SAP Business Network for Logistics The COVID-19 pandemic revealed and reiterated the urgent need for companies to understand their supply chains in depth. The quick, drastic disruptions to demand for certain goods, as well as the shipping and transport needs, drove stockouts, shortages, and price swings of 1,000x and more in some cases. SAP Business Network for Logistics leverages the power of SAP Business Network to extend other SAP solutions, such as SAP Transportation Management, SAP Corporate Serialization, SAP Yard Logistics, and SAP Integrated Business Planning, to connect stakeholders across your logistics ecosys- tem for seamless, digitalized collaboration and advanced insights. As per Figure 16.39, transportation collaboration enabled by SAP Business Network allows shippers and carriers to manage and collaborate on sales orders, stock transfer orders, returns, outbound deliveries, shipments, and scheduling agreements. 16 Integrating SAP S/4HANA with SAP Signavio, SAP Ariba, SAP Business Network, and SAP Fieldglass 648 Figure 16.39 Logistics for SAP Business Network: Transportation Collaboration Order collaboration in SAP Business Network for Logistics enables the following:  Collaborate from end to end for transportation needs; plan externally, leveraging a full contract-to-settlement process, including disputes, across multiple forms of transportation.  Ease transacting with your logistics service providers; business partners can interact according to their preference and technical ability via a web UI and/or APIs. Sup- ported global standards include ANSI X.12 and UN/EDIFACT, including EDI 204, 990, and 210.  Consolidated worklists and timely notifications for carriers; read attribute and bulk changes for efficient workflow with email updates for requests.  Exchange key data along the complete order lifecycle; free-text notes and attach- ments, such as bill of lading, reference IDs, and mode-specific such as VGM and driver/vessel assignment.  Automatic updates in your transport management system; out-of-the-box integra- tion with SAP Transportation Management/embedded TM in SAP S/4HANA for freight orders and bookings, as well as public SOAP APIs for custom integration.  B2B connectivity with digital freight forwarders (Uber Freight and Instafreight), other B2B networks (Descartes), and B2B carriers (CH Robinson).  Dock appointment scheduling; integration with backend systems for seamless oper- ations, collaborate on appointments, efficient dock and gate management, sharing of master and operational data, master data definition for yard, gates, docking loca- tions, loading points, and capacities. SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace is another solution area in SAP Business Network for Logistics. Functionality here includes: Sales Orders Stock Transport Orders Returns Outbound Deliveries Shipments Scheduling Agreements Freight Planning Freight Orders Resource Utilization Transportation Documents Freight Execution Freight Monitoring Freight Charges Freight Settlement Freight Cost Accounting Freight Units SAP S/4HANA/ Transportation Contracting Tendering, Quotation Processing, and Subcontracting External Planning Dock Appointment Scheduling and Gate Processing Execution Milestones and Documents Settlement Self-Billing, Carrier Invoicing, and Dispute Management Shipper SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration Web UI, APIs Carrier • General Ledger Posting • Material Valuation • Sales Order Profitability Analysis © 649 16.4 SAP Business Network for Logistics  Order fulfillment process tracking and goods in-transit; milestone monitoring and exception management with shipment monitoring  Milestone monitoring with real-time visibility; geolocation tracking with predictive expected time of arrival across multiple modes of transport  Receive milestone updates via API or EDI from your logistics service providers  Inform stakeholders of progress and exceptions via email  Understand the impact of deviations from plan by viewing the document flow and event correlations  Flexible and extensible setup with standard apps and templates as well as custom scenarios  Integrate with your ERP and logistics systems via standard, extractor-based IDocs SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace allows you to glean advanced insights for order fulfillment and goods in transit, driving collaboration across the network. Hav- ing advanced insights into order fulfillment and goods in transit helps you better man- age exceptions and disruptions. Enabling early detection allows for mitigation. Stakeholders are informed of progress as well as shipment insights, which can be enriched with real-time geographic location and transport emissions data to make appropriate decisions during the shipping process. These execution insights are com- bined with performance insights, including dashboards, risk-control analysis, critical deviation detection, carrier performance analysis, and custom analytics. sections.title: SAP Business Network for Asset Management
sections.en: 16.5 SAP Business Network for Asset Management SAP Business Network for Asset Management seeks to transform the fragmented asset lifecycle into a unified, collaborative, and streamlined process across stakeholders, pro- viding a single source of truth to the main stakeholder groups (asset operators, OEM suppliers and/or engineering/construction, and service providers). SAP Business Net- work for Asset Management brings together these groups to collaborate on common asset specifications and business processes, maximizing asset availability, improving process efficiency, securing operations, and generating new business models, as shown in Figure 16.41. Figure 16.41 SAP Business Network for Asset Management SAP Business Network for Asset Management’s main capabilities leverage a common digital twin, allowing stakeholders to collaborate in a common taxonomy in areas such as the following: 1. Model/equipment request If an asset operator faces issues while using a piece of equipment, the asset operator can get a recommendation on the model from a relevant stakeholder—say, the manufacturer—by creating a model request in the system and involving the OEM directly. 2. Announcements An announcement allows communication among the various business partners that have a relationship with a model or a piece of equipment. For example, an announcement can communicate that an existing instruction has been updated or Equipment Model Equipment Model Work Order Confirmation Service Bulletins Location Maintenance Request Failure Modes Work Order Planning Specifications & Drawings System Equipment Obsolescence Analysis Manufacturer Spare Parts • Simplify collaboration by registering a common digital twin in the network • Find all asset informa- tion in one place • Share best practices for optimal maintenance processes and equip- ment performance • Sustainable operations by collaborating with OEMs to optimize main- tenance processes and improvement programs • Provide opportunity for a new business model by selling equipment as a service Design Manufacture/Build Commissioning Operate & Maintain Retire & Decommission C o l l a b o r a t i v e A s s e r t M a i n t a i n a n c e C o l l a b o r a t i v e A s s e r t M a i n t a i n a n c e © 651

sections.en: 16.6 SAP Fieldglass that the spare parts list for a piece of equipment has been updated. Announcements can be used within a single company or between companies. An announcement can be any of the following types:  Availability  Instruction change  Service bulletin  Recall  New policy  New firmware  New model  Document change  Spare parts change  Model information change SAP Business Network for Asset Management allows suppliers, operators, service pro- viders, and other stakeholders to collaborate on a common digital twin for equipment definition and maintenance. This approach drives optimal maintenance processes, better asset performance, operational costs reduction, and safer operations. 16.6 SAP Fieldglass Founded in Chicago in 1999 and acquired by SAP in 2014, SAP Fieldglass has been pro- viding cloud-based vendor management solutions (VMSs) for over two decades. SAP Fieldglass enables total talent and spend management by answering five key questions about your external supplier of third-party workers:  Who’s working for you?  What are they doing?  Where are they located?  What facilities/systems are they using?  How much are you paying them? To properly answer these questions, SAP Fieldglass interfaces with both procurement and HR systems, as shown in Figure 16.42. The key areas in SAP Fieldglass are the contingent labor and statement of work (SOW) workflows, as shown in Figure 16.43. At the contingent labor level, a buyer may be selecting an individual rather than a firm to perform the work, and the deliverables are down to the timesheet level rather than at an overall project completion level. 16 Integrating SAP S/4HANA with SAP Signavio, SAP Ariba, SAP Business Network, and SAP Fieldglass 652 Figure 16.42 SAP Fieldglass Integration Figure 16.43 Services versus Contingent Workflow The next sections cover key integration technologies and approaches for SAP Fieldglass.
